```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# run-and-mark.sh — run a long command as a child, block until it exits, and
3	# record completion durably.
4	#
5	# Launch this ONCE in the background (e.g. your agent harness's background
6	# shell flag). The harness wakes you when it exits; you never poll.
7	#
8	# The command is run as a *child of this script* so plain `wait` suffices —
9	# there is no portable way to wait on a foreign pid (`tail --pid` is GNU-only,
10	# macOS has neither that nor flock/fswatch).
11	#
12	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
13	
14	set -u
15	
16	usage() {
17	  cat <<'EOF'
18	Usage: run-and-mark.sh --marker-dir DIR --name NAME [OPTIONS] -- <command> [args...]
19	
20	Run <command>, block until it finishes, and write a durable completion marker
21	so a later session can learn the outcome without re-running anything.
22	
23	Required:
24	  --marker-dir DIR   Directory for marker files. Created if absent.
25	  --name NAME        Run identifier. Must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]+.
26	
27	Options:
28	  --dry-run          Print what would happen; run nothing. Exit 0.
29	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
30	
31	Everything after `--` is the command. It is executed directly (no shell), so
32	quote nothing extra:
33	  run-and-mark.sh --marker-dir .runs --name v2 -- python train.py --epochs 40
34	
35	Files written (all inside DIR):
36	  NAME.start         Written immediately: JSON with pid, host, start time, cmd.
37	  NAME.exit          Written at completion: the exit code, one integer + newline.
38	  NAME.meta          Written at completion: JSON with the full record.
39	
40	Both terminal files are written to a .tmp sibling and renamed, so a concurrent
41	reader never observes a half-written marker. Keep DIR on the same filesystem
42	you read from — `mv` is only atomic within one filesystem.
43	
44	Output:
45	  stdout   one JSON object at completion (the same content as NAME.meta)
46	  stderr   two lines: one at start, one at completion. Nothing per-tick.
47	
48	Exit codes:
49	  <cmd>    the command's own exit code (0 on success)
50	  1        invalid arguments
51	  2        marker directory not writable
52	
53	Note: a shell reports a signal-killed child as 128+signal (137 = SIGKILL,
54	often the OOM killer). That is preserved in NAME.exit.
55	
56	Examples:
57	  run-and-mark.sh --marker-dir .runs --name v2_full -- python train.py
58	  run-and-mark.sh --marker-dir .runs --name eval --dry-run -- ./eval.sh
59	  run-and-mark.sh --marker-dir .runs --name sweep -- sbatch --wait sweep.sbatch
60	EOF
61	}
62	
63	die() { printf 'error: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
64	
65	MARKER_DIR=""
66	NAME=""
67	DRY_RUN=0
68	
69	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
70	  case "$1" in
71	    --marker-dir) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--marker-dir requires a value (try --help)" 1
72	                  MARKER_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
73	    --name)       [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--name requires a value (try --help)" 1
74	                  NAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
75	    --dry-run)    DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
76	    --help|-h)    usage; exit 0 ;;
77	    --)           shift; break ;;
78	    -*)           die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
79	    *)            die "unexpected argument '$1' — the command goes after '--'" 1 ;;
80	  esac
81	done
82	
83	[ -n "$MARKER_DIR" ] || die "--marker-dir is required (try --help)" 1
84	[ -n "$NAME" ]       || die "--name is required (try --help)" 1
85	[ $# -gt 0 ]         || die "no command given — put it after '--' (try --help)" 1
86	
87	case "$NAME" in
88	  *[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*) die "--name '$NAME' has characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-]" 1 ;;
89	esac
90	
91	# JSON string escaping: backslash and double-quote only. Control characters are
92	# not expected in argv or hostnames; if they appear the field is still parseable
93	# because we escape the two structural characters.
94	json_escape() {
95	  printf '%s' "$1" | sed -e 's/\\/\\\\/g' -e 's/"/\\"/g'
96	}
97	
98	# Render the command as a JSON array.
99	cmd_json() {
100	  local first=1 arg out=""
101	  for arg in "$@"; do
102	    if [ $first -eq 1 ]; then first=0; else out="$out, "; fi
103	    out="$out\"$(json_escape "$arg")\""
104	  done
105	  printf '[%s]' "$out"
106	}
107	
108	now_iso() { date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'; }
109	
110	START_FILE="$MARKER_DIR/$NAME.start"
111	EXIT_FILE="$MARKER_DIR/$NAME.exit"
112	META_FILE="$MARKER_DIR/$NAME.meta"
113	CMD_JSON=$(cmd_json "$@")
114	HOST=$(hostname 2>/dev/null || printf 'unknown')
115	
116	if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]; then
117	  printf 'dry-run: would create %s\n' "$MARKER_DIR" >&2
118	  printf 'dry-run: would write %s, then run the command, then %s + %s\n' \
119	    "$START_FILE" "$EXIT_FILE" "$META_FILE" >&2
120	  printf '{"dry_run": true, "name": "%s", "marker_dir": "%s", "command": %s}\n' \
121	    "$(json_escape "$NAME")" "$(json_escape "$MARKER_DIR")" "$CMD_JSON"
122	  exit 0
123	fi
124	
125	mkdir -p "$MARKER_DIR" 2>/dev/null \
126	  || die "cannot create marker directory '$MARKER_DIR'" 2
127	[ -w "$MARKER_DIR" ] \
128	  || die "marker directory '$MARKER_DIR' is not writable" 2
129	
130	# A stale terminal marker from a previous run would make this run look already
131	# finished the moment a reader looked. Clear both before starting.
132	rm -f "$EXIT_FILE" "$META_FILE"
133	
134	STARTED_AT=$(now_iso)
135	printf '{"name": "%s", "host": "%s", "pid": %d, "started_at": "%s", "command": %s}\n' \
136	  "$(json_escape "$NAME")" "$(json_escape "$HOST")" "$$" "$STARTED_AT" "$CMD_JSON" \
137	  > "$START_FILE.tmp" && mv "$START_FILE.tmp" "$START_FILE"
138	
139	printf '%s start %s: %s\n' "$STARTED_AT" "$NAME" "$*" >&2
140	
141	# Run as our own child so `wait` — the one primitive available everywhere —
142	# is enough. Do not background-and-detach; we must survive to write the marker.
143	"$@" &
144	CHILD=$!
145	wait "$CHILD"
146	RC=$?
147	
148	FINISHED_AT=$(now_iso)
149	
150	# Exit code first: it is what readers key on, so it must not appear before the
151	# run is genuinely over. Temp-then-rename keeps it atomic.
152	printf '%s\n' "$RC" > "$EXIT_FILE.tmp" && mv "$EXIT_FILE.tmp" "$EXIT_FILE"
153	
154	META=$(printf '{"name": "%s", "host": "%s", "pid": %d, "started_at": "%s", "finished_at": "%s", "exit_code": %d, "command": %s}' \
155	  "$(json_escape "$NAME")" "$(json_escape "$HOST")" "$$" "$STARTED_AT" "$FINISHED_AT" "$RC" "$CMD_JSON")
156	printf '%s\n' "$META" > "$META_FILE.tmp" && mv "$META_FILE.tmp" "$META_FILE"
157	
158	printf '%s done %s: exit=%d\n' "$FINISHED_AT" "$NAME" "$RC" >&2
159	printf '%s\n' "$META"
160	
161	exit "$RC"
162
```

````text
40	
41	- The command finishes in seconds or a couple of minutes — just run it.
42	- You want run-level metrics, curves, or parameter tracking → `mlflow-tracking`.
43	- You want to record what the run *meant* → `experiment-knowledge-harness`.
44	- You need the Slurm resource-request or GPU-isolation details themselves →
45	  `slurm-hpc`.
46	
47	## The ladder
48	
49	Pick the **lowest-numbered tier that applies**. Do not skip down because a
50	higher tier needs a little setup — the setup is the point.
51	
52	| Tier | Mechanism | Use when |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| **0** | **The scheduler owns the chain.** Submit B at the same time as A, with a dependency. | There is a next step. Survives session death, compaction, laptop sleep, and agent restarts entirely. |
55	| **1** | **One blocking wait, backgrounded.** A command that blocks until done, launched once in the background. The harness wakes you when it exits. | You need to *react* at completion. Zero in-context polls while waiting. |
56	| **2** | **Stream filtered events.** A background command that prints only milestone lines. | You must react *mid-run* — OOM, early stopping, a metric crossing a threshold — not just at the end. |
57	| **3** | **Scheduled check-in.** A cron / wake-up prompt. | Last resort. Nothing above can reach the job (e.g. a remote system you hold no handle to). |
58	
59	### Tier 0 — let the scheduler own the chain
60	
61	The agent is not involved in the transition at all. This is almost always
62	right for "run B after A finishes".
63	
64	```bash
65	# Slurm. Note the ${JID%%;*} — --parsable emits "jobid;cluster" when a
66	# cluster name is configured, and "afterok:123;mycluster" is not a job id.
67	JID=$(sbatch --parsable phase_a.sbatch); JID=${JID%%;*}
68	
69	sbatch --dependency=afterok:"$JID" \
70	       --kill-on-invalid-dep=yes \
71	       --mail-type=INVALID_DEPEND,END,FAIL \
72	       phase_b.sbatch
73	```
74	
75	```bash
76	# pueue (local shell jobs). Use the pueue-job-queue skill's wrapper — it
77	# already handles defensive id parsing and emits JSON.
78	P=skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts
79	A=$("$P"/submit.sh --label phase-a -- ./phase_a.sh | jq -r .task_id)
80	"$P"/submit.sh --label phase-b --after "$A" -- ./phase_b.sh
81	```
82	
83	`--kill-on-invalid-dep=yes` is **not optional**. See Gotchas.
84	
85	### Tier 1 — one blocking wait, backgrounded
86	
87	Launch a command that blocks until the work is done, in the background. The
88	harness re-invokes you when it exits, so you spend nothing while waiting.
89	
90	```bash
91	sbatch --wait phase_a.sbatch          # blocks; exit code mirrors the job's
92	```
93	```bash
94	scripts/run-and-mark.sh --marker-dir .runs --name v2_full -- python train.py
95	```
96	
97	Launch it **once**, backgrounded — not in a loop, and not in the foreground.
98	If your harness exposes a background flag on its shell tool, that is the one to
99	use; see `references/claude-code-mechanisms.md` for the Claude Code specifics,
100	including which mechanism actually wakes you on completion and which does not.
101	
102	For a job you did **not** start and hold no handle to, block on a condition in
103	a subshell rather than in your context:
104	
105	```bash
106	until ! squeue -h -j "$JID" | grep -q .; do sleep 60; done
107	sacct -j "$JID" --format=State,ExitCode --noheader
108	```
109	
110	### Tier 2 — stream filtered events
111	
112	Only when you need to act before the end. Filter **in the shell**, never by
113	feeding raw logs into context:
114	
115	```bash
116	tail -F runs/v2_full.log \
117	  | stdbuf -oL grep --line-buffered -E \
118	      'Training complete|Early stopping|CUDA out of memory|Traceback'
119	```
120	
121	A bare `tail -F` on a training log is an anti-pattern: every epoch line becomes
122	an event and you have reinvented the expensive poll with extra steps.
123	
124	### Tier 3 — scheduled check-in
125	
126	Legitimate only when no handle exists — a job on a machine you cannot hold a
127	blocking connection to. If you land here, make each tick cheap: check one thing
128	and report one line. Know your scheduler's limits (in Claude Code: session-
129	scoped, and recurring tasks expire after 7 days — see
130	`references/claude-code-mechanisms.md`).
131	
132	## The invariant: completion must be durable
133	
134	Orthogonal to all four tiers. **Whatever waits, something must survive not
135	waiting.**
136	
137	Sessions die, contexts compact, laptops sleep, SSH drops. If the only record
138	that Phase A succeeded is in the agent's context, that record is one disconnect
139	from gone — and the usual recovery is re-running eight hours of GPU time.
140	
141	So every long run writes an atomic completion marker:
142	
143	```bash
144	python train.py; rc=$?
145	printf '%s\n' "$rc" > runs/v2.exit.tmp && mv runs/v2.exit.tmp runs/v2.exit
146	```
147	
148	`mv` within one filesystem is atomic, so a reader never sees a half-written
149	marker — it sees either no marker or a complete one. `scripts/run-and-mark.sh`
150	does this for you; `scripts/check-runs.sh` reads the markers back and tells a
151	fresh session what finished while it was away.
152	
153	**Absence of a marker means "unknown" — never "failed", never "fine".** A run
154	that started and has no marker was probably killed. That is exit code 4 from
155	`check-runs.sh`, and it is a question for the user, not something to silently
156	re-run.
157	
158	## Choosing
159	
160	```
161	Is there a next step to run after this one?
162	├─ yes → Tier 0: submit it now with a dependency. Done — you are not in the loop.
163	└─ no  → Do you need to react before the end (OOM, early stop, threshold)?
164	         ├─ yes → Tier 2: stream, filtered at the shell.
165	         └─ no  → Can you hold a blocking handle on the work?
166	                  ├─ yes → Tier 1: one blocking command, backgrounded.
167	                  └─ no  → Tier 3: scheduled check-in, cheapest possible tick.
168	
169	In every branch: the job writes a durable exit-code marker.
170	```
171	
172	## Available scripts
173	
174	- **`scripts/run-and-mark.sh`** — run something long as a child process, block
175	  until it exits, record completion atomically. Launch **once**, backgrounded.
176	  - Flags: `--help`, `--dry-run`, `--marker-dir DIR`, `--name NAME`, `-- <cmd>`
177	- **`scripts/check-runs.sh`** — report what finished while you were away; the
178	  resume path after a session dies.
179	  - Flags: `--help`, `--marker-dir DIR`, `--name NAME`, `--json`
180	
181	```bash
182	scripts/run-and-mark.sh --marker-dir .runs --name v2_full -- python train.py
183	scripts/check-runs.sh --marker-dir .runs --json
184	```
185	
186	## Bundled assets
187	
188	- `assets/chained.sbatch.template` — a Phase A / Phase B pair wired with
189	  `--parsable`, `afterok`, `--kill-on-invalid-dep=yes`, a `SIGUSR1` checkpoint
````

50	                              (--via 'fly ssh console -a x --pty=false -C')
51	  connect                     the API over stdin/stdout (ssh box hc connect)
52	  schema                      the API as JSON Schema, for app builders
53	
54	<t> is an address like t7 or t1b, or a name. In a terminal, attach, read, get,
55	kill, rm, wait and interrupt pick one when it's left out.
56	Options: --json (default when piped; run and read print text), -V --version,
57	--licenses (what hc includes, and their licenses).
58	Per command: hc <command> --help
59	Settings: ~/.config/herdr-core/config.toml. notes = false: hc types nothing
60	on its own (no notes to parent agents, no <hc> tags on messages).
61	shell = ["nu"] overrides the shell for new terminals and keep recovery.
62	
63	Examples
64	  hc run --on vps "cd app && npm test"     like ssh, in a terminal that stays
65	  hc run --bg claude                       Claude Code in a new terminal
66	  hc attach t3                             take it over
67	  hc run reviewer "review src/x.rs"        a template with a task
68	
69	Agent? Run: hc --skill
70	```

````text
1	# Agent templates
2	
3	Save a command and a role once, then start an agent by name with a task.
4	Templates do not install agents or configure their status reporting.
5	
6	[Back to the README](../README.md) · [Command reference](commands.md#hc-templates)
7	
8	## Make a reviewer
9	
10	Save this as `~/.config/herdr-core/templates/reviewer.md` on Linux or macOS:
11	
12	```markdown
13	---
14	description: Read-only code review. Give it file paths and scope.
15	command: pi
16	---
17	You are a focused review agent. Read the code before giving findings.
18	Do not edit files or start other agents.
19	Report bugs with file paths, lines, and a short reason.
20	If a parent assigned the review, report back with hc send.
21	```
22	
23	Use an installed interactive agent command. Put model choices and other agent options in that command.
24	On Windows, templates live under `%APPDATA%\herdr-core\templates` by default.
25	Setting `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` changes the config home on either platform.
26	
27	```sh
28	hc templates
29	hc run --bg --name review --cwd /path/to/repo reviewer "Review src/x.rs only."
30	hc read review --lines 100
31	hc send review "Recheck the error path."
32	```
33	
34	Use background mode for agents so their screen does not stream into your caller's output.
35	You can still attach and take over with `hc attach review`.
36	
37	## File format
38	
39	Each template is one Markdown file ending in `.md`.
40	The filename without that suffix is the template's name.
41	The optional name field is ignored; the filename wins.
42	Files are read fresh on each use.
43	
44	Start the file with a line containing three hyphens. End the header the same way.
45	The header is a small line-based format, not full YAML:
46	
47	| Field | Meaning |
48	| --- | --- |
49	| `command` | Required shell command that starts the agent. |
50	| `description` | Short text shown in the template list. |
51	| `ready` | Default: wait for an OSC 7501 status report. The value `quiet` waits for output to settle instead. |
52	| `submit` | Override the key sequence used to submit text. |
53	| `stop` | Override the key sequence used to interrupt a turn. |
54	| `paste_gap_ms` | Override the pause before submitting pasted text, in milliseconds. |
55	
56	Values are literal text after the first colon, trimmed at each end.
57	Do not add YAML quotes around them or use multiline YAML values.
58	Unknown fields are ignored.
59	The body is the agent's opening instructions. Core appends your task after a blank line.
60	The command runs through `sh`, which must be on PATH on Windows too.
61	
62	## Readiness and input
63	
64	By default, core waits for the agent's first status report before sending the opening message.
65	If that does not arrive within 30 seconds by default, it leaves the screen alone.
66	A trust dialog might be waiting for you. Read the screen before sending again.
67	The run result reports whether the first message was sent.
68	
69	For a program that does not report status, opt into quiet readiness:
70	
71	```markdown
72	---
73	description: An interactive assistant without status reports.
74	command: my-assistant
75	ready: quiet
76	submit: enter
77	stop: ctrl+c
78	paste_gap_ms: 100
79	---
80	Stay within the assigned files. Ask when blocked.
81	```

83	Quiet output is not proof that an agent is ready. Use this only when you know its startup flow.
84	It does not give the program an agent status; core still never guesses status from the screen.
85	See `hc keys --help` for key notation and `hc --skill` for the delegation workflow.
86	
87	When a terminal is launched on another machine, that machine resolves the template and runs its command.
88	Put the template and agent there first.

1	# herdr-core API
2	
3	`hc.openrpc.json` is the whole request/response API as an
4	[OpenRPC](https://open-rpc.org) document: every method with its params,
5	result and errors in JSON Schema. It is generated from the Rust types (a
6	test fails when it is stale), and `hc schema` or the `rpc.discover` method
7	returns the same document from a running core.
8	
9	This file covers what OpenRPC does not describe: the two connection modes,
10	the attach stream, and event notifications.
11	
12	Status: preview (protocol generation 1, version 0.x).
13	
14	The API only grows. `released.openrpc.json` is the API as last released;
15	a test fails on any change that would break a client of it: a removed
16	method, param or result field, a new required input, an input that accepts
17	less, or an answer that can carry a new kind of value or loses its type.
18	At each release, copy `hc.openrpc.json` over it. A real break needs a new
19	protocol generation, decided on purpose.
20	
21	## Connecting
22	
23	On Unix, core listens on a Unix socket; on Windows, it uses a named pipe.
24	See [endpoint rules](../docs/security.md#state-and-endpoints) for default paths,
25	fallbacks, and overrides. `hc connect` speaks the same protocol over
26	stdin/stdout, so `ssh box hc connect` is a remote core.
27	
28	A connection starts in **plain mode**: JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line.
29	Any language or `socat` works.
30	
31	```
32	→ {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"terminal.list","params":{}}
33	← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"terminals":[...],"hidden_finished":0}}
34	```
35	
36	Errors are JSON-RPC errors with a stable kind and a hint:
37	
38	```
39	{"code":-32000,"message":"no terminal t9","data":{"kind":"not_found","hint":"..."}}
40	```
41	
42	`hello` with `{"framed": true}` switches the connection to **framed mode**
43	after its reply. Attach needs it; everything else works in both modes.
44	
45	## Framed mode
46	
47	Every frame: `[channel u32 LE][kind u8][len u32 LE][payload]`, payload at
48	most 16 MiB.
49	
50	| kind | name | payload |
51	|---|---|---|
52	| 0 | DATA | channel 0: one JSON-RPC message; other channels: stream bytes |
53	| 1 | CREDIT | u32 LE: bytes the receiver consumed |
54	| 2 | CLOSE | the channel is over; from the core, a JSON reason |
55	| 3 | RESIZE | u16 LE cols, u16 LE rows: viewer → core, core → observer |
56	| 4 | FOCUS | viewer → core: 1 gained focus, 0 lost it |
57	| 5 | FACTS | viewer → core: JSON display facts (`Display` in the schema) |
58	| 6 | AUTOMATIC_INPUT | viewer → core: terminal-generated reply bytes, not human activity |
59	
60	Channel 0 carries JSON-RPC both ways. Calls on it run side by side.
61	
62	### Attach streams
63	
64	`terminal.attach` returns a `channel`. On it the core sends the first paint
65	(the current screen, optional history, the latest status report and title,
66	and `CSI ?9001h` or `l`: whether the program asked for win32-input-mode,
67	as Windows' ConPTY does when it starts), then the program's raw output,
68	minus terminal queries the core already answered. The core never encodes
69	keys: a viewer that honors 9001 sends key events in that format itself.
70	The viewer sends keys as DATA on the same channel, and RESIZE,
71	FOCUS and FACTS as it changes. The last active viewer sets the size
72	(active: it attached, typed, resized or gained focus); `observe` viewers never type or resize.
73	Automatic query answers (including mode 2048 reports, kitty graphics and XTGETTCAP
74	replies) use AUTOMATIC_INPUT, not DATA. Their bytes reach the program unchanged,
75	including duplicates from multiple viewers, but do not take size/display ownership
76	or reset the human quiet period. They follow the same input serialization as DATA.
77	Tag replies at their source, never by inspecting their bytes; arbitrary splits are valid.
78	Cores advertise `automatic_input` in `hello.features`; `terminal.attach` confirms
79	`automatic_input: true` only for a supporting path. Clients must require both before
80	sending kind 6; absent/false means send DATA (legacy activity behavior). Old cores
81	ignore unknown local frame kinds, so sending kind 6 without negotiation loses input.
82	Relays preserve the tag and close a previously capable stream if support is lost
83	on reconnect; attach again to negotiate the fallback. Untagged DATA is unchanged.
84	Observers may opt in with `resize_notifications: true` on `terminal.attach`:
85	the client must apply incoming RESIZE before consuming subsequent DATA.
86	The reply confirms `resize_notifications: true` only when every core on the path
87	supports it. False or an absent field means the client must track size through
88	size events instead; no replacement paints are injected for this request.
89	Cores advertise `resize_notifications` in both hello requests and replies, so an
90	older intermediate relay cannot silently drop the grid announcements. If a
91	previously capable path loses support on reconnect, its stream closes; attach
92	again to negotiate the fallback.
93	These confirmed observers receive the terminal's actual grid before their first paint.
94	When that grid changes, pending output is superseded by RESIZE followed by an
95	authoritative paint (starting with CAN to cancel any unfinished sequence).
96	Size/paint pairs share stream ordering and wait for DATA credit; RESIZE itself
97	does not consume credit. Intermediate unsent grids are coalesced, and a paint is
98	serialized only when the observer has credit. The attach reply precedes stream
99	frames, including on core-to-core relays and reconnects.
100	Without this opt-in, existing event-driven observers keep their previous output
101	behavior: no additional resize paints or RESIZE frames.
102	
103	Flow control: a stream starts with 256 KiB of credit. The viewer sends
104	CREDIT for the bytes it has written out. A viewer that falls more than
105	4 MiB behind gets a fresh repaint instead of the backlog. A stalled stream
106	never blocks channel 0 or other streams.
107	
108	A viewer detaches by sending CLOSE; the core answers with an empty CLOSE.
109	When the program ends, the core sends CLOSE with
110	`{"reason":"exited","exit_code":0,"signal":null}` (`reason` as in the
111	terminal record: exited, killed, server_stop, ...).
112	
113	## Events
114	
115	`events.subscribe` replies with a snapshot (`seq`, matching terminals) and,
116	in framed mode, a channel; in plain mode the connection then carries only
117	notifications. Notifications are JSON-RPC messages without an id:
118	
119	```
120	{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"event","params":{"seq":42,"type":"status","terminal":"t7","data":{...}}}
121	{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"heartbeat","params":{"seq":42}}
122	{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"missed","params":{"seq":57,"terminals":[...]}}
123	```
124	
125	Each event's `data`, and how to apply it to a snapshot:
126	
127	| type | data | apply |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| `created` | the whole `Terminal` record | add it |
130	| `lost` | `{reason, exit_code, signal, finished_ms: null}` | kept terminal remains `live`; set these, clear `pid` and drop `foreground` |
131	| `restarted` | the whole `Terminal` record | replace it; reattach to the new shell |
132	| `keep` | `{keep}` | set `keep` |
133	| `finished` | `{reason, exit_code, signal, finished_ms}` | set `state: "finished"` and these, and drop `foreground`; status is cleared just before (a `status` event) |
134	| `removed` | `{}` | drop it |
135	| `status` | `{status, records, reported}`: the root status (null when cleared), every record by key, whether it ever reported | replace all three |
136	| `turn` | `{turn, state}`: the turn counter after a turn ended, and the word it ended on | set `turn` |
137	| `title` | `{title}` | set `title` |
138	| `labels` | `{labels}`: all labels now; plus `record` (the whole `Terminal`) when it newly matches your filter | replace `labels`; with `record`, add it; with a label filter, a terminal that no longer matches leaves your view (you still get this event) |
139	| `size` | `{cols, rows}` | set both |
140	| `foreground` | `{pid, name, argv, cwd}`, or null: what runs in it now (the foreground process group's leader) and its folder; read about twice a second | set `foreground` |
141	
142	Terminals on machines this core added are in the same stream, addressed as
143	seen from here (`rohan/t7`), in the same order and filters (`terminal`,
144	`children_of`, labels). When a machine's line comes back, its terminals that
145	changed meanwhile arrive as `created` again (replace the record) and those
146	that went as `removed`; forgetting the machine removes its terminals.
147	
148	`run --keep` or `terminal.keep {terminal, keep}` keeps a lost terminal live
149	without a program until this machine's shell can start in its last observed
150	folder (then its start folder, then home). The original command is never
151	re-run. Loss closes existing attach streams with its reason; wait for
152	`restarted` and attach again. An exit with a code and explicit kill stay final.
153	Death by signal without an exit code is loss (`signaled`) for kept terminals;
154	non-kept behavior is unchanged. Windows reports no signals, so `signaled` never
155	fires there: native termination normally reports an exit code. A replacement
156	killed by a shutdown signal is lost again instead of closing its record.
157	Repeated failures back off by 1.5, 3, 6, 12, 30, then 60 seconds forever; a
158	program that lived at least 10 seconds resets the delay. Recovery
159	runs on every OS after a grace delay, but not while the core stops/restarts
160	or Windows reports session shutdown. During recovery, send/keys/interrupt/attach
161	return `unavailable`: "lost, waiting for its new shell"; retry after `restarted`.
162	Server stop parks kept terminals; the next core start gives them fresh shells.
163	Waits end on `lost` as on `finished`: they follow the program, not the kept record.
164	
165	An initial spawn that times out remains claimed with `reason: "spawn_pending"`;
166	input/attach are unavailable until the holder answers. It may already be running,
167	so core does not clear the claim or start another program on a guess. Explicit
168	kill cancels it; a core restart reconciles the holder. A late spawn failure clears
169	the claim and retries if kept, or finishes if keep was disabled.
170	
171	`reason` on a finished terminal: `exited`, `killed`, `server_stop`,
172	`host_shutdown`, `holder_lost`, `stopped_by_restart`. Kept live records may
173	also have `reason: "signaled"` while waiting for a new shell. `seq` rises by one per event, in order. A `heartbeat`
174	arrives every 15 s with the current `seq` (when no events are queued for you). A subscriber that falls behind
175	gets `missed` with a fresh snapshot: drop events whose `seq` is not above
176	it. `seq` restarts with each core process; take a fresh snapshot after
177	reconnecting.
178	
179	## Documents
180	
181	`doc.get {name, on?}` reads opaque JSON and its version. An unwritten name
182	returns `{value: null, version: 0}`. `doc.set {name, value, version, on?}`
183	writes only if the version matches, returning the new version. A stale write
184	fails with kind `conflict` and the current version in its message; read again
185	before retrying. Writing null deletes the value but retains the version, so
186	an old writer cannot recreate it unnoticed.
187	
188	Names follow the terminal name rules. Each value is limited to 1 MiB of
189	serialized JSON. Documents persist atomically in `docs.json` in core state,
190	survive restart and handover, and disappear when that state is wiped. Core
191	never interprets their contents. A broken document file is warned about and
192	renamed to `docs.json.bad`; the core starts with empty documents rather than
193	making terminals unavailable. These methods are API-only, with no CLI verb.
194	
195	Unfiltered event subscribers receive changes as:
196	
197	```
198	{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"event","params":{"seq":43,"type":"doc","data":{"name":"herdr-app","version":2}}}
199	```
200	
201	There is no `terminal` on a doc event. Changes on an added machine arrive in
202	the same stream with `machine: "rohan"` (this core's name for it). Terminal,
203	parent and label filters exclude doc events. The event carries no value;
204	call `doc.get` to read it, using `on` for another machine.
205	
206	Subscribe before reading. Read documents after subscribing or reconnecting,
207	a `missed` notification, or a remote machine reconnect: snapshots contain
208	terminals only, not documents, and changes while disconnected are not replayed.
209	A remote stream's `missed`, and each successful establishment of its event
210	subscription (including the first connection), are reported locally as `missed`
211	to unfiltered subscribers, using the local sequence. Refetch documents on all
212	watched machines after it.
213	
214	## Status
215	
216	A terminal's status is whatever its program reported through OSC 7501, the
217	Program Status Protocol (`idle`, `working`,
218	`done`, `blocked`, `error`, ...), stored as reported. hc never infers status
219	from the screen. Programs that don't speak 7501 have no status.
220

  The page lists `agent.get`, `agent.prompt`, `agent.wait`, and `agent.start`, but gives no specific `agent.get` or `agent.start` semantics. It describes `agent.wait` as server-owned and event-driven; it pins the resolved pane occupant so a replacement cannot satisfy the wait.

  The page documents `agent_session` as a read-only reference with `source`, `agent`, `kind`, and `value`. It does not specify revision checks, session-mismatch checks, or related preconditions. It does state that session-only reports do not affect waits, notifications, or rollups.

- **Errors**
  Errors have an `id`, `error.code`, and `error.message`. For decoded request lines, errors echo the request ID; invalid JSON or an ambiguous/missing top-level string ID yields an empty ID. Invalid UTF-8 may close the connection without a response.

  No such behavior is documented. Notifications are described as user notifications through configured toast delivery; the page does not say they submit prompts to agents.

84	    t.status.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| s.state == "working")
85	}

87	fn state_word(t: &Terminal) -> Option<String> {

91	/// A paste the way a terminal sends one: bracketed when the program asked.
92	pub fn paste(bracketed: bool, text: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
93	    let text = text.replace("\x1b[201~", "");
94	    if bracketed { format!("\x1b[200~{text}\x1b[201~").into_bytes() } else { text.into_bytes() }
95	}

97	pub struct Sent {
98	    pub status: Option<String>,
99	    pub turn: u64,
100	    /// Whether it went `working` soon after; None when it never reports status.
101	    pub started: Option<bool>,
102	}

104	pub enum Interrupted {
105	    Stopped,
106	    Exited,
107	    StillWorking,
108	    Unknown,
109	}

111	impl Core {
112	    /// Types `steps` (built by `prepare` from the live state) into terminal `id`.
113	    /// `quiet`: how long a person must have stopped typing first (zero: don't wait).
114	    pub async fn type_in<T>(
115	        &self,
116	        id: u32,
117	        quiet: Duration,
118	        prepare: impl FnOnce(&State, &Terminal) -> Result<(T, Vec<Step>), RpcError>,
119	    ) -> Result<T, RpcError> {
120	        let queue = self.lock().queues.entry(id).or_default().clone();
121	        let _turn = queue.lock().await;
122	        loop {
123	            let left = self.lock().gates.get(&id).and_then(|g| g.last_human).map(|t| quiet.saturating_sub(t.elapsed()));
124	            match left {
125	                Some(left) if !left.is_zero() => tokio::time::sleep(left).await,
126	                _ => break,
127	            }
128	        }
129	        let (out, steps) = {
130	            let mut st = self.lock();
131	            let t = st.reg.terminals.get(&id).filter(|t| t.is_live()).ok_or_else(|| {
132	                RpcError::new(
133	                    "finished",
134	                    format!("{} has finished", crate::terminals::address(id)),
135	                    format!("hc read {}", crate::terminals::address(id)),
136	                )
137	            })?;
138	            t.check_program()?;
139	            let prepared = prepare(&st, t)?;
140	            st.gates.entry(id).or_default().busy = true;
141	            prepared
142	        };
143	        for step in steps {
144	            match step {
145	                Step::Write(bytes) => {
146	                    if let Some(link) = self.lock().link(id) {
147	                        link.input(id, &bytes);
148	                    }
149	                }
150	                Step::Pause(d) => tokio::time::sleep(d).await,
151	            }
152	        }
153	        let mut st = self.lock();
154	        let gate = st.gates.entry(id).or_default();
155	        let held = gate.set_busy(false);
156	        if let Some(link) = st.link(id) {
157	            link.input(id, &held);
158	        }
159	        Ok(out)
160	    }
161	
162	    /// Paste + Enter, after a person has paused typing. Refuses a blocked
163	    /// program (typing would answer its dialog) unless `force`.
164	    pub async fn send(&self, id: u32, text: &str, force: bool, only_if: Option<&str>) -> Result<Sent, RpcError> {
165	        if let Some(t) = self.lock().reg.terminals.get(&id) {
166	            t.check_program()?;
167	        }
168	        self.settle(id).await?;
169	        let (status, turn, reported) = self
170	            .type_in(id, quiet(), |st, t| {
171	                let word = state_word(t);
172	                if word.as_deref() == Some("blocked") && !force {
173	                    return Err(RpcError::new(
174	                        "blocked",
175	                        format!(
176	                            "{} is blocked ({})",
177	                            crate::terminals::address(id),
178	                            t.status.as_ref().and_then(|s| s.kind.as_deref()).unwrap_or("waiting")
179	                        ),
180	                        format!(
181	                            "typing would answer its dialog; read its screen first (hc read {}), or --force",
182	                            crate::terminals::address(id)
183	                        ),
184	                    ));
185	                }
186	                if let Some(want) = only_if
187	                    && word.as_deref() != Some(want)
188	                {
189	                    return Err(RpcError::new(
190	                        "status_mismatch",
191	                        format!(
192	                            "{} is {}, not {want}",
193	                            crate::terminals::address(id),
194	                            word.as_deref().unwrap_or("silent")
195	                        ),
196	                        "nothing was typed",
197	                    ));
198	                }
199	                let screen = st.screens.get(&id).expect("live terminal has a screen");
200	                // A template may say how its agent submits (default: Enter after 200 ms).
201	                let submit = match &t.submit {
202	                    Some(key) => crate::keys::encode(screen, key)?,
203	                    None => b"\r".to_vec(),
204	                };
205	                let gap = t.paste_gap_ms.map_or(PASTE_GAP, Duration::from_millis);
206	                let steps =
207	                    vec![Step::Write(paste(screen.dec_mode(2004), text)), Step::Pause(gap), Step::Write(submit)];
208	                Ok(((word, t.turn, t.reported), steps))
209	            })
210	            .await?;
211	        let started = if reported {
212	            let went =
213	                |st: &State| st.reg.terminals.get(&id).is_none_or(|t| t.turn > turn || working(t) || !t.is_live());
214	            self.wait_for(started_window(), went).await;
215	            let st = self.lock();
216	            Some(st.reg.terminals.get(&id).is_some_and(|t| t.turn > turn || working(t)))
217	        } else {
218	            None
219	        };
220	        Ok(Sent { status, turn, started })
221	    }
222	
223	    /// A starting agent can report before it is ready for a paste (Pi swaps its
224	    /// input box right after its first report and drops a paste in flight):
225	    /// in its first seconds, wait until its screen has been still a moment.
226	    async fn settle(&self, id: u32) -> Result<(), RpcError> {
227	        let deadline = Instant::now() + SETTLE_MAX;
228	        loop {
229	            let ready = {
230	                let st = self.lock();
231	                let age = st
232	                    .reg
233	                    .terminals
234	                    .get(&id)
235	                    .map(|t| Duration::from_millis(crate::runtime::now_ms().saturating_sub(t.created_ms)));
236	                age.is_none_or(|age| {
237	                    age >= Duration::from_millis(STARTUP_MS)
238	                        || st.last_output.get(&id).map_or(age, Instant::elapsed) >= env_ms("HC_SETTLE_MS", 800)
239	                })
240	            };
241	            if ready {
242	                return Ok(());
243	            }
244	            if Instant::now() >= deadline {
245	                return Err(RpcError::new(
246	                    "unavailable",
247	                    format!("{} is still starting: its output has not settled", crate::terminals::address(id)),
248	                    format!("nothing was typed; check hc read {}, then retry", crate::terminals::address(id)),
249	                ));
250	            }
251	            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
252	        }
253	    }
254	
255	    /// Named keys, after a person has paused typing.
256	    pub async fn keys(&self, id: u32, names: &[String]) -> Result<(Option<String>, u64), RpcError> {
257	        self.type_in(id, quiet(), |st, t| {
258	            let screen = st.screens.get(&id).expect("live terminal has a screen");
259	            let mut steps = Vec::new();
260	            for name in names {
261	                steps.push(Step::Write(crate::keys::encode(screen, name)?));
262	                steps.push(Step::Pause(KEY_GAP));
263	            }
264	            Ok(((state_word(t), t.turn), steps))
265	        })
266	        .await
267	    }
268	
269	    /// Esc for programs that report status, else ctrl+c; then watch what happens.
270	    pub async fn interrupt(&self, id: u32, timeout: Duration) -> Result<(Interrupted, String), RpcError> {
271	        let (reported, pid) = {
272	            let st = self.lock();
273	            let t = st.reg.terminals.get(&id).ok_or_else(|| RpcError::new("not_found", "terminal removed", ""))?;
274	            t.check_program()?;
275	            (t.reported, t.pid.unwrap_or(0) as i32)
276	        };
277	        let before = if reported { -1 } else { self.foreground(id).await };
278	        let key = self
279	            .type_in(id, Duration::ZERO, |st, t| {
280	                let default = if reported { "esc" } else { "ctrl+c" };
281	                let key = t.stop.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| default.into());
282	                let screen = st.screens.get(&id).expect("live terminal has a screen");
283	                let bytes = crate::keys::encode(screen, &key)?;
284	                Ok((key, vec![Step::Write(bytes)]))
285	            })
286	            .await?;
287	        let live = |st: &State| st.reg.terminals.get(&id).is_some_and(|t| t.is_live());
288	        if reported {
289	            let settled = |st: &State| st.reg.terminals.get(&id).is_none_or(|t| !t.is_live() || !working(t));
290	            self.wait_for(timeout, settled).await;
291	            let st = self.lock();
292	            let outcome = match st.reg.terminals.get(&id) {
293	                Some(t) if !t.is_live() => Interrupted::Exited,
294	                Some(t) if working(t) => Interrupted::StillWorking,
295	                _ => Interrupted::Stopped,
296	            };
297	            return Ok((outcome, key));
298	        }
299	        // No status reports: a shell that gets the terminal back has stopped its job.
300	        let deadline = Instant::now() + timeout;
301	        loop {
302	            if !live(&self.lock()) {
303	                return Ok((Interrupted::Exited, key));
304	            }
305	            if before != pid && self.foreground(id).await == pid {
306	                return Ok((Interrupted::Stopped, key));
307	            }
308	            if Instant::now() >= deadline {
309	                return Ok((Interrupted::Unknown, key));
310	            }
311	            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
312	        }
313	    }
314	
315	    /// The process group in the foreground of terminal `id`, or -1.
316	    pub(crate) async fn foreground(&self, id: u32) -> i32 {
317	        let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
318	        {
319	            let mut st = self.lock();
320	            st.foreground.entry(id).or_default().push(tx);
321	            let Some(link) = st.link(id) else { return -1 };
322	            link.send(&proto::frame(proto::FOREGROUND, id, &[]));
323	        }
324	        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), rx).await.ok().and_then(Result::ok).unwrap_or(-1)
325	    }
326	}

1	//! Parents and children: news about a child is typed into its parent agent
2	//! as a marked note, only when the parent can take it and hasn't seen it.
3	
4	use crate::input::{Step, paste};
5	use crate::rpc::RpcError;
6	use crate::runtime::{Core, State, now_ms};
7	use crate::terminals::{Terminal, parse_id};
8	use std::sync::Arc;
9	use std::time::Duration;
10	
11	/// Work that can't happen on the thread that noticed it.
12	pub enum Job {
13	    /// Try to type pending notes into this parent.
14	    Notes(u32),
15	    /// The parent finished: end children that asked to die with it.
16	    Orphaned(u32),
17	    /// News for a parent on a core that dialed in (`desktop/t3`).
18	    NotesAfar(String),
19	}
20	
21	fn parent_id(t: &Terminal) -> Option<u32> {
22	    t.parent.as_deref().and_then(parse_id)
23	}
24	
25	fn says(t: &Terminal, word: &str) -> bool {
26	    t.is_live() && t.status.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| s.state == word)
27	}
28	
29	fn blocked(t: &Terminal) -> bool {
30	    says(t, "blocked")
31	}
32	
33	/// Blocked or errored: stuck in a way it can't report itself.
34	fn stuck(t: &Terminal) -> bool {
35	    blocked(t) || says(t, "error")
36	}
37	
38	/// The last lines a plain program wrote, for its exit note: blanks dropped,
39	/// long lines cut, no control characters (the note is typed in).
40	fn last_lines(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
41	    const LINES: usize = 20;
42	    const WIDTH: usize = 300;
43	    let mut lines: Vec<String> = text
44	        .lines()
45	        .rev()
46	        .map(|l| l.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_control() || *c == '\t').take(WIDTH).collect::<String>())
47	        .filter(|l| !l.trim().is_empty())
48	        .take(LINES)
49	        .collect();
50	    lines.reverse();
51	    lines
52	}
53	
54	/// A parent can take a note: a live agent not on a dialog (typing could answer
55	/// it). A working agent takes typed text as a message, like any steer.
56	fn can_take_note(t: &Terminal) -> bool {
57	    t.is_live() && t.reported && !blocked(t)
58	}
59	
60	/// `t7 reviewer`: address, then name or template.
61	pub fn who(t: &Terminal) -> String {
62	    match t.name.as_ref().or(t.template.as_ref()) {
63	        Some(name) => format!("{} {name}", t.address),
64	        None => t.address.clone(),
65	    }
66	}
67	
68	/// What a child can't say itself: it is blocked, it hit an error, or it is
69	/// gone. Everything else it reports with hc send. `address`: the child as
70	/// its parent calls it (`rohan/t7` from another machine). `last`: the last
71	/// lines of a plain program that ended, shown before where to read more.
72	fn note(t: &Terminal, address: &str, last: &[String]) -> String {
73	    let status = t.status.as_ref();
74	    let (what, look) = if blocked(t) {
75	        let kind = status.and_then(|s| s.kind.as_deref()).unwrap_or("waiting");
76	        (format!("is blocked ({kind})"), "See")
77	    } else if stuck(t) {
78	        match status.and_then(|s| s.msg.lines().next()).map(|m| m.trim_end_matches('.')).filter(|m| !m.is_empty()) {
79	            Some(msg) => (format!("hit an error: {}", msg.chars().take(200).collect::<String>()), "See"),
80	            None => ("hit an error".into(), "See"),
81	        }
82	    } else {
83	        let how = match (t.exit_code, t.signal) {
84	            (Some(code), _) => format!("exit {code}"),
85	            (_, Some(sig)) => format!("signal {sig}"),
86	            _ => t.reason.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "ended".into()),
87	        };
88	        (format!("exited ({how})"), "Read")
89	    };
90	    let name = t.name.as_ref().or(t.template.as_ref()).map(|n| format!(" {n}")).unwrap_or_default();
91	    let gap = match last.is_empty() {
92	        true => ". ".to_string(),
93	        false => format!(". Last lines:\n{}\n", last.join("\n")),
94	    };
95	    format!("<hc>{address}{name} {what}{gap}{look}: hc read {address}</hc>")
96	}

98	impl Core {
99	    /// The note about child `id`, called `address` by its parent.
100	    fn note_for(&self, st: &State, id: u32, address: &str) -> String {
101	        let t = &st.reg.terminals[&id];
102	        // Any end the parent hasn't seen is news, a success too: a background
103	        // build that worked is what it waits to hear. A plain program's shows its last lines.
104	        let last = match !t.is_live() && !t.reported {
105	            true => last_lines(&self.screen_text(st, id).unwrap_or_default()),
106	            false => Vec::new(),
107	        };
108	        note(t, address, &last)
109	    }

111	    /// Something notable happened to `id` (a turn ended, it got stuck, it exited).
112	    pub fn news(&self, st: &mut State, id: u32) {
113	        let Some(t) = st.reg.terminals.get_mut(&id) else { return };
114	        t.news += 1;
115	        if std::mem::take(&mut t.told_parent) && !stuck(t) && t.is_live() {
116	            t.seen = t.news; // a turn that ended after reporting to the parent
117	        }
118	        match (parent_id(t), &t.parent) {
119	            (Some(p), _) if t.notify => drop(self.jobs.send(Job::Notes(p))),
120	            (None, Some(afar)) if t.notify => drop(self.jobs.send(Job::NotesAfar(afar.clone()))),
121	            _ => {}
122	        }
123	    }
124	
125	    /// The caller looked at `id`; if it is the parent, that news is seen.
126	    pub fn saw(&self, caller: Option<&str>, id: u32) {
127	        let mut st = self.lock();
128	        if let Some(t) = st.reg.terminals.get_mut(&id)
129	            && caller.is_some()
130	            && t.parent.as_deref() == caller
131	            && t.seen < t.news
132	        {
133	            t.seen = t.news;
134	            t.seen_ms = Some(now_ms());
135	            self.save(&st);
136	        }
137	    }
138	
139	    /// Text from the agent `from` (a caller address) to the agent `to`, wrapped in
140	    /// a tag that says who sent it. As is when either isn't an agent: a person,
141	    /// a shell, a dialog. `reach`: also say how to answer (a worker's first message).
142	    pub fn tagged(&self, from: Option<&str>, to: u32, text: &str, reach: bool) -> String {
143	        // `notes = false`: nothing hc adds on its own, tags included.
144	        if !self.notes_on() {
145	            return text.to_string();
146	        }
147	        let st = self.lock();
148	        let sender = from.and_then(parse_id).filter(|f| *f != to).and_then(|f| st.reg.terminals.get(&f));
149	        let target = st.reg.terminals.get(&to);
150	        // A child on another machine calling back (`rohan/t7`).
151	        if let Some(afar) = from.filter(|f| f.contains('/'))
152	            && target.is_some_and(|t| t.reported)
153	        {
154	            return format!("<hc from=\"{afar}\">{text}</hc>");
155	        }
156	        match sender.filter(|s| s.reported && target.is_some_and(|t| t.reported)) {
157	            Some(s) if reach => {
158	                format!("<hc from=\"{}\" reach=\"hc send {} when done or stuck\">{text}</hc>", who(s), s.address)
159	            }
160	            Some(s) => format!("<hc from=\"{}\">{text}</hc>", who(s)),
161	            None => text.to_string(),
162	        }
163	    }

165	    /// Children of `parent` that are stuck or gone with news it hasn't seen,
166	    /// been told, or isn't already waiting for.
167	    fn unseen(&self, st: &State, address: &str) -> Vec<u32> {
168	        let address = address.to_string();
169	        st.reg
170	            .terminals
171	            .values()
172	            .filter(|t| t.parent.as_deref() == Some(address.as_str()) && t.notify)
173	            .filter(|t| t.news > t.seen.max(t.noted) && (stuck(t) || !t.is_live()))
174	            .filter(|t| !st.waiting.contains_key(&(address.clone(), t.id())))
175	            .map(Terminal::id)
176	            .collect()
177	    }

179	    /// Runs jobs for as long as the core runs.
180	    pub async fn run_jobs(self: Arc<Self>, mut jobs: tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<Job>) {
181	        while let Some(job) = jobs.recv().await {
182	            match job {
183	                Job::Notes(parent) => {
184	                    let start = self.lock().note_tasks.insert(parent);
185	                    if start {
186	                        tokio::spawn(self.clone().deliver_notes(parent));
187	                    }
188	                }
189	                Job::NotesAfar(parent) => {
190	                    let mut st = self.lock();
191	                    let Some(called) = crate::remote::called_there(&st, &parent) else { continue };
192	                    let kids = self.unseen(&st, &parent);
193	                    if kids.is_empty() {
194	                        continue;
195	                    }
196	                    let notes: Vec<String> = kids
197	                        .iter()
198	                        .map(|id| self.note_for(&st, *id, &format!("{called}/{}", crate::terminals::address(*id))))
199	                        .collect();
200	                    for id in &kids {
201	                        let t = st.reg.terminals.get_mut(id).expect("listed");
202	                        t.noted = t.noted.max(t.news);
203	                    }
204	                    self.save(&st);
205	                    crate::remote::tell_peer(&self, &mut st, &parent, &notes);
206	                }
207	                Job::Orphaned(parent) => {
208	                    let address = crate::terminals::address(parent);
209	                    let kids: Vec<u32> = {
210	                        let mut st = self.lock();
211	                        let kids: Vec<u32> = st
212	                            .reg
213	                            .terminals
214	                            .values()
215	                            .filter(|t| {
216	                                t.is_live() && t.die_with_parent && t.parent.as_deref() == Some(address.as_str())
217	                            })
218	                            .map(Terminal::id)
219	                            .collect();
220	                        st.killing.extend(&kids);
221	                        kids
222	                    };
223	                    let core = self.clone();
224	                    tokio::spawn(async move { core.kill(&kids).await });
225	                }
226	            }
227	        }
228	    }

230	    /// Types notes into `parent` whenever it can take them, until there are none.
231	    fn notes_on(&self) -> bool {
232	        crate::config::load(&self.paths.config).map(|c| c.notes.unwrap_or(true)).unwrap_or(true)
233	    }

235	    async fn deliver_notes(self: Arc<Self>, parent: u32) {
236	        let enabled = self.notes_on();
237	        loop {
238	            let ready = |st: &State| st.reg.terminals.get(&parent).is_none_or(|t| !t.is_live() || can_take_note(t));
239	            while !self.wait_for(Duration::from_secs(60), ready).await {}
240	            let alive = self.lock().reg.terminals.get(&parent).is_some_and(|t| t.is_live());
241	            if !alive || !enabled {
242	                break;
243	            }
244	            match self.type_note(parent).await {
245	                Ok(true) => continue,
246	                Ok(false) => {}
247	                Err(_) => continue, // it got busy while we waited for quiet: try again
248	            }
249	            let mut st = self.lock();
250	            if self.unseen(&st, &crate::terminals::address(parent)).is_empty() && !st.afar_notes.contains_key(&parent) {
251	                st.note_tasks.remove(&parent);
252	                return;
253	            }
254	        }
255	        self.lock().note_tasks.remove(&parent);
256	    }
257	
258	    /// One batch of notes, built at typing time so stale news is dropped.
259	    async fn type_note(&self, parent: u32) -> Result<bool, RpcError> {
260	        let quiet = crate::config::load(&self.paths.config)
261	            .ok()
262	            .and_then(|c| c.notes_quiet)
263	            .map_or_else(crate::input::quiet, |s| Duration::from_secs_f64(s.max(0.0)));
264	        // Notes from other machines were decided there: type them as they are.
265	        let afar = self.lock().afar_notes.remove(&parent).unwrap_or_default();
266	        let typed = self
267	            .type_in(parent, quiet, |st, t| {
268	                if !can_take_note(t) {
269	                    return Err(RpcError::new("busy", "the parent got busy", ""));
270	                }
271	                let kids = self.unseen(st, &crate::terminals::address(parent));
272	                if kids.is_empty() && afar.is_empty() {
273	                    return Ok((Vec::new(), Vec::new()));
274	                }
275	                let mut text: Vec<String> =
276	                    kids.iter().map(|id| self.note_for(st, *id, &st.reg.terminals[id].address)).collect();
277	                text.extend(afar.iter().cloned());
278	                let bracketed = st.screens.get(&parent).is_some_and(|s| s.dec_mode(2004));
279	                let told = kids.iter().map(|id| (*id, st.reg.terminals[id].news)).collect();
280	                let steps = vec![
281	                    Step::Write(paste(bracketed, &text.join("\n"))),
282	                    Step::Pause(crate::input::PASTE_GAP),
283	                    Step::Write(b"\r".to_vec()),
284	                ];
285	                Ok((told, steps))
286	            })
287	            .await;
288	        let told: Vec<(u32, u64)> = match typed {
289	            Ok(told) => told,
290	            Err(e) => {
291	                if !afar.is_empty() {
292	                    self.lock().afar_notes.entry(parent).or_default().splice(0..0, afar);
293	                }
294	                return Err(e);
295	            }
296	        };
297	        let had_afar = !afar.is_empty();
298	        let mut st = self.lock();
299	        for (id, news) in &told {
300	            if let Some(t) = st.reg.terminals.get_mut(id) {
301	                t.noted = t.noted.max(*news);
302	            }
303	        }
304	        self.save(&st);
305	        Ok(!told.is_empty() || had_afar)
306	    }
307	}
308	
309	#[cfg(test)]
310	mod tests {
311	    use super::*;
312	    use crate::terminals::{NewTerminal, Registry};
313	
314	    #[test]

````text
1	# Security and trust
2	
3	Core runs commands with your account's access. It is not a sandbox or a permission broker for agents.
4	Anyone who can connect to its API can run commands, read and change files, and control its terminals with that access.
5	
6	[Back to the README](../README.md) · [API](../schema/README.md) · [Report a vulnerability](../SECURITY.md)
7	
8	## What runs
9	
10	The CLI starts a background core when it needs one.
11	Holder processes own the terminals so a core restart or update can leave programs running.
12	Programs run as the account that runs core, with its filesystem and network access.
13	Templates are shell commands and opening instructions, not isolation rules.
14	
15	Do not run core as root or as an administrator unless you intend to give its clients that access.
16	A status of blocked can prevent a normal send, but it is not an access boundary against another client.
17	
18	## Who can connect
19	
20	On Unix, core listens on a local Unix socket, not a public TCP port.
21	It creates its state and socket directories with mode 0700.
22	It does not repair permissions on directories that already exist.
23	Keep custom socket paths in directories only your account can enter.
24	There is no separate API password or per-client permission check.
25	Other programs running as your account are part of the trust boundary.
26	
27	On Windows, core uses named pipes. Their access rules allow the current account and SYSTEM.
28	The integrity label prevents a lower-integrity process from controlling an elevated core.
29	State files use the filesystem's directory permissions; core does not install a separate Windows state-directory ACL.
30	
31	Do not expose the socket or forward the raw API to people you would not trust with a shell on that machine.
32	
33	## Sessions
34	
35	The default session is named default.
36	Setting `HC_SESSION` selects a separate core, terminals, and state directory:
37	
38	```sh
39	HC_SESSION=scratch hc ls
40	```
41	
42	Sessions are useful for tests and separate sets of work.
43	They are not security boundaries: another process under the same account can select the same session.
44	Config and templates are shared across sessions in the same config home.
45	Tests should also use scratch XDG directories so they do not touch your real state or config.
46	
47	## Remote trust
48	
49	SSH handles login, host keys, and encryption. Core carries its protocol through that connection.
50	A custom connection command must provide its own trust and transport guarantees.
51	Core does not add another encryption layer or authenticate a remote user itself.
52	
53	Adding a machine gives local clients access to its hc account's commands, files, and terminals.
54	Trust the destination, the SSH target, and any custom connection command.
55	Machine installation or update copies executable code there and restarts that session's core.
56	Forgetting a machine removes the connection here, not its remote programs or state.
57	See [machines](machines.md).
58	
59	## State and endpoints
60	
61	| Item | Default |
62	| --- | --- |
63	| Unix state | `~/.local/state/herdr-core/<session>/` |
64	| Unix config | `~/.config/herdr-core/config.toml` |
65	| Windows state | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\herdr-core\<session>\` |
66	| Windows config | `%APPDATA%\herdr-core\config.toml` |
67	| Templates | A templates directory beside the config file |
68	
69	`XDG_STATE_HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` override the state and config homes on both platforms.
70	On Unix, sockets live under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/herdr-core/` when set.
71	Otherwise core uses `/run/user/<uid>/herdr-core/` if that runtime directory exists, then falls back to the session's state directory.
72	The client socket is named `<session>.sock`; holder sockets sit beside it.
73	On Windows, pipe names include the account name and session.
74	
75	`HC_SOCKET` overrides the client endpoint. Otherwise the socket setting in config can override it.
76	A custom endpoint does not move the state directory.
77	Keep Unix socket paths short; the OS limits their length.
78	
79	State includes terminal records, saved screens and history, machine connections, peer records, and API documents.
80	Core and holder logs also live there. Treat the whole directory as private: terminal output and saved screens may contain secrets.
81	State is not encrypted by core. Removing state is destructive, not a way to stop running programs safely.
82	
83	## Updates and signing
84	
85	```sh
86	hc update
87	hc update --version 0.1.5
88	```
89	
90	The version form means at least that version, not an exact downgrade.
91	Updates restart the core while holders keep the terminals running.
92	An update may also restart an older running core when the installed binary is already current.
93	
94	Release installers and updates download a manifest and check the archive's SHA-256 against it.
95	The default release service is HTTPS at releases.herdr.dev.
96	This trusts the release service and HTTPS; a checksum is not an independently signed release manifest.
97	The manifest is not verified with a separate signing key.
98	
99	Windows release signing is conditional in the release workflow.
100	When the signing profile is configured, the workflow signs and verifies the executable with Azure Artifact Signing.
101	If the profile is unset, it publishes unsigned builds. Windows may block those builds.
102	Do not assume every downloaded build is signed.
103	
104	`hc update --from /path/to/herdr-core` installs a local build instead of downloading one.
105	Only use a build you trust. The updater's compatibility checks are not a review of its code.
106
````

````text
1	# herdr-core (`hc`)
2	
3	`hc` runs programs and coding agents in terminals that stay alive after you leave.
4	Agents can start other agents, send them work, and hear back; you can attach to any terminal and take over.
5	
6	Core draws nothing. Use it from your shell, an agent, or your own app.
7	
8	## Install
9	
10	Linux and macOS:
11	
12	```sh
13	curl -fsSL https://releases.herdr.dev/core/install.sh | sh
14	```
15	
16	Windows (PowerShell):
17	
18	```powershell
19	powershell -c "irm https://releases.herdr.dev/core/install.ps1 | iex"
20	```
21	
22	Builds are available for Linux and macOS on x86_64 and aarch64, and Windows on x86_64.
23	Linux builds are static. On Windows, templates and quoted shell commands need `sh` on PATH, such as Git for Windows provides.
24	
25	Run `hc update` to update. Running terminals keep running.
26	See [security](docs/security.md) for the trust and signing details.
27	
28	## Run it and come back
29	
30	```sh
31	hc run cargo test                  # stream output and wait for it
32	hc run --bg --name web bun dev     # start it and return
33	hc ls                             # see live terminals
34	hc attach web                     # take over; Ctrl+\ detaches
35	hc read web --lines 100            # read without attaching
36	```
37	
38	Closing your viewer does not end the program.
39	A waiting run checks in after 180 seconds by default, leaving the program running.
40	It prints the terminal's address so you can read it or wait again.
41	
42	For a terminal you want to keep even if its program is lost, use `hc run --keep`.
43	Recovery starts a fresh shell, never reruns the task.
44	A normal exit or an explicit kill still ends it.
45	
46	## Default shell
47	
48	With no program, `hc run --bg` starts the machine's shell: `$SHELL` (or
49	`/bin/sh`) on Unix, PowerShell 7 on Windows if available, else Windows PowerShell.
50	Override it in `~/.config/herdr-core/config.toml` (Windows:
51	`%APPDATA%\herdr-core\config.toml`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/herdr-core/config.toml`
52	when set):
53	
54	```toml
55	shell = ["nu"]
56	# Windows Git Bash (literal strings keep backslashes):
57	# shell = ['C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe', '--login', '-i']
58	```
59	
60	The list is an executable followed by separate arguments, without extra path
61	quoting. It must contain a nonempty executable. Changes apply to the next new
62	shell or `keep` recovery, including recovery after a restart; no restart is
63	needed. Running terminals, explicit programs, and quoted command lines keep
64	their behavior. A bad setting reports a config error; a shell that cannot start
65	reports `spawn_failed`. Recovery stays pending and retries, with errors in
66	`core.log` (config) or `holder.log` (spawn); it never silently falls back to another shell.
67	
68	## Agents run agents
69	
70	Give an agent `hc --skill`. It prints the agent docs in one read, including how to delegate, wait, report back, and clean up.
71	
72	[Templates](docs/templates.md) give an agent a command and a role.
73	After saving the reviewer example from that page:
74	
75	```sh
76	hc templates
77	hc run --bg --name review reviewer "Review src/x.rs. Read-only."
78	hc send review "Focus on the error path."
79	hc read review --lines 100
80	```
81	
82	Agents started inside an hc terminal become its children.
83	They can report back with `hc send` and wait for their children with `hc wait --children all`.
84	The parent gets notes when a child needs attention or ends.
85	Children end with their parent unless started with `--outlive-parent`.
86	
87	## Every machine
88	
89	```sh
90	hc machine add my-ssh-host --name box
91	hc run --on box --cwd /srv/app cargo test
92	hc attach box/t3
93	```
94	
95	Use the address returned by your run, not the example's `box/t3`.
96	Programs and files stay on that machine. Your local core brings its terminals into the same list.
97	[Machines](docs/machines.md) covers SSH, custom connections, remote files, and reconnecting.
98	
99	## Status comes from the program
100	
101	An agent can say it is working, done, blocked, or in error through OSC 7501, the Program Status Protocol.
102	Core stores what it reports. It does not guess from screen text or recognize agent brands.
103	A program that does not report status has none.
104	
105	Use `hc get review` for a snapshot or `hc events` to follow changes.
106	
107	## Build your own client
108	
109	`hc schema` prints the request/response API as OpenRPC with JSON Schema.
110	[The API docs](schema/README.md) cover connecting, terminal streams, events, and status.
111	Use `hc connect` to carry the protocol over stdin and stdout, including through SSH.
112	
113	## Docs
114	
115	- [Commands](docs/commands.md): generated from the binary's help.
116	- [Machines](docs/machines.md): work across machines.
117	- [Templates](docs/templates.md): reusable agent roles.
118	- [Security](docs/security.md): access, state, and updates.
119	- [API](schema/README.md): build a client.
120	
121	For a quick lookup, run `hc --help` or a command's help, such as `hc run --help`.
122	For agents, use `hc --skill`.
123	
124	## Build from source
125	
126	You need Rust, Zig 0.16, and just. CI pins the Rust version in [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml).
127	
128	```sh
129	git submodule update --init --depth 1
130	cargo build --locked -p herdr-core
131	just check
132	```
133	
134	`just install` installs this checkout and restarts your core. Running terminals keep running.
135	`just docs` refreshes the command reference. `just docs-check` checks it and the examples; CI runs the same tests.
136	
137	See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for contributor setup and checks.
138	
139	License: [Apache-2.0](LICENSE). `hc --licenses` prints the included third-party licenses.
140	After a dependency change, regenerate them with `just notices`.
141
````

1	//! `terminal.run`: start a program or template, and with `wait` see it through like a shell.
2	
3	use super::*;
4	
5	pub(super) async fn terminal_run(core: Ctx<'_>, mut p: RunParams) -> Result<RunResult, RpcError> {
6	    // A template is found only by template lookup, never by terminal name.
7	    let template = match p.argv.first() {
8	        Some(name) => crate::templates::load(&core.paths, name)?,
9	        None => None,
10	    };
11	    let first = template.as_ref().map(|t| crate::templates::first_message(t, &p.argv[1..].join(" ")));
12	    match (&template, p.line.take(), p.argv.is_empty()) {
13	        // A shell line (VAR=value prefixes, quotes, ~); sh replaces itself with a single command.
14	        (Some(t), None, _) => p.argv = vec!["sh".into(), "-c".into(), t.command.clone()],
15	        // The shell is this machine's: the caller may be on another kind.
16	        (None, Some(line), true) => p.argv = crate::platform::shell_line(&line),
17	        (None, None, true) => p.argv = crate::config::load(&core.paths.config)?.shell()?,
18	        (None, None, false) => {}
19	        _ => return Err(RpcError::invalid_params("give argv or line, not both")),
20	    }
21	    let quiet_ready = template.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.ready_when_quiet);
22	    let caller = p.caller.clone();
23	    let timeout = if p.wait { Some(wait_timeout(core, p.timeout)?) } else { None }; // checked before it starts
24	    if p.wait {
25	        // A pager in a real terminal waits for a person: a waited run would hang on it.
26	        for pager in ["PAGER", "GIT_PAGER", "GH_PAGER"] {
27	            p.env.insert(pager.into(), "cat".into());
28	        }
29	    }
30	    let started = start(core, p, template).await?;
31	    let id = started.id();
32	    let first_message = match first.filter(|text| !text.is_empty()) {
33	        Some(text) => Some(core.first_message(id, quiet_ready, &text, caller.as_deref()).await),
34	        None => None,
35	    };
36	    let (wait, output) = match timeout {
37	        None => (None, None),
38	        Some(timeout) => {
39	            // A template's task: wait for the turn it started, not the idle before it.
40	            let after_turn = first_message.as_ref().and_then(|f| f.turn);
41	            let r = watch(core, caller.clone(), id, WaitSpec { output: None, timeout, after_turn }).await;
42	            let full_screen = core.lock().screens.get(&id).is_some_and(|s| s.alt_screen());
43	            let read = ReadParams {
44	                terminal: crate::terminals::address(id),
45	                caller: None,
46	                lines: if full_screen { 0 } else { FINISHED_LINES },
47	            };
48	            let text = tail(terminal_read(core, read).await.map(|r| r.text).unwrap_or_default(), id);
49	            has_seen(core, caller.as_deref(), id);
50	            (Some(r), Some(text))
51	        }
52	    };
53	    core.flush_saved().await?;
54	    Ok(RunResult { terminal: Public(started), first_message, wait, output })
55	}

57	/// Output a run hands back: at most `RUN_OUTPUT` bytes, whole lines from the
58	/// end (errors are at the end), saying where the rest is.
59	pub(crate) fn tail(text: String, id: u32) -> String {
60	    const RUN_OUTPUT: usize = 50_000;
61	    if text.len() <= RUN_OUTPUT {
62	        return text;
63	    }
64	    let mut from = text.len() - RUN_OUTPUT;
65	    while !text.is_char_boundary(from) {
66	        from += 1;
67	    }
68	    let from = text[from..].find('\n').map_or(from, |at| from + at + 1);
69	    format!(
70	        "[hc] earlier output cut: hc read {} --lines {FINISHED_LINES}\n{}",
71	        crate::terminals::address(id),
72	        &text[from..]
73	    )
74	}
75	
76	/// A stopping core starts nothing: whatever it started now would outlive the stop.
77	pub(crate) fn not_stopping(st: &crate::runtime::State) -> Result<(), RpcError> {
78	    match st.stopping {
79	        true => Err(RpcError::new("unavailable", "the core is stopping", "run it again once it has stopped")),
80	        false => Ok(()),
81	    }
82	}
83	
84	pub(super) async fn start(
85	    core: &Arc<Core>,

88	) -> Result<Terminal, RpcError> {

107	    let identity = format!(
108	        "{} {}",

110	        env.get("TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION").map_or("", String::as_str)
111	    )
112	    .trim()

117	        // Started from a terminal on the machine that dialed in: `desktop/t3`.
118	        (None, Some(caller)) if !p.no_parent && from_afar => {
119	            caller.split_once('/').and_then(|(_, t)| crate::terminals::parse_id(t)).map(|_| caller.clone())
120	        }
121	        (None, Some(caller)) if !p.no_parent => crate::terminals::parse_id(caller)
122	            .filter(|id| core.lock().reg.terminals.contains_key(id))
123	            .map(crate::terminals::address),

125	    };

128	        not_stopping(&st)?;
129	        let instance = st

131	            .ok_or_else(|| {

143	            parent,

146	            keep: p.keep,

150	            cwd: cwd.clone(),

162	        st.pending.insert(id, tx);

176	        Ok(Ok(Ok(started))) => Ok(started),

178	            st.pending.remove(&id);
179	            let keep = st.reg.terminals.get(&id).is_some_and(|t| {
180	                t.keep && t.is_live() && (t.reason.is_some() || t.pid.is_some() || !matches!(&other, Ok(Ok(Err(_)))))
181	            });
182	            if keep {

184	                if t.pid.is_none() && t.reason.is_none() {
185	                    t.reason = Some("spawn_pending".into());
186	                    core.save(&st);
187	                }
188	            } else {
189	                st.screens.remove(&id);
190	                core.remove(&mut st, id);
191	            }
192	            let error = match other {
193	                Ok(Ok(Err(e))) => e,
194	                _ => "the holder did not answer".into(),
195	            };

202	pub(crate) fn terminal_env(
203	    core: &Core,

207	) -> (BTreeMap<String, String>, String) {

193	/// Decided from the children's current facts, again on every change:
194	/// `all`: none is working (one that hasn't reported yet is still starting);
195	/// the reply lists every child, finished ones too. `any`: a child with news
196	/// (for the parent itself: news it hasn't seen, even from before the wait), or
197	/// a message typed into the waiting parent (it sits in its queue until this
198	/// call ends); idle children are waited on too.
199	/// `others`: children on other machines count too, so none here is no answer.
200	pub(super) async fn wait_children(
201	    core: &Arc<Core>,
202	    p: &WaitParams,
203	    mode: &str,
204	    timeout: Duration,
205	    others: bool,
206	) -> Result<WaitResult, RpcError> {
207	    if p.output.is_some() {
208	        return Err(RpcError::invalid_params("children waits take no output; wait on one terminal for that"));
209	    }
210	    let (parent, address) = children_of(core, p)?;
211	    let done = |children: Vec<WaitResult>| WaitResult {
212	        terminal: address.clone(),
213	        ended: true,
214	        reason: "children".into(),
215	        status: None,
216	        turn: 0,
217	        exit_code: None,
218	        signal: None,
219	        children,
220	        from: None,
221	    };
222	    let any = mode == "any";
223	    let caller = p.caller.clone();
224	    let listen = caller.as_deref() == Some(address.as_str());
225	    let kids_of = |st: &crate::runtime::State| -> Vec<Terminal> {
226	        st.reg.terminals.values().filter(|t| t.parent.as_deref() == Some(address.as_str())).cloned().collect()
227	    };
228	    let busy = |t: &Terminal| {
229	        t.is_live() && !t.program_lost() && (!t.reported || t.status.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| s.state == "working"))
230	    };
231	    // While the caller waits on them, it needs no notes about them.
232	    let (start, _watching): (std::collections::HashMap<u32, u64>, Vec<Watching>) = {
233	        let mut st = core.lock();
234	        let kids = kids_of(&st);
235	        let watching = kids
236	            .iter()
237	            .filter_map(|t| caller.clone().map(|c| (c, t.id())))
238	            .map(|key| {
239	                *st.waiting.entry(key.clone()).or_default() += 1;
240	                Watching { core: core.clone(), key: Some(key) }
241	            })
242	            .collect();
243	        (kids.iter().map(|t| (t.id(), t.news)).collect(), watching)
244	    };
245	    let news = |t: &Terminal| match listen {
246	        true => t.news > t.seen.max(t.noted),
247	        false => t.news > start.get(&t.id()).copied().unwrap_or(0),
248	    };
249	    // The caller has these now; a `--rm` child it was waiting for can go.
250	    let seen = |ids: &[u32]| ids.iter().for_each(|&id| has_seen(core, caller.as_deref(), id));
251	    let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + timeout;
252	    loop {
253	        let changed = core.changed.notified();
254	        tokio::pin!(changed);
255	        changed.as_mut().enable();
256	        let (kids, message) = {
257	            let mut st = core.lock();
258	            (kids_of(&st), parent.filter(|_| listen).and_then(|id| st.messages.remove(&id)))
259	        };
260	        let ready: Option<Vec<&Terminal>> = match any {
261	            true => {
262	                let fresh: Vec<&Terminal> = kids.iter().filter(|t| news(t)).collect();
263	                let nothing_can_happen = !others && !kids.iter().any(Terminal::is_live) && message.is_none();
264	                (!fresh.is_empty() || message.is_some() || nothing_can_happen).then_some(fresh)
265	            }
266	            false => (!kids.iter().any(busy)).then(|| kids.iter().collect()),
267	        };
268	        if let (None, Some(from)) = (&ready, &message) {
269	            let children = kids.iter().map(|t| as_is(t, !busy(t))).collect();
270	            return Ok(WaitResult { ended: false, reason: "message".into(), from: from.clone(), ..done(children) });
271	        }
272	        if let Some(results) = ready {
273	            seen(&results.iter().map(|t| t.id()).collect::<Vec<_>>());
274	            let mut r = done(results.iter().map(|t| as_is(t, true)).collect());
275	            if let Some(from) = message {
276	                if r.children.is_empty() {
277	                    r.reason = "message".into();
278	                }
279	                r.from = from;
280	            }
281	            return Ok(r);
282	        }
283	        if tokio::time::Instant::now() >= deadline {
284	            let children = kids.iter().filter(|t| t.is_live()).map(|t| as_is(t, !busy(t))).collect();
285	            return Ok(WaitResult { ended: false, reason: "timeout".into(), ..done(children) });
286	        }

18

21	- The TODO item is in `P?` and needs evaluation before it can be prioritized
