13	/// Remembers our binary's path at startup. After an update swaps the file,
14	/// asking the OS again would name the deleted old binary.
15	pub fn remember_exe() {
16	    if let Ok(exe) = std::env::current_exe() {

22	/// The package manager this hc came from, or "system package manager" as a

24	pub fn installed_by() -> Option<&'static str> {
25	    let exe = EXE.get().cloned().or_else(|| std::env::current_exe().ok())?;
26	    let path = exe.canonicalize().unwrap_or(exe);
27	    manager_of(&path.to_string_lossy()).or_else(|| (!platform::can_replace(&path)).then_some("system package manager"))

30	fn manager_of(path: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
31	    [("/Cellar/", "homebrew"), ("/nix/store/", "nix"), ("/mise/installs/", "mise")]
32	        .into_iter()
33	        .find(|(mark, _)| path.contains(mark))
34	        .map(|(_, manager)| manager)

46	/// Which build this process runs: the linker's build id, so a copy of the same
47	/// bytes is the same build (a lazy filesystem swaps in such a copy under a
48	/// running core). Elsewhere, or without one: same file, same build. Taken at
49	/// startup, so an update that swaps the file later doesn't change it.
50	pub fn build_id() -> String {
51	    static BUILD: std::sync::OnceLock<String> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
52	    BUILD
53	        .get_or_init(|| {
54	            #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
55	            if let Some(id) = running_build_id() {
56	                return format!("elf:{id}");
57	            }
58	            let exe = EXE.get().cloned().or_else(|| std::env::current_exe().ok());
59	            exe.and_then(|e| std::fs::metadata(e).ok()).map(|m| platform::file_identity(&m)).unwrap_or_default()
60	        })
61	        .clone()

81	fn connect_starting(paths: &Paths, explicit: bool) -> Result<Stream, RpcError> {
82	    match platform::connect(&paths.socket) {
83	        Ok(stream) => return Ok(stream),
84	        Err(e) => {
85	            if let Some(error) = platform::connect_error(&e, false) {
86	                return Err(error);
87	            }
88	        }
89	    }
90	    if let Some(err) = listening_elsewhere(paths) {
91	        return Err(err);
92	    }
93	    platform::may_autostart(explicit)?;
94	    spawn_core(paths)?;
95	    wait_for_socket(&paths.socket, "core").map_err(unavailable)
96	}

116	#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
117	fn running_build_id() -> Option<String> {
118	    use std::io::Read;
119	    let mut head = Vec::new();
120	    std::fs::File::open("/proc/self/exe").ok()?.take(64 << 10).read_to_end(&mut head).ok()?;
121	    elf_build_id(&head)
122	}
123	
124	/// The GNU build-id note of a 64-bit little-endian ELF, from its first bytes.
125	#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
126	fn elf_build_id(elf: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {
127	    let int = |at: usize, len: usize| {
128	        let bytes = elf.get(at..at.checked_add(len)?)?;
129	        Some(bytes.iter().rev().fold(0usize, |n, &b| n << 8 | b as usize))
130	    };
131	    if elf.get(..6)? != b"\x7fELF\x02\x01" {
132	        return None;
133	    }
134	    let (table, size) = (int(0x20, 8)?, int(0x36, 2)?);
135	    (0..int(0x38, 2)?).find_map(|i| {
136	        let header = table.checked_add(i.checked_mul(size)?)?;
137	        if int(header, 4)? != 4 {
138	            return None; // not PT_NOTE
139	        }
140	        let mut at = int(header + 8, 8)?;
141	        let end = at.checked_add(int(header + 0x20, 8)?)?;
142	        while at.checked_add(12)? <= end {
143	            let (name, desc, kind) = (int(at, 4)?, int(at + 4, 4)?, int(at + 8, 4)?);
144	            let desc_at = (at + 12).checked_add(name.next_multiple_of(4))?;
145	            if kind == 3 && elf.get(at + 12..at + 12 + name)? == b"GNU\0" {
146	                let id = elf.get(desc_at..desc_at.checked_add(desc)?)?;
147	                return Some(id.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect());
148	            }
149	            at = desc_at.checked_add(desc.next_multiple_of(4))?;
150	        }
151	        None
152	    })
153	}
154	
155	#[cfg(all(test, target_os = "linux"))]
156	#[test]
157	fn the_build_is_named_by_the_linkers_build_id() {
158	    let elf = std::fs::read("/proc/self/exe").unwrap();
159	    let id = elf_build_id(&elf).expect("the linker stamps a build id");
160	    assert_eq!(build_id(), format!("elf:{id}"));
161	    let note = elf.windows(16).position(|w| w[12..] == *b"GNU\0" && w[8..12] == [3, 0, 0, 0]).unwrap() + 16;
162	    assert_eq!(id.len() / 2, elf[note - 12] as usize);
163	    assert_eq!(&id[..2], format!("{:02x}", elf[note]));
164	    assert_eq!(elf_build_id(b"#!/bin/sh\n"), None);
165	}

167	pub fn spawn_core(paths: &Paths) -> Result<(), RpcError> {
168	    spawn_detached(paths, &["serve"], "core.log").map_err(|e| unavailable(format!("cannot start core: {e}")))
169	}
170	
171	/// Starts `herdr-core <args>` on its own (Linux: as a user service), logging
172	/// to the state dir.
173	pub fn spawn_detached(paths: &Paths, args: &[&str], log: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {
174	    paths.create_dirs()?;
175	    let log = paths.state.join(log);
176	    let exe = EXE.get().cloned().map_or_else(std::env::current_exe, Ok)?;
177	    let mut cmd = Command::new(exe);
178	    // A core or holder started from inside a terminal is not that terminal's:
179	    // ending the terminal must not end them.
180	    cmd.args(args).env_remove(crate::sweep::VAR).env(crate::sweep::RUNTIME, "1");
181	    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
182	    if let Some(started) = platform::systemd::spawn(&cmd, &log) {
183	        return started;
184	    }
185	    if platform::spawn_core_job(&mut cmd, &log) {
186	        return Ok(());
187	    }
188	    let log = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(log)?;
189	    platform::spawn_detached(cmd, log)
190	}

192	pub fn wait_for_socket(path: &std::path::Path, what: &str) -> Result<Stream, String> {
193	    let start = Instant::now();
194	    loop {
195	        if let Ok(stream) = platform::connect(path) {
196	            return Ok(stream);
197	        }
198	        if start.elapsed() > Duration::from_secs(5) {
199	            return Err(format!("{what} did not start within 5 s"));
200	        }
201	        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));
202	    }
203	}

205	const CLOSED: &str = "the core closed the connection";
206	
207	/// A call the core cut off: if a core answers again soon it was a restart
208	/// (an update, usually) and the command can simply run again.
209	pub fn explain_closed(paths: &Paths, err: RpcError) -> RpcError {
210	    if err.message != CLOSED {
211	        return err;
212	    }
213	    // A loaded machine can take seconds to bring the new core up (seen on CI
214	    // at over 3 s); only a core that really stopped waits this out.
215	    let start = Instant::now();
216	    while start.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(10) {
217	        if connect_existing(paths).is_some() {
218	            return RpcError::new(
219	                "unavailable",
220	                "the core restarted while this ran (an update?)",
221	                "run the command again; terminals kept running",
222	            );
223	        }
224	        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
225	    }
226	    RpcError::new(
227	        "unavailable",
228	        "the core stopped while this ran",
229	        "run the command again to start it; see core.log in the state directory if it keeps stopping",
230	    )
231	}
232	
233	/// One plain-mode call. Returns the result, the core's error, or `unavailable`.
234	pub fn call(stream: &Stream, method: &str, params: Value) -> Result<Value, RpcError> {
235	    let lost = |e: std::io::Error| unavailable(format!("lost the core: {e}"));
236	    let req = json!({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": method, "params": params});
237	    (&*stream).write_all(format!("{req}\n").as_bytes()).map_err(lost)?;
238	    let mut line = String::new();
239	    BufReader::new(stream).read_line(&mut line).map_err(lost)?;
240	    if line.is_empty() {
241	        return Err(unavailable(CLOSED.into()));
242	    }
243	    let reply: Value = serde_json::from_str(&line).map_err(|e| unavailable(e.to_string()))?;
244	    match reply.get("error") {
245	        Some(err) => Err(RpcError::from_json(err)),
246	        None => Ok(reply["result"].clone()),
247	    }
248	}

250	/// The hc terminal we run in, if it belongs to the core we talk to: its id
251	/// means nothing to another session's core.
252	pub fn terminal_id() -> Option<String> {
253	    let own_core = std::env::var_os("HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET")
254	        .is_none_or(|s| Paths::from_env().is_ok_and(|p| p.socket.as_os_str() == s));
255	    std::env::var("HC_TERMINAL_ID").ok().filter(|_| own_core)
256	}

1	//! Where a core lives (socket, holder socket, state, config) and how its
2	//! state files are read and written.
3	
4	use crate::rpc::RpcError;
5	use std::io;
6	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
7	
8	/// Where one core keeps its socket and state. `HC_SESSION` names an isolated core.
9	pub struct Paths {
10	    pub socket: PathBuf,
11	    pub holder_socket: PathBuf,
12	    pub state: PathBuf,
13	    pub config: PathBuf,
14	}
15	
16	impl Paths {
17	    pub fn from_env() -> Result<Paths, RpcError> {
18	        let session = session(std::env::var("HC_SESSION").ok())?;
19	        let xdg = |var: &str, fallback: PathBuf| {
20	            std::env::var_os(var).filter(|v| !v.is_empty()).map_or(fallback, PathBuf::from)
21	        };
22	        let (state_home, config_home) = crate::platform::data_dirs();
23	        let state = xdg("XDG_STATE_HOME", state_home).join("herdr-core").join(&session);
24	        let config = xdg("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", config_home).join("herdr-core").join("config.toml");
25	        // Where sockets go (Windows: the named pipe namespace), and their name prefix.
26	        let (run, prefix) = crate::platform::endpoints(&state);
27	        // HC_SOCKET, else `socket` in config, else the runtime dir. The holder sits beside it.
28	        let chosen = std::env::var_os("HC_SOCKET")
29	            .filter(|v| !v.is_empty())
30	            .map(PathBuf::from)
31	            .or_else(|| crate::config::load(&config).ok()?.socket.map(PathBuf::from));
32	        let (socket, holder_socket) = match chosen {
33	            Some(socket) => (socket.clone(), socket.with_extension("holder.sock")),
34	            None => (run.join(format!("{prefix}{session}.sock")), run.join(format!("{prefix}{session}.holder.sock"))),
35	        };
36	        // Holders listen on `<holder_socket minus .sock>.<id>.sock`: the longest path.
37	        let longest = holder_socket.as_os_str().len() + 1 + HOLDER_ID;
38	        let max = crate::platform::MAX_SOCKET_PATH;
39	        if socket.as_os_str().len().max(longest) > max {
40	            return Err(RpcError::new(
41	                "usage",
42	                format!(
43	                    "the socket path for session {session:?} is too long here ({longest} bytes; this system allows {max})"
44	                ),
45	                "use a shorter HC_SESSION (or socket in the config)",
46	            ));
47	        }
48	        Ok(Paths { socket, holder_socket, config, state })
49	    }
50	
51	    pub fn create_dirs(&self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
52	        use crate::platform::private_dir;
53	        private_dir(&self.state)?;
54	        private_dir(self.socket.parent().expect("socket has a parent"))?;
55	        private_dir(self.holder_socket.parent().expect("socket has a parent"))
56	    }
57	}

59	/// A state file, or the empty default only when it doesn't exist yet: an
60	/// unreadable or broken one is an error, never silently replaced.
61	pub fn read_state<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned + Default>(path: &Path) -> io::Result<T> {
62	    let at = |e: &dyn std::fmt::Display| format!("{}: {e}", path.display());
63	    match std::fs::read(path) {
64	        Ok(bytes) => serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|e| io::Error::other(at(&e))),
65	        Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(T::default()),
66	        Err(e) => Err(io::Error::new(e.kind(), at(&e))),
67	    }
68	}
69	
70	pub fn write_atomic(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {
71	    let tmp = path.with_extension("tmp");
72	    std::fs::write(&tmp, bytes)?;
73	    std::fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).open(&tmp)?.sync_all()?;
74	    std::fs::rename(tmp, path)
75	}
76	
77	/// Hex digits in a holder's socket name.
78	pub const HOLDER_ID: usize = 8;
79	
80	/// The session name goes into folder and pipe names. Spaces around it are
81	/// dropped (cmd's `set X=a & ...` keeps the one before `&`); characters a
82	/// path can't hold are refused.
83	fn session(raw: Option<String>) -> Result<String, RpcError> {
84	    let name = raw.as_deref().map(str::trim).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).unwrap_or("default");
85	    if name == "." || name == ".." || name.chars().any(|c| c.is_control() || r#"/\:*?"<>|"#.contains(c)) {
86	        return Err(RpcError::new(
87	            "usage",
88	            format!("HC_SESSION {name:?} can't be a folder name"),
89	            "use letters, digits, - _ .",
90	        ));
91	    }
92	    Ok(name.into())
93	}

107	        assert_eq!(super::read_state::<Vec<u32>>(&dir.join("ok.json")).unwrap(), [1, 2]);

2	//! use. Frontmatter says how to start the agent; the body is its first message.

5	use crate::rpc::RpcError;

12	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
13	pub struct Template {
14	    pub name: String,
15	    pub description: String,
16	    /// Shell command line that starts the agent (the model is written here).
17	    pub command: String,
18	    pub body: String,
19	    /// `report` (default): ready at its first status report. `quiet`: ready
20	    /// once its output goes quiet, for agents that don't report status.
21	    pub ready_when_quiet: bool,
22	    pub submit: Option<String>,
23	    pub stop: Option<String>,
24	    pub paste_gap_ms: Option<u64>,
25	}
26	
27	#[derive(Serialize, JsonSchema)]
28	pub struct TemplateInfo {
29	    pub name: String,
30	    pub description: String,
31	    pub command: String,
32	    /// Set when the file can't be used.
33	    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
34	    pub error: Option<String>,
35	}
36	
37	pub fn dir(paths: &Paths) -> PathBuf {
38	    paths.config.parent().expect("config file has a dir").join("templates")
39	}
40	
41	fn parse(name: &str, text: &str) -> Result<Template, String> {
42	    let text = text.replace("\r\n", "\n");
43	    let rest = text.strip_prefix("---\n").ok_or("no frontmatter (start the file with ---)")?;
44	    let end = rest.find("\n---").ok_or("frontmatter never closes (---)")?;
45	    let (front, body) = (&rest[..end], &rest[end + 4..]);
46	    let mut t = Template {
47	        name: name.into(),
48	        description: String::new(),
49	        command: String::new(),
50	        body: body.strip_prefix('\n').unwrap_or(body).trim_end().into(),
51	        ready_when_quiet: false,
52	        submit: None,
53	        stop: None,
54	        paste_gap_ms: None,
55	    };
56	    for line in front.lines().filter(|l| !l.trim().is_empty()) {
57	        let (key, value) = line.split_once(':').ok_or_else(|| format!("not `key: value`: {line:?}"))?;
58	        let value = value.trim().to_string();
59	        match key.trim() {
60	            "name" => {} // the file name is the name
61	            "description" => t.description = value,
62	            "command" => t.command = value,
63	            "ready" => t.ready_when_quiet = value == "quiet",
64	            "submit" => t.submit = Some(value),
65	            "stop" => t.stop = Some(value),
66	            "paste_gap_ms" => t.paste_gap_ms = Some(value.parse().map_err(|_| "paste_gap_ms must be a number")?),
67	            _ => {} // unknown keys are someone else's
68	        }
69	    }
70	    if t.command.is_empty() {
71	        return Err("no command".into());
72	    }
73	    Ok(t)
74	}

76	/// The template called `name`, if there is one.
77	pub fn load(paths: &Paths, name: &str) -> Result<Option<Template>, RpcError> {
78	    if name.is_empty() || name.contains('/') || name.starts_with('.') {
79	        return Ok(None);
80	    }
81	    let path = dir(paths).join(format!("{name}.md"));
82	    match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
83	        Ok(text) => parse(name, &text)
84	            .map(Some)
85	            .map_err(|e| RpcError::new("invalid_template", format!("{}: {e}", path.display()), "see hc templates")),
86	        Err(_) => Ok(None),
87	    }
88	}

90	pub fn list(paths: &Paths) -> Vec<TemplateInfo> {

92	        .into_iter()
93	        .flatten()
94	        .flatten()
95	        .filter_map(|e| e.file_name().to_str()?.strip_suffix(".md").map(String::from))
96	        .collect();
97	    names.sort();
98	    names
99	        .into_iter()
100	        .map(|name| match load(paths, &name) {
101	            Ok(Some(t)) => TemplateInfo { name, description: t.description, command: t.command, error: None },
102	            Ok(None) => TemplateInfo {
103	                name,
104	                description: String::new(),
105	                command: String::new(),
106	                error: Some("unreadable".into()),
107	            },
108	            Err(e) => TemplateInfo { name, description: String::new(), command: String::new(), error: Some(e.message) },
109	        })
110	        .collect()

132	impl Core {
133	    /// Sends a template's first message once the agent is ready for input:
134	    /// its first status report (or, with `ready: quiet`, its output going quiet).
135	    /// Without that, nothing is typed: the screen may be a dialog.
136	    /// From an agent, it says who asked and how to answer.
137	    pub async fn first_message(&self, id: u32, quiet: bool, text: &str, from: Option<&str>) -> FirstMessage {
138	        let not_sent = |reason: String| FirstMessage { sent: false, started: None, reason: Some(reason), turn: None };
139	        let live = |st: &State| st.reg.terminals.get(&id).is_some_and(|t| t.is_live());
140	        let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + ready_timeout();
141	        if quiet {
142	            loop {
143	                let quiet_since = self.lock().last_output.get(&id).map(|t| t.elapsed() >= crate::input::OUTPUT_SETTLE);
144	                if quiet_since == Some(true) || !live(&self.lock()) {
145	                    break;
146	                }
147	                if tokio::time::Instant::now() >= deadline {
148	                    return not_sent(format!(
149	                        "its output never went quiet; check its screen (hc read {0}), then hc send {0}",
150	                        crate::terminals::address(id)
151	                    ));
152	                }
153	                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
154	            }
155	        } else {
156	            let reported = |st: &State| st.reg.terminals.get(&id).is_none_or(|t| t.reported || !t.is_live());
157	            let reported_now = |st: &State| st.reg.terminals.get(&id).is_some_and(|t| t.reported);
158	            if !self.wait_for(ready_timeout(), reported).await || !reported_now(&self.lock()) {
159	                if !live(&self.lock()) {
160	                    return not_sent("it exited before it was ready".into());
161	                }
162	                return not_sent(format!(
163	                    "it never reported its status, so it may be showing a dialog; check its screen (hc read {0}), then hc send {0}",
164	                    crate::terminals::address(id)
165	                ));
166	            }
167	        }
168	        if !live(&self.lock()) {
169	            return not_sent("it exited before it was ready".into());
170	        }
171	        let text = self.tagged(from, id, text, true);
172	        match self.send(id, &text, false, None).await {
173	            Ok(sent) => FirstMessage { sent: true, started: sent.started, reason: None, turn: Some(sent.turn) },
174	            Err(e) => not_sent(e.message),
175	        }
176	    }
177	}

1	//! `wait`: until a terminal is not working, driven by its events so even a
2	//! quick flicker counts. Already not working: it returns at once.
3	
4	use crate::events::{Filter, Sink};
5	use crate::runtime::Core;
6	use schemars::JsonSchema;
7	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
8	use std::time::Duration;
9	
10	/// Output kept for `output` matching.
11	const SEEN_MAX: usize = 64 * 1024;
12	
13	pub struct WaitSpec {
14	    /// Ends when output produced after the wait started contains this; then
15	    /// only blocked, error or exit end it otherwise.
16	    pub output: Option<String>,
17	    pub timeout: Duration,
18	    /// End at once if this turn already ended (a wait right after a send).
19	    pub after_turn: Option<u64>,
20	}
21	
22	#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema, Debug)]
23	pub struct WaitResult {
24	    pub terminal: String,
25	    /// False on timeout: a check-in, the terminal is still running.
26	    pub ended: bool,
27	    /// status, exit (including program loss in a kept terminal), output, timeout,
28	    /// or not_started (after a send: it did not start working; a plain wait
29	    /// still follows that send's turn); with
30	    /// `children`: children; message (someone messaged the waiter, any
31	    /// wait); for each child in `children`: status, exit, or running (still
32	    /// working).
33	    pub reason: String,
34	    /// The exact word the program reported (current word on timeout or output).
35	    pub status: Option<String>,
36	    pub turn: u64,
37	    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,
38	    pub signal: Option<i32>,
39	    /// With `children`: one result per child it reports on.
40	    pub children: Vec<WaitResult>,
41	    /// With a message: the sender's address (the text is already in your input);
42	    /// null when a person sent it.
43	    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
44	    pub from: Option<String>,
45	}
46	
47	/// Whether a status change from `prev` to `new` ends the wait.
48	fn ends(prev: Option<&str>, new: Option<&str>) -> bool {
49	    new != Some("working") && (prev == Some("working") || new != prev)
50	}
51	
52	/// Blocked or errored: no output is coming, the caller has to look.
53	fn stuck(word: Option<&str>) -> bool {
54	    matches!(word, Some("blocked" | "error"))
55	}
56	
57	/// Output without escape sequences, for matching what a person would read.
58	fn strip(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
59	    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes);
60	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
61	    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
62	    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
63	        if c != '\x1b' {
64	            if !c.is_control() || c == '\n' {
65	                out.push(c);
66	            }
67	            continue;
68	        }
69	        match chars.next() {
70	            Some('[') => while chars.next().is_some_and(|c| !('@'..='~').contains(&c)) {},
71	            Some(']') | Some('P') | Some('_') => {
72	                while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
73	                    if c == '\x07' {
74	                        break;
75	                    }
76	                    if c == '\x1b' && chars.peek() == Some(&'\\') {
77	                        chars.next();
78	                        break;
79	                    }
80	                }
81	            }
82	            _ => {}
83	        }
84	    }
85	    out
86	}
87	
88	impl Core {
89	    /// A wait's answer from the terminal's current facts; `word` overrides its status.
90	    pub fn wait_result(&self, id: u32, ended: bool, reason: &str, word: Option<Option<String>>) -> WaitResult {
91	        let st = self.lock();
92	        let t = st.reg.terminals.get(&id);
93	        WaitResult {
94	            terminal: crate::terminals::address(id),
95	            ended,
96	            reason: reason.into(),
97	            status: word.unwrap_or_else(|| t.and_then(|t| t.status.as_ref().map(|s| s.state.clone()))),
98	            turn: t.map_or(0, |t| t.turn),
99	            exit_code: t.and_then(|t| t.exit_code),
100	            signal: t.and_then(|t| t.signal),
101	            children: Vec::new(),
102	            from: None,
103	        }
104	    }
105	
106	    /// A message typed into `waiter` while it works ends the wait too: it
107	    /// sits in the waiter's queue until this returns.
108	    pub async fn wait(&self, id: u32, spec: WaitSpec, waiter: Option<u32>) -> WaitResult {
109	        let (tx, mut events) = tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel();
110	        let (out_tx, mut output) = tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel();
111	        let start = {
112	            let mut st = self.lock();
113	            self.subscribe(
114	                &mut st,
115	                Filter { terminal: Some(crate::terminals::address(id)), ..Default::default() },
116	                Sink::Waiter(tx),
117	            );
118	            if spec.output.is_some() {
119	                st.output_watch.entry(id).or_default().push(out_tx);
120	            }
121	            st.reg.terminals.get(&id).cloned()
122	        };
123	        let result =
124	            |ended: bool, reason: &str, word: Option<Option<String>>| self.wait_result(id, ended, reason, word);
125	        let Some(start) = start.filter(|t| t.is_live() && !t.program_lost()) else {
126	            return result(true, "exit", None);
127	        };
128	        if spec.after_turn.is_some_and(|k| start.turn > k) {
129	            return result(true, "status", None);
130	        }
131	        // Already not working: that is the answer. A program that never reported
132	        // is working until it exits. Not after a send whose turn hasn't started:
133	        // idle then is the old turn's word.
134	        let now = start.status.as_ref().map(|s| s.state.as_str());
135	        let pending = spec.after_turn.is_some() && !stuck(now);
136	        let already =
137	            if spec.output.is_some() { stuck(now) } else { start.reported && !pending && ends(Some("working"), now) };
138	        if already {
139	            return result(true, "status", None);
140	        }
141	        let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + spec.timeout;
142	        let mut prev = start.status.map(|s| s.state);
143	        let mut seen = String::new();
144	        loop {
145	            let changed = self.changed.notified();
146	            tokio::pin!(changed);
147	            changed.as_mut().enable();
148	            if let Some(from) = waiter.and_then(|w| self.lock().messages.remove(&w)) {
149	                return WaitResult { from, ..result(false, "message", None) };
150	            }
151	            tokio::select! {
152	                _ = changed, if waiter.is_some() => {}
153	                event = events.recv() => {
154	                    let Some(event) = event else { return result(true, "exit", None) };
155	                    match event["type"].as_str() {
156	                        Some("status") => {
157	                            let new = event["data"]["status"]["state"].as_str().map(String::from);
158	                            let stop = if spec.output.is_some() { stuck(new.as_deref()) } else { ends(prev.as_deref(), new.as_deref()) };
159	                            if stop {
160	                                return result(true, "status", Some(new));
161	                            }
162	                            prev = new;
163	                        }
164	                        Some("finished") | Some("lost") | Some("removed") => {
165	                            // With --rm the record may already be gone: the event says how it ended.
166	                            let mut r = result(true, "exit", Some(None));
167	                            let data = &event["data"];
168	                            r.exit_code = r.exit_code.or(data["exit_code"].as_i64().map(|c| c as i32));
169	                            r.signal = r.signal.or(data["signal"].as_i64().map(|s| s as i32));
170	                            r.turn = r.turn.max(start.turn);
171	                            return r;
172	                        }
173	                        _ => {}
174	                    }
175	                }
176	                Some(bytes) = output.recv() => {
177	                    seen.push_str(&strip(&bytes));
178	                    if spec.output.as_deref().is_some_and(|needle| seen.contains(needle)) {
179	                        return result(true, "output", None);
180	                    }
181	                    if seen.len() > SEEN_MAX {
182	                        let cut = seen.len() - SEEN_MAX / 2;
183	                        let cut = (cut..seen.len()).find(|i| seen.is_char_boundary(*i)).unwrap_or(0);
184	                        seen.drain(..cut);
185	                    }
186	                }
187	                _ = tokio::time::sleep_until(deadline) => return result(false, "timeout", None),
188	            }
189	        }
190	    }
191	}

201	        assert!(ends(Some("working"), Some("idle")));
202	        assert!(ends(Some("working"), Some("error")));
203	        assert!(ends(Some("working"), None), "cleared counts as not working");
204	        assert!(!ends(Some("idle"), Some("idle")), "a repeated word is no change");
205	        assert!(!ends(Some("idle"), Some("working")));

# Pueue → Herdr / Herdr Core agent continuation feasibility

## Context

使用者希望研究 `skills/local/pueue-job-queue/` 的兩種延伸：a/b/c jobs 完成後，由 d 回傳結果並喚回原本的 agent；或帶著預設 prompt 與結果建立乾淨的新 agent conversation。需要比較現有 Herdr 與新推出的 Herdr Core，做小型隔離測試，再判斷哪些內容值得納入 skill，而不是直接建立完整編排框架。

目前為規劃階段：僅做本地 help/schema 與上游文件／原始碼唯讀研究；尚未執行 jobs、傳送 prompts、安裝 hc 或修改 skill。

## 已確認的起點

- 本機：Herdr client/server 0.9.5（protocol 22）、Pueue 4.0.2、Codex 0.166.0；`HERDR_ENV=1`；`hc` 不在 PATH。
- Pueue `add --after` 是 **all-success**，不是 all-finished；失敗 dependency 會使 d 失敗且不執行。`pueue wait <ids>` 可等待 terminal 狀態，但 waiter 不應占用被等待 jobs 所需的 worker slot。
- Herdr `agent prompt` 是 agent-aware terminal submission；`notification show` 是給人的 UI 通知，不是喚起 agent turn。`agent get` 有 terminal ID 與可選 agent-session identity；prompt schema 沒有 expected-session compare-and-send precondition。
- Herdr socket 選擇優先序：explicit `--session` → `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` → `HERDR_SESSION` → default。延後執行需明確記錄 routing，不能使用 focused pane。
- Core 與現有 Herdr 的介面不同；Core 狀態依程式回報 OSC 7501，不辨識 agent 畫面。Core 的 send/inbox/parent 語意待本次上游閱讀補齊。
- 新版 Codex 有 `queue --thread ... --message ... [--resume]`；`--resume` 失敗僅警告、命令仍可能成功。因此列為 version-gated 對照，不把 command exit 0 視為 agent 已續跑。

## 建議範圍（研究完成後補齊）

1. 複用既有 queue completion 與 isolated-test helpers；把執行結果封裝成穩定檔案，再交給可選 transport。
2. 分開驗證 all-success d 與 all-settled notification；不改全域 pueued callback。
3. 對照 existing-session continuation 與 fresh-conversation handoff；fresh 不使用 resume/fork，亦不表示跳過 system/project instructions。
4. 先以 reference recipe + gotchas 為發布單位；只有測試證明重複且脆弱的邏輯才增加窄用途 helper。
5. 最終報告明列 verified / source-only / skipped，以及採納或暫緩的理由。

## 待補齊

- 既有 skill 可複用的精確 functions/files 與測試命令。
- Core send/run/parent 的實際 delivery 語意與隔離方式。
- 具體測試矩陣、檔案變更清單與驗收條件。

## Recommendation

**Use an opt-in completion adapter; leave Pueue’s dependency semantics unchanged.** Separate three actions: passive notification, prompting the original agent, and starting a fresh agent. They have different safety and delivery guarantees.

Read-only inspection completed; no files, queues, panes, or td state changed. Tests and live Herdr commands were not run.

### Dependency semantics

- **Success-only:** `d.after: [a,b,c]` already works. The submitter translates each dependency into `--after`; if any parent fails, `d` becomes `DependencyFailed` and never executes. Evidence: [submit-dag.py:242–252](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit-dag.py#L242), [dag-patterns.md:41–52](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/references/dag-patterns.md#L41). Failure propagation has an integration test: [test_submit.py:43–53](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/tests/test_submit.py#L43).
- **All-terminal, including failures:** use `wait.py --ids …` **without `--fail-fast`**, then dispatch. It waits until every selected task is `Done`; only `Success` counts as successful. Evidence: [wait.py:153–164](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py#L153), [wait.py:236–250](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py#L236).
- For all-terminal behavior, **do not make the watcher itself depend on `a,b,c`**. Run it outside the worker queue, or submit it independently into a dedicated control group. Avoid consuming worker slots or selecting itself.

### Existing hooks and reuse

- **Watcher exists:** `wait.py` polls internally, emits state changes on stderr and one JSON result on stdout. It has no notification, callback, or Herdr dispatch option. [wait.py:46–72](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py#L46), [wait.py:253–280](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py#L253).
- **Daemon callback is documented, not implemented by this skill:** a global shell command after each finished task, with claimed `PUEUE_*` environment variables. No callback tests exist. Verify those variables and coverage of killed/dependency-failed tasks against the installed Pueue before relying on them. Avoid a global callback for the first integration: it requires daemon configuration and per-run filtering/deduplication. [daemon-and-config.md:149–154](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/references/daemon-and-config.md#L149), [pueue.yml.example:40–44](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/assets/pueue.yml.example#L40).
- **Durability recipe already exists nearby:** one background blocking wait, plus atomic completion records that survive session loss. Reuse this design rather than scheduled agent polling. [long-running-jobs/SKILL.md:85–100](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/long-running-jobs/SKILL.md#L85), [completion-contracts.md:16–53](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/long-running-jobs/references/completion-contracts.md#L16). The existing marker script preserves command exit status, but does **not** save its output as a result artifact: [run-and-mark.sh:141–161](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/long-running-jobs/scripts/run-and-mark.sh#L141).

### Herdr integration constraints

- Capture explicit **server/session context, original pane/agent identity, cwd, run identity, and task IDs** at submission. Pane IDs change on moves; names follow live occupants; IDs are server-scoped. Never fall back to the focused pane. [Herdr SKILL.md:57–91](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/vendor/herdr/SKILL.md#L57).
- **Original agent:** use the agent surface, not raw terminal injection. Check identity/readiness; blocked or uncertain targets should leave a durable pending-delivery record rather than receive automatic input.
- **Fresh agent:** create an explicitly targeted, no-focus sibling pane, preserve cwd, parse the returned pane ID, start the requested agent kind, then prompt. `agent start` does not create layout. [Herdr SKILL.md:107–145](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/vendor/herdr/SKILL.md#L107).
- Prompt submission is not proof of a completed turn; timeout/stall is not proof of nondelivery. Blind retries can duplicate work. [Herdr SKILL.md:145–171](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/vendor/herdr/SKILL.md#L145).
- A passive notification is **not** an agent-context wake-up. Exact notification syntax needs installed CLI discovery; the vendored skill only names that command group.

### Important pitfalls

1. **Selectors are unions, frozen at startup.** Combining `--label-prefix` and `--group` broadens selection, not narrows it. Prefer explicit IDs from submission JSON. [wait.py:93–125,185–186](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py#L93).
2. **Exit 5 alone is insufficient:** vanished tasks also exit 5, without a JSON summary. Require valid JSON containing all expected IDs in `state == "Done"` before treating failure completion as final. [wait.py:201–207](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py#L201).
3. **Pause-on-failure can prevent all-terminal completion indefinitely.** The recommended config enables it, whereas test fixtures disable it. Use a timeout and report paused/incomplete state; never silently resume the user’s queue. [pueue.yml.example:23–30](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/assets/pueue.yml.example#L23), [conftest.py:88–96](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/tests/conftest.py#L88).
4. Persist results before cleanup/delivery; keep **job outcome separate from delivery outcome**. Pass concise summaries and artifact paths, not unbounded logs or entire captured environments.
5. No DAG output/ID interpolation exists. Validation retains only `cmd`, `after`, and `group`; adding YAML `notify:` or `env:` fields currently has no effect. [submit-dag.py:154–184](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit-dag.py#L154).

### Safest proposed file scope

**Add**
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/herdr-complete.py` — opt-in wait/result/dispatch adapter; explicit modes, finite timeouts, dry-run, structured output.
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/references/herdr-integration.md` — both dependency policies, target capture, recovery and delivery semantics.
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/tests/test_herdr_complete.py` — stub Herdr; no real pane mutations.

**Update**
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/SKILL.md` — short optional workflow/reference link.
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/tests/README.md` — adapter tests.
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/tests/conftest.py` — scope daemon fixtures/skipping to integration tests so stub-only tests run without Pueue.

Keep `submit.sh`, `submit-dag.py`, `wait.py`, default daemon config, and vendored Herdr unchanged initially.

**Test approach:** reuse the isolated daemon fixture and DAG timestamp assertions ([conftest.py:59–151](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/tests/conftest.py#L59), [test_dag.py:29–54](/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/tests/test_dag.py#L29)). Add cases for a fast failed parent plus slower siblings, missing tasks, pause/timeout, unknown terminal variants, unavailable/replaced/blocked agent, ambiguous delivery, fresh-pane response parsing, and dry-run making zero mutations.

444	async fn terminal_send(core: Ctx<'_>, p: SendParams) -> Result<SendResult, RpcError> {
445	    let timeout = wait_timeout(core, p.timeout)?; // checked before anything is typed
446	    let id = resolve(core, &p.terminal)?;
447	    let text = core.tagged(p.caller.as_deref(), id, &p.text, false);
448	    let sent = core.send(id, &text, p.force, p.only_if.map(|w| word(&w)).as_deref()).await?;
449	    if let Some(child) = p.caller.as_deref().and_then(crate::terminals::parse_id) {
450	        let mut st = core.lock();
451	        if let Some(c) = st
452	            .reg
453	            .terminals
454	            .get_mut(&child)

456	        {
457	            c.told_parent = true;
458	        }

463	            .caller

469	        st.messages.insert(id, from);

471	        core.changed.notify_waiters();
472	    }
473	    core.saw(p.caller.as_deref(), id);
474	    if let Some(caller) = &p.caller {
475	        core.lock().last_send.insert((caller.clone(), id), sent.turn);
476	    }
477	    let wait = if p.wait && sent.started == Some(false) {
478	        Some(core.wait_result(id, false, "not_started", None))
479	    } else if p.wait {
480	        let spec = WaitSpec { output: None, timeout, after_turn: Some(sent.turn) };
481	        Some(watched(core, p.caller.clone(), id, spec).await)
482	    } else {
483	        None
484	    };
485	    core.flush_saved().await?;
486	    Ok(SendResult { status: sent.status, turn: sent.turn, started: sent.started, wait })
487	}

722	fn follow_events(paths: &Paths, params: Value, json: bool) -> Result<(), RpcError> {
723	    use std::io::BufRead;

728	    } else {
729	        println!("{}", table(&json!({"terminals": snapshot["terminals"]})));
730	    }

732	        let Ok(line) = line else { break };
733	        if json {
734	            println!("{line}");
735	            continue;
736	        }
737	        let msg: Value = serde_json::from_str(&line).unwrap_or_default();
738	        let p = &msg["params"];
739	        match msg["method"].as_str() {
740	            Some("event") if p["type"] == "doc" => {
741	                let name = p["data"]["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("?");
742	                let machine = p["machine"].as_str().map(|m| format!("{m}/")).unwrap_or_default();
743	                println!("{machine}{name}  doc  version {}", p["data"]["version"]);

770	/// A run that waited: its output as text (like read), a last line when there
771	/// is more to say, and the program's exit code as hc's (124: still running).
772	fn ran(r: &Value) -> Result<Option<Out>, RpcError> {
773	    use std::io::Write;
774	    let t = r["address"].as_str().unwrap_or("?");
775	    // An older hc (on another machine) ignores the wait: it only started it.
776	    if r.get("wait").is_none() {
777	        let fix = t.split_once('/').map(|(m, _)| format!(": hc machine update {m}")).unwrap_or_default();
778	        println!("[hc] started as {t}, not waited on: that hc is older{fix}");
779	        std::process::exit(0);
780	    }
781	    let w = &r["wait"];
782	    let status = w["status"].as_str().unwrap_or("no status");
783	    let (note, code) = match w["reason"].as_str() {
784	        Some("timeout") => (Some(format!("still running as {t}: hc wait {t}, hc read {t}")), 124),
785	        Some("exit") => match (w["exit_code"].as_i64(), w["signal"].as_i64()) {
786	            (Some(0), _) => (None, 0),
787	            (Some(c), _) => (Some(format!("{t} exited (exit {c})")), c as i32),
788	            (_, Some(sig)) => (Some(format!("{t} ended by signal {sig}")), 128 + sig as i32),
789	            _ => (Some(format!("{t} ended")), 1),
790	        },
791	        _ if status == "blocked" => (Some(format!("{t} is blocked: read it, then answer with hc send or hc keys")), 0),
792	        _ => (Some(format!("{t} is {status}: hc send {t} <text>")), 0),
793	    };

````text
1	# Script design for agent skills
2	
3	Condensed from <https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/using-scripts>. Read this
4	before adding anything to `scripts/` in a skill.
5	
6	The headline difference from "regular" CLI design: **the caller is an LLM that
7	reads your stderr to decide what to do next.** Optimize for that.
8	
9	## Table of contents
10	
11	1. [One-off commands vs bundled scripts](#one-off-commands-vs-bundled-scripts)
12	2. [Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx`](#pin-versions)
13	3. [Self-contained scripts (PEP 723 etc.)](#self-contained-scripts)
14	4. [Agentic CLI design rules](#agentic-cli-design-rules)
15	5. [Error message style](#error-message-style)
16	6. [Structured output](#structured-output)
17	7. [Idempotency, dry-run, exit codes](#idempotency-dry-run-exit-codes)
18	8. [Bash 3.2 compatibility (macOS)](#bash-32-compatibility-macos)
19	9. [Quick script checklist](#quick-script-checklist)
20	
21	---
22	
23	## One-off commands vs bundled scripts
24	
25	If a published tool already does the job and the invocation is short, **don't
26	bundle a script** — reference the tool directly:
27	
28	```bash
29	uvx ruff@0.8.0 check .
30	npx eslint@9.0.0 --fix .
31	```
32	
33	Bundle a script when:
34	
35	- The invocation grows past ~3 flags or needs computed arguments.
36	- You need to compose multiple tools.
37	- The logic must be tested independently.
38	- You want to give the agent a stable interface even if the underlying tool
39	  changes.
40	
41	State runtime prerequisites in `SKILL.md` ("Requires Node 18+", "Requires
42	`uv`"). Don't assume the agent's environment.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## Pin versions
47	
48	Unpinned `uvx`, `npx`, `pipx` invocations behave inconsistently as upstreams
49	release new versions. Always pin:
50	
51	```bash
52	# Good
53	uvx ruff@0.8.0 check .
54	npx eslint@9.0.0 --fix .
55	pipx run 'black==24.10.0' .
56	
57	# Bad — silently breaks when upstream ships a breaking change
58	uvx ruff check .
59	npx eslint --fix .
60	```
61	
62	`@latest` is fine **if** the skill explicitly says "tracks upstream latest" and
63	the user understands that.
64	
65	---
66	
67	## Self-contained scripts
68	
69	When a script needs dependencies, prefer **inline declarations** over a
70	sibling `requirements.txt` / `package.json`. The agent can run the script with
71	one command and no setup.
72	
73	### Python — PEP 723
74	
75	```python
76	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
77	# /// script
78	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
79	# dependencies = [
80	#   "beautifulsoup4>=4.12,<5",
81	# ]
82	# ///
83	"""Extract <p class="info"> from an HTML file."""
84	import sys
85	from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
86	
87	with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
88	    html = f.read()
89	print(BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser").select_one("p.info").get_text())
90	```
91	
92	Run with `uv run scripts/extract.py file.html`. `uv` creates an isolated
93	environment, installs declared deps, and runs — every time, deterministically.
94	
95	For full reproducibility, `uv lock --script scripts/extract.py` produces
96	`scripts/extract.py.lock`.
97	
98	### Deno
99	
100	```typescript
101	#!/usr/bin/env -S deno run
102	import * as cheerio from "npm:cheerio@1.0.0";
103	// ...
104	```

107	
108	```typescript

110	import * as cheerio from "cheerio@1.0.0";
111	// ...
112	```

114	If a `node_modules/` exists anywhere up the tree, Bun's auto-install is

128	---
129	
130	## Agentic CLI design rules
131	
132	### No interactive prompts, ever
133	
134	Agents run in non-interactive shells. A script that calls `read`, `input()`,
135	or any TTY prompt **hangs indefinitely**. There is no recovery.
136	
137	```
138	# Bad
139	$ python scripts/deploy.py
140	Target environment: _
141	
142	# Good
143	$ python scripts/deploy.py
144	Error: --env is required. Options: development, staging, production.
145	Usage: python scripts/deploy.py --env staging --tag v1.2.3
146	```
147	
148	Accept all input via flags, env vars, or stdin (non-blocking — check `isatty`).
149	
150	### `--help` is the primary documentation
151	
152	The agent reads `--help` to learn the script. Make it concise but complete:
153	
154	```
155	Usage: scripts/process.py [OPTIONS] INPUT_FILE
156	
157	Process input data and produce a summary report.
158	
159	Options:
160	  --format FORMAT    Output format: json, csv, table (default: json)
161	  --output FILE      Write output to FILE instead of stdout
162	  --verbose          Print progress to stderr
163	  --dry-run          Show what would happen without doing it
164	
165	Examples:
166	  scripts/process.py data.csv
167	  scripts/process.py --format csv --output report.csv data.csv
168	
169	Exit codes:
170	  0  success
171	  1  invalid arguments
172	  2  input file not found
173	  3  processing failed
174	```
175	
176	The exit-codes block matters — the agent uses them to branch retry behavior.
177

````text
1	---
2	name: pueue-job-queue
3	description: Drive Nukesor/pueue (https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue) for queued, parallel, scheduled, and lightly-DAG'd shell jobs — wraps `pueue add --after`, `pueue status --json`, `pueue log --json`, group-level parallelism, and `pueued` daemon health. Use when the user wants to background long-running shell commands across reboots, queue dozens of jobs with capped parallelism, run a fan-out / fan-in pipeline of shell steps, says "pueue", "pueued", "pueue add", "pueue queue", "pueue group", "task queue for shell", "background this job", or asks how to schedule/parallelize CLI work without a real orchestrator (Airflow/Prefect/Dagster). Good fit for ML sweeps, long-running data pipelines, batched evaluations, scheduled `--delay` jobs, "wait for X then run Y" sequences.
4	---
5	
6	# pueue job queue
7	
8	Pueue is a daemon-backed shell job queue. The daemon (`pueued`) accepts tasks
9	via the `pueue` CLI, runs them across parallelism-capped **groups**, persists
10	state across reboots, and exposes status / logs as JSON. This skill teaches
11	the agent to drive pueue end-to-end: submit single tasks or whole DAGs, cap
12	parallelism per group, block until completion, retrieve logs, and retry.
13	
14	The skill is a **CLI bridge**, not a scheduler. Pueue's `--after` is **AND-only**
15	and **success-only** — that maps cleanly to declarative DAGs and not much
16	beyond. For OR-deps, conditional branching, retry-with-backoff, or distributed
17	scheduling, escalate to a real orchestrator (see "When NOT to use").
18	
19	## When to use
20	
21	- "Run these 30 commands, max 4 at a time" → `pueue group add ml && pueue parallel 4 --group ml` then loop `submit.sh --group ml`.
22	- "Kick off a long training job and let me close my laptop" → `submit.sh -- ./train.sh` (pueue persists across reboots).
23	- "Run task B only after task A finishes successfully" → `submit.sh --after $A_ID -- ./b.sh`.
24	- "Fan out 4 trainings, then evaluate" → `submit-dag.py dag.yaml`.
25	- "Schedule this for tonight" → `submit.sh --delay 6h -- ./nightly.sh`.
26	- "Block until task 17 is done, then tell me what happened" → `wait.py --ids 17`.
27	- The user mentions pueue, pueued, the pueue CLI, or asks about a "task queue for shell jobs".
28	
29	## When NOT to use
30	
31	- **One short shell command** the user wants to run right now. Just run it. Pueue adds daemon overhead for nothing.
32	- **Cross-host *scheduling*** (jobs distributed across N machines) → Airflow / Dagster / Prefect / Slurm. Note this is not the same as driving a *single* remote daemon, which pueue does support — see `references/remote-daemon.md`.
33	- **Conditional / OR / retry-with-backoff dependencies** → real orchestrator. Pueue's `--after` is AND-only and success-only.
34	- **Typed task IO and artifact tracking** (data lineage, cached intermediate outputs) → DVC (`dvc exp run --queue`), Prefect, Airflow.
35	- **Long-running services** (web servers, daemons) → systemd, launchd, supervisord. Pueue is for finite tasks.
36	
37	## Authoritative sources
38	
39	- Repo: https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue
40	- Wiki: https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki
41	- `pueue --help`, `pueue <subcommand> --help`, `man pueue`
42	
43	## Mental model
44	
45	| Concept | What it is | How to interact |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| **Daemon** (`pueued`) | Long-running process holding queue state. Required. | `pueued -d` to start. `pueue shutdown` to stop. |
48	| **Task** | One shell command, identified by integer id. | `pueue add ...`, `pueue status`, `pueue kill`, `pueue remove`. |
49	| **Group** | Named queue with its own parallelism limit. `default` always exists. | `pueue group add <name>`, `pueue parallel N --group <name>`. |
50	| **Dependency** | Task waits for one or more parents to **succeed** before running. | `pueue add --after <id> --after <id> -- <cmd>`. AND-only, success-only. |
51	| **Status** | Tagged enum: `Queued`, `Running`, `Stashed`, `Paused`, `Locked`, `Done`. `Done` carries a `result` (`Success`, `Killed`, `DependencyFailed`, or `{"Failed": <exit_code>}`). | `pueue status --json`. |
52	
53	## Setup quickstart
54	
55	```bash
56	# 1. Verify daemon is healthy. Auto-start if missing.
57	bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/check-daemon.sh --start --json | jq
58	
59	# 2. (Optional) Create a group with 4 parallel slots.
60	pueue group add ml
61	pueue parallel 4 --group ml
62	```
63	
64	For per-OS daemon paths and launchd/systemd setup, read
65	`references/daemon-and-config.md`.
66	
67	## Always pass a label
68	
69	`pueue status` shows the **label** column before the command. In a busy
70	queue, scanning labels is the only way to tell `train.py` runs apart at a
71	glance. **Always pass `--label`** when submitting, and bias toward names
72	that distinguish *this* task from its siblings.
73	
74	Convention:
75	
76	- Shape: `<verb>-<subject>-<key>` (≤30 chars). `verb` = action,
77	  `subject` = artifact, `key` = the variable that distinguishes this run.
78	- Encode the discriminator: seed, dataset slice, model variant, date, host.
79	- Don't restate the command — `train.py --seed 1` becomes label
80	  `train-baseline-seed1`, not `python-train-py-seed-1`.
81	- For DAGs, `submit-dag.py --label-prefix <run>-` makes every task labeled
82	  `<run>-<task_name>` so `wait.py --label-prefix <run>-` selects the whole
83	  graph and `pueue clean` can be filtered later.
84	
85	| Good | Bad |
86	|---|---|
87	| `train-baseline-seed1` | `task1` (no metadata) |
88	| `eval-prod-2026q1` | `python eval.py --quarter 2026q1` (restates cmd) |
89	| `fetch-prices-AAPL` | `fetch-data` (multiple identical labels) |
90	| `nightly-featurize` (DAG) | `step-2-of-5` (rename a step → label rots) |
91	
92	## Workflow A — submit one task
93	
94	```bash
95	bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit.sh \
96	  --label train-baseline --group ml \
97	  -- python train.py --seed 1
98	# stdout: {"task_id":17,"label":"train-baseline","group":"ml","after":[],...}
99	# stderr: submitted task 17 (group=ml, label=train-baseline)
100	```
101	
102	Capture the id with `jq -r .task_id`. The script wraps `pueue add
103	--print-task-id` and falls back to a status-by-label lookup if the id parse
104	fails (defensive against future format changes).
105	
106	## Workflow B — batched runs with capped parallelism
107	
108	```bash
109	# One-time: create + size the group
110	pueue group add sweep
111	pueue parallel 4 --group sweep
112	
113	# Loop: submit 30 tasks; pueue runs at most 4 at a time
114	for SEED in $(seq 1 30); do
115	  bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit.sh \
116	    --label "sweep-$SEED" --group sweep \
117	    -- python train.py --seed "$SEED"
118	done
119	
120	# Block until all sweep-* tasks are done
121	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py \
122	  --label-prefix sweep- --group sweep
123	```
124	
125	Group parallelism is the parallelism primitive in pueue — there is no
126	per-task pool. Set it once, submit freely.
127	
128	## Workflow C — fan-out / fan-in DAG
129	
130	For multi-task pipelines with success-only dependencies, write a YAML spec
131	and submit it declaratively. **Prefer `--isolated-group`** — it creates a
132	fresh group sized to the DAG's fan-out width and leaves your other groups
133	(especially `default`) untouched:
134	
135	```bash
136	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit-dag.py \
137	  skills/local/pueue-job-queue/assets/dag.example.yaml \
138	  --label-prefix nightly- --isolated-group
139	# stderr: isolated-group: created 'dag-dcda9347' with parallel_tasks=2
140	# stdout: {"tasks":{"fetch":17,...},
141	#          "topo_order":[...],
142	#          "width_per_group":{"dag-dcda9347":2},
143	#          "isolated_group":"dag-dcda9347"}
144	```
145	
146	Each task gets the label `<--label-prefix><task_name>` so you can
147	`wait.py --label-prefix nightly-` later. After the run, clean up with
148	`pueue group remove <name>` (or run `cleanup.sh --remove-empty-groups`).
149	
150	The submitter topo-sorts, validates the graph (cycle detection, unknown
151	references, missing `cmd:`), computes the **DAG width per group** (the
152	minimum `parallel_tasks` needed for fan-out to actually run in parallel),
153	then submits in order — wiring `--after` from the in-flight name→id map.
154	**No partial submits**: validation fails loud before any `pueue add` runs.
155	
156	Three parallelism modes, in order of recommendation:
157	
158	1. **`--isolated-group [NAME]`** (recommended). Fresh group, sized to width,
159	   no side effects on other groups. NAME auto-generates from spec hash if
160	   omitted. Mutually exclusive with `--default-group`.
161	2. **`--auto-parallel`**. Mutates `pueue parallel` on the target group in
162	   place. Use this when the DAG is meant to live in a long-lived shared
163	   group (e.g. `ml`) and that group's parallelism should permanently grow.
164	3. **No flag**. Only warns (in stderr + JSON's `parallelism_warnings`).
165	   Useful in `--dry-run` planning.
166	
167	See `assets/dag.example.yaml` for a 5-task fan-out/fan-in template and
168	`references/dag-patterns.md` for more shapes.
169	
170	## Workflow D — block until tasks reach terminal state
171	
172	```bash
173	# Wait for specific ids
174	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py --ids 17,18,19 --timeout-seconds 300
175	
176	# Wait for everything in a group
177	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py --group ml
178	
179	# Wait for a label prefix (e.g. all tasks the DAG submitter created)
180	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py --label-prefix nightly-
181	```
182	
183	Output is a JSON summary on stdout:
184	
185	```json
186	{"summary": {"total": 4, "success": 3, "failed": 1, "killed": 0, "dependency_failed": 0},
187	 "tasks": [{"id": 17, "status": "Done", "result": "Success", "exit_code": 0,
188	            "label": "nightly-fetch", "group": "ml",
189	            "start": "...", "end": "..."}],
190	 "elapsed_seconds": 42.3}
191	```
192	
193	Exit codes: `0` all succeeded, `5` ≥1 task failed/killed/dependency-failed,
194	`6` timeout. The agent can branch on exit code instead of parsing JSON.
195	
196	## Workflow E — logs, retry, kill
197	
198	One-line `pueue` calls (full list in `references/cli-cheatsheet.md`):
199	
200	```bash
201	pueue log --json --full 17        # full stdout/stderr as JSON
202	pueue restart --in-place 17       # retry in-place (overwrites old log)
203	pueue kill 17 && pueue remove 17  # kill + drop from queue
204	```
205	
206	For ad-hoc filtering, prefer pueue's built-in QUERY DSL over piping
207	through `jq` — it's faster (server-side filter) and shorter:
208	
209	```bash
210	pueue status --json 'status=Failed order_by end desc first 10'
211	pueue status --json 'label %= sweep-'   # substring match
212	```
213	
214	See `references/json-schema.md` for the QUERY grammar + jq fallbacks.
215	
216	## Workflow F — periodic cleanup
217	
218	Pueue's task list grows unbounded. `pueue status --json` walks the whole
219	table, so a queue with thousands of completed tasks slows down everything
220	that touches status. Run `cleanup.sh` weekly:
221	
222	```bash
223	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/cleanup.sh \
224	  --successful-only --remove-empty-groups --logs-older-than 30
225	# stdout: {"cleaned_tasks":[...], "removed_groups":["dag-abc12345"],
226	#          "deleted_logs":[...], "kept_running":[...], ...}
227	```
228	
229	`--successful-only` keeps failures around for inspection; drop the flag
230	for a full sweep. Pair with the agent's existing weekly maintenance habit
231	(or `/schedule` an agent to run it).
232	
233	## Available scripts
234	
235	- **`scripts/check-daemon.sh`** — Single-shot daemon health + version + log-dir check, with optional auto-start. Outputs JSON to stdout.
236	  - Flags: `--start`, `--json` (default on), `--help`.
237	  - Exit: `0` healthy, `2` pueue not installed, `3` daemon unreachable, `4` client/daemon version mismatch.
238	- **`scripts/submit.sh`** — Submit ONE task, return clean JSON `{task_id, group, label, after, ...}`. Wraps `pueue add --print-task-id` with defensive id parsing. Auto-creates the group if missing.
239	  - Flags: `--label`, `--group`, `--after` (repeatable), `--immediate`, `--stashed`, `--delay`, `--priority`, `--working-dir`, `--escape`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
240	  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` pueue not installed, `3` `pueue add` failed, `4` daemon unreachable.
241	- **`scripts/wait.py`** — Block until selected tasks reach terminal status; emit a JSON summary. Selectors: `--ids`, `--label`, `--label-prefix`, `--group`. Quiet by default — emits only one initial line + state-change events on stderr; pass `--verbose` for per-tick output.
242	  - Flags: `--ids`, `--label` (repeatable), `--label-prefix`, `--group`, `--poll-seconds`, `--timeout-seconds`, `--fail-fast`, `--verbose`, `--help`.
243	  - Exit: `0` all succeeded, `1` arg error, `4` daemon unreachable, `5` ≥1 failed/killed/dependency-failed, `6` timeout.
244	- **`scripts/submit-dag.py`** — Declarative DAG submitter. Reads YAML or JSON (file path or `-` for stdin), topo-sorts, validates, submits with wired `--after`, returns `{name → id, topo_order, width_per_group, isolated_group?}`. Computes DAG fan-out width per group; with `--isolated-group [NAME]` creates a fresh dedicated group sized to the width (preferred — leaves user's other groups untouched). With `--auto-parallel` mutates target groups in place. Without either, only warns.
245	  - Flags: `--format`, `--default-group`, `--label-prefix`, `--dry-run`, `--print-graph`, `--auto-parallel`, `--isolated-group [NAME]`, `--help`.
246	  - Exit: `0` all submitted, `1` schema/cycle/unknown-ref/conflicting flags, `2` pueue not installed, `3` mid-run pueue failure (stdout still emits IDs that DID submit, for cleanup).
247	- **`scripts/cleanup.sh`** — Prune pueue task history, empty groups, and old log files. Wraps `pueue clean` + `pueue group remove` for empty non-default groups + optional log-file mtime pruning. Emits a JSON report. Run weekly to keep `pueue status --json` fast.
248	  - Flags: `--successful-only`, `--group GROUP`, `--remove-empty-groups`, `--logs-older-than N`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
249	  - Exit: `0` ok (or dry-run), `1` bad args, `2` pueue not installed, `3` daemon unreachable.

Short version: `ssh host 'pueue add ...'` to submit; a forwarded client to read/control.

264	## See also
265	
266	- `long-running-jobs` — pueue is one *implementation* of "let the queue own the
267	  chain" (`--after`) and "block once" (`wait.py`). That skill owns the prior
268	  question: **which** of those an agent should reach for, when a scheduled
269	  check-in is ever justified, and how to record completion durably so a run
270	  survives losing the session. Read it if you are tempted to poll
271	  `pueue status` on a timer.

273	
274	## Gotchas
275	
276	- **DAG fan-out is gated by `parallel_tasks` per group.** Even when two siblings both depend only on `A` and the DAG allows them to run in parallel, they will *serialize* if their group's `parallel_tasks=1`. Pueue's parallelism primitive is the group, not the dependency graph. `submit-dag.py` warns when DAG width exceeds the group's slots and suggests the exact `pueue parallel N --group G` command; pass `--auto-parallel` to apply it.
277	- **`pueue add -- bash -c 'sleep 60'` does not preserve quoting.** Pueue joins all `<COMMAND>` args and re-shells. The single-quoted `'sleep 60'` is unwrapped by *your* shell before pueue sees it, then pueue re-splits. Quote the **whole** command as one arg: `pueue add 'sleep 60'` or `submit.sh -- 'bash -c "sleep 60 && echo done"'`.
278	- **`--after` is AND-only and success-only.** Failed parent → dependent's `status.Done.result` becomes `"DependencyFailed"` and it never runs. There is no OR, no run-on-failure, no retry-on-failure. If you need that, you need a real orchestrator.
279	- **Pueue does NOT auto-create groups.** `pueue add --group new_name` exits 1 with `"Group new_name doesn't exists. Use one of these: [...]"`. `submit.sh` calls `pueue group add` first if the group is missing.
280	- **`pueue restart` (default) creates a NEW task id.** The old id stays in history with its result. To retry in-place (reusing the id, overwriting the log), pass `--in-place`. Choose deliberately — agent users often want `--in-place` for "retry this".
281	- **`pause_group_on_failure` is config-only, no CLI flag.** Set it in `pueue.yml`; reload with `pueue reset` or restart `pueued`.
282	- **Logs live in platform-specific dirs**, not your CWD. macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/pueue/logs/`. Linux: `~/.local/share/pueue/logs/`. Windows: `%APPDATA%\pueue\logs\`. `pueue log --json --full <id>` reads them for you.
283	- **`pueue wait` returns 0 even if the waited-on tasks failed.** It blocks until terminal, period. To know success/failure, query `pueue status --json` afterward (or use `wait.py`, which does this for you and returns a non-zero exit on failures).
284	- **`pueue remove` requires each id as a separate positional arg** (not a space-joined string from a subshell). Use bash arrays: `IDS=($(...)) && pueue remove "${IDS[@]}"`.
285	- **`pueue clean --successful-only` is a flag, not the default.** Plain `pueue clean` removes ALL finished tasks (including failures, which you may want to keep for debugging). Be deliberate.
286	- **`pueue add --print-task-id` writes the bare integer to stdout.** No JSON, no prose. `submit.sh` parses with a regex that tolerates future format changes; if you bypass `submit.sh`, capture with `ID=$(pueue add --print-task-id ... )` directly.
287	- **A terminal result that isn't `Success` is a failure — don't enumerate the bad ones.** `result` is a tagged enum, and `{"FailedToSpawn": "<os error>"}` is dict-shaped, not the bare string older notes implied. Matching a known-bad list let it fall through as success, so `wait.py` returned `0` for a task that never started. It now allowlists `Success` and fails closed on anything else.
288	- **Driving a remote daemon: the working directory is resolved on the CLIENT.** `pueue add` records and canonicalizes the cwd locally, so submitting to a remote daemon fails three different ways — local cwd sent (task ends `FailedToSpawn`), remote-only path rejected outright (`Failed to canonicalize given working directory path`), or a macOS symlink silently rewritten (`/tmp` → `/private/tmp`). Use `ssh host 'pueue add ...'` to submit; a forwarded client is for reading and control. See `references/remote-daemon.md`.
289
````

````text
1	# Tests for pueue-job-queue
2	
3	Run the full suite:
4	
5	```bash
6	# From repo root
7	uv run --extra dev pytest skills/local/pueue-job-queue/tests/ -q
8	bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/tests/test_contracts.sh
9	```
10	
11	The pytest suite spins up an **isolated** `pueued` under a tempdir-scoped
12	config — your real queue is never touched. Skipped entirely if `pueue` /
13	`pueued` aren't on `PATH`.
14	
15	## Layout
16	
17	- `conftest.py` — `pueue_env` session fixture starts an isolated daemon and
18	  yields an env dict. The `_clean_between_tests` autouse fixture wipes
19	  tasks between tests (kill + clean).
20	- `fixtures/simple-dag.yaml` — 4-task diamond used by `test_dag.py`.
21	- `test_submit.py` — `submit.sh` paths: minimal, `--after` chain, dependency
22	  failure propagation, group autocreate, dry-run, error paths.
23	- `test_dag.py` — `submit-dag.py` paths: dry-run validation, end-to-end submit
24	  + topo invariant check (each child's `start` ≥ parent's `end`), cycle
25	  detection, unknown `after`, missing `cmd`, stdin spec.
26	- `test_wait.py` — `wait.py` paths: success/failure/timeout exit codes
27	  (0/5/6), label-prefix selector, no-selector arg error.
28	- `test_contracts.sh` — bash exit-code contract: every script supports
29	  `--help` (exit 0); arg errors return 1; `check-daemon.sh` against an
30	  unreachable daemon returns 3.
31	
32	## Requirements
33	
34	- `uv` (for `uv run --extra dev pytest`).
35	- `pueue` and `pueued` on `PATH`. The whole suite is auto-skipped if either
36	  is missing.
37	- Tests use ports / sockets only under `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="pueue-test-")`;
38	  no host-wide config is touched.
39	
40	## Why these levels
41	
42	The skill manipulates a stateful daemon over a JSON-RPC-ish wire — three
43	regressions could happen silently and only the tests catch them:
44	
45	| Regression                                                        | Caught by |
46	|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
47	| `submit.sh` parses non-integer task id (e.g. JSON-wrapped output) | `test_submit.test_submit_minimal` |
48	| `--group X` doesn't autocreate, future pueue version regresses    | `test_submit.test_submit_autocreates_group` |
49	| `submit-dag.py` submits even on cycle / unknown `after`           | `test_dag.test_dag_cycle_detected`, `test_dag_unknown_after` |
50	| `wait.py` mis-classifies `{"Failed": N}` vs `"Failed"` string     | `test_wait.test_wait_failure_returns_5` |
51	| Status enum gains a new variant (e.g. Pueue 5.x)                  | `test_wait_*` start failing — re-verify schema |

159	}
160	
161	/// After `t` and a first digit 1-9, ids count in these 30: no vowels (no
162	/// words), no `l` (reads as 1).
163	const SYMBOLS: &[u8; 30] = b"0123456789bcdfghjkmnpqrstvwxyz";
164	
165	/// Counter `n` (from 1) as written: t1..t9, t10..t9z, t100..t9zz, ...
166	pub fn address(n: u32) -> String {
167	    let (mut rest, mut size, mut len) = (u64::from(n) - 1, 9u64, 0);
168	    while rest >= size {
169	        rest -= size;
170	        size *= 30;
171	        len += 1;
172	    }
173	    let mut tail = vec![0u8; len];
174	    for b in tail.iter_mut().rev() {
175	        *b = SYMBOLS[(rest % 30) as usize];
176	        rest /= 30;
177	    }
178	    format!("t{}{}", rest + 1, String::from_utf8(tail).expect("ascii"))
179	}
180	
181	/// Shaped like an id, whether or not the number fits: names may not be.
182	pub fn id_shaped(local: &str) -> bool {
183	    let Some(rest) = local.strip_prefix('t') else { return false };
184	    rest.starts_with(|c: char| matches!(c, '1'..='9')) && rest.bytes().all(|b| SYMBOLS.contains(&b))
185	}
186	
187	pub fn parse_id(local: &str) -> Option<u32> {
188	    if !id_shaped(local) {
189	        return None;
190	    }
191	    let mut symbols = local[1..].bytes().map(|b| SYMBOLS.iter().position(|&s| s == b).unwrap() as u64);
192	    let mut rest = symbols.next()? - 1;
193	    let (mut before, mut size) = (0u64, 9u64);
194	    for v in symbols {
195	        rest = rest.checked_mul(30)?.checked_add(v)?;
196	        before = before.checked_add(size)?;
197	        size = size.checked_mul(30)?;
198	    }
199	    u32::try_from(before.checked_add(rest)? + 1).ok()
200	}

1	//! The API only grows. `schema/released.openrpc.json` is the API as last
2	//! released; the code's must accept every request that one accepted and
3	//! give every answer field that one gave. Refreshed at each release.
4	
5	use serde_json::{Value, json};
6	use std::collections::BTreeSet;
7	
8	fn resolve<'a>(doc: &'a Value, s: &'a Value) -> &'a Value {
9	    match s["$ref"].as_str().and_then(|r| r.strip_prefix("#/components/schemas/")) {
10	        Some(name) => resolve(doc, &doc["components"]["schemas"][name]),
11	        None => s,
12	    }
13	}
14	
15	/// Its kinds of value (`string`, `null`, ...) and the object schemas among them.
16	fn shape<'a>(doc: &'a Value, s: &'a Value) -> (BTreeSet<String>, Vec<&'a Value>) {
17	    let s = resolve(doc, s);
18	    let mut kinds = BTreeSet::new();
19	    let mut objects = Vec::new();
20	    match &s["type"] {
21	        Value::String(t) => drop(kinds.insert(t.clone())),
22	        Value::Array(ts) => kinds.extend(ts.iter().filter_map(|t| t.as_str().map(String::from))),
23	        _ => {}
24	    }
25	    if s.get("properties").is_some() || s.get("items").is_some() || s.get("enum").is_some() {
26	        objects.push(s);
27	    }
28	    for member in s["anyOf"].as_array().into_iter().chain(s["oneOf"].as_array()).flatten() {
29	        let (k, o) = shape(doc, member);
30	        kinds.extend(k);
31	        objects.extend(o);
32	    }
33	    (kinds, objects)
34	}
35	
36	fn names(v: &Value) -> BTreeSet<String> {
37	    v.as_array().into_iter().flatten().filter_map(|x| x.as_str().map(String::from)).collect()
38	}
39	
40	fn props(s: &Value) -> Vec<(&String, &Value)> {
41	    s["properties"].as_object().into_iter().flatten().collect()
42	}
43	
44	/// `input`: the new side must accept all the old did. Else (output) the new
45	/// side must give all the old gave, nothing the old couldn't.
46	fn compare(old: (&Value, &Value), new: (&Value, &Value), input: bool, at: &str, depth: u8, out: &mut Vec<String>) {
47	    if depth > 8 {
48	        return;
49	    }
50	    let (ok, oo) = shape(old.0, old.1);
51	    let (nk, no) = shape(new.0, new.1);
52	    let (wider, narrower) = if input { (&nk, &ok) } else { (&ok, &nk) };
53	    if !wider.is_empty() && !narrower.is_subset(wider) {
54	        out.push(format!("{at}: type {ok:?} became {nk:?}"));
55	    }
56	    // An answer that promised a shape keeps promising it (untyped is wider).
57	    if !input && ((!ok.is_empty() && nk.is_empty()) || (!oo.is_empty() && no.is_empty())) {
58	        out.push(format!("{at}: lost its type"));
59	    }
60	    let (Some(o), Some(n)) = (oo.first(), no.first()) else { return };
61	    let (oe, ne) = (names(&o["enum"]), names(&n["enum"]));
62	    if !oe.is_empty() && (if input { !oe.is_subset(&ne) } else { !ne.is_subset(&oe) }) {
63	        out.push(format!("{at}: values {oe:?} became {ne:?}"));
64	    }
65	    if o.get("items").is_some() {
66	        compare((old.0, &o["items"]), (new.0, &n["items"]), input, &format!("{at}[]"), depth + 1, out);
67	    }
68	    let (oreq, nreq) = (names(&o["required"]), names(&n["required"]));
69	    for (k, os) in props(o) {
70	        let path = format!("{at}.{k}");
71	        match n["properties"].get(k) {
72	            None => out.push(format!("{path}: removed")),
73	            Some(ns) => compare((old.0, os), (new.0, ns), input, &path, depth + 1, out),
74	        }
75	        if !input && oreq.contains(k) && !nreq.contains(k) {
76	            out.push(format!("{path}: may be missing now"));
77	        }
78	    }
79	    if input {
80	        for k in nreq.difference(&oreq) {
81	            out.push(format!("{at}.{k}: newly required"));
82	        }
83	    }
84	}
85	
86	fn breaks(old: &Value, new: &Value) -> Vec<String> {

88	    let methods = |doc: &Value| doc["methods"].as_array().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
89	    let new_methods = methods(new);
