1	//! Status facts from OSC 7501, kept per terminal exactly as reported.
2	//! A report replaces its record; `clear` removes a record and its children.
3	//! The turn goes up each time the root record leaves `working`, for any reason.
4	
5	use crate::terminals::Terminal;
6	use ghostty_vt::StatusReport;
7	use schemars::JsonSchema;
8	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
9	
10	const MAX_RECORDS: usize = 256;
11	
12	/// One 7501 record. Words are the program's own; nothing is translated.
13	#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
14	pub struct Status {
15	    /// idle, working, done, blocked or error.
16	    pub state: String,
17	    /// permission, question or auth (blocked only, when the program said).
18	    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
19	    pub kind: Option<String>,
20	    /// 0..100 (working or blocked, when the program said).
21	    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
22	    pub progress: Option<u8>,
23	    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty", default)]
24	    pub app: String,
25	    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty", default)]
26	    pub title: String,
27	    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty", default)]
28	    pub msg: String,
29	}
30	
31	impl Status {
32	    fn from(r: &StatusReport) -> Status {
33	        Status {
34	            state: r.state.into(),
35	            kind: r.kind.map(Into::into),
36	            progress: r.progress,
37	            app: r.app.clone(),
38	            title: r.title.clone(),
39	            msg: r.message.clone(),
40	        }
41	    }
42	
43	    /// The report again as OSC 7501, for a new viewer's first paint.
44	    pub fn encode(&self, id: &str) -> String {
45	        let mut fields = vec![format!("state={}", self.state)];
46	        let mut push = |key: &str, value: &str| {
47	            if !value.is_empty() {
48	                fields.push(format!("{key}={value}"));
49	            }
50	        };
51	        push("id", id);
52	        push("kind", self.kind.as_deref().unwrap_or(""));
53	        push("progress", &self.progress.map(|p| p.to_string()).unwrap_or_default());
54	        push("app", &self.app);
55	        push("title", &base64(self.title.as_bytes()));
56	        push("msg", &base64(self.msg.as_bytes()));
57	        format!("\x1b]7501;{}\x1b\\", fields.join(":"))
58	    }
59	}
60	
61	/// What a report changed, for events and waiters.
62	#[derive(Default, Debug, PartialEq)]
63	pub struct Change {
64	    pub status: bool,
65	    pub turn_ended: bool,
66	    /// It just got stuck: blocked on the user or errored (wasn't that before).
67	    pub stuck: bool,
68	}
69	
70	fn working(t: &Terminal) -> bool {
71	    t.status.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| s.state == "working")
72	}
73	
74	fn end_turn(t: &mut Terminal, was_working: bool) -> bool {
75	    let ended = was_working && !working(t);
76	    if ended {
77	        t.turn += 1;
78	    }
79	    ended
80	}
81	
82	fn stuck(t: &Terminal) -> Option<&str> {
83	    t.status.as_ref().map(|s| s.state.as_str()).filter(|w| *w == "blocked" || *w == "error")
84	}
85	
86	fn word(t: &Terminal) -> Option<String> {
87	    t.status.as_ref().map(|s| s.state.clone())
88	}
89	
90	fn stamp(t: &mut Terminal, was: Option<String>) {
91	    if word(t) != was {
92	        t.status_ms = Some(crate::runtime::now_ms());
93	    }
94	}
95	
96	pub fn apply(t: &mut Terminal, r: &StatusReport) -> Change {
97	    let (was_working, was_word) = (working(t), word(t));
98	    let was = stuck(t).map(String::from);
99	    t.reported = true;
100	    if r.state == "clear" {
101	        if r.id.is_empty() {
102	            t.status = None;
103	            t.records.clear();
104	        } else {
105	            let child = format!("{}/", r.id);
106	            t.records.retain(|id, _| *id != r.id && !id.starts_with(&child));
107	        }
108	    } else if r.id.is_empty() {
109	        t.status = Some(Status::from(r));
110	    } else {
111	        // Over the limit, the record updated longest ago goes (approximated by first id).
112	        if !t.records.contains_key(&r.id) && t.records.len() >= MAX_RECORDS - 1 {
113	            let oldest = t.records.keys().next().cloned().expect("non-empty");
114	            t.records.remove(&oldest);
115	        }
116	        t.records.insert(r.id.clone(), Status::from(r));
117	    }
118	    stamp(t, was_word);
119	    Change {
120	        status: true,
121	        turn_ended: end_turn(t, was_working),
122	        stuck: stuck(t).is_some() && stuck(t) != was.as_deref(),
123	    }
124	}
125	
126	/// The program ended: its status facts reset.
127	pub fn reset(t: &mut Terminal) -> Change {
128	    let (was_working, was_word) = (working(t), word(t));
129	    let had = t.status.is_some() || !t.records.is_empty();
130	    t.status = None;
131	    t.records.clear();
132	    stamp(t, was_word);
133	    Change { status: had, turn_ended: end_turn(t, was_working), stuck: false }
134	}
135	
136	fn base64(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
137	    const TABLE: &[u8] = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/";
138	    let mut out = String::new();
139	    for chunk in bytes.chunks(3) {
140	        let n = chunk.iter().enumerate().fold(0u32, |n, (i, b)| n | (*b as u32) << (16 - 8 * i));
141	        for i in 0..4 {
142	            out.push(if i <= chunk.len() { TABLE[(n >> (18 - 6 * i) & 63) as usize] as char } else { '=' });
143	        }
144	    }
145	    out
146	}

# Herdr

Herdr organizes terminals into workspaces, tabs, and panes, recognizes coding agents running inside panes, and exposes the current session through the `herdr` CLI.

Before issuing any control command, verify that this agent is running inside a Herdr-managed pane:

```bash
test "${HERDR_ENV:-}" = 1
```

If the check fails, say that you are not running inside Herdr and stop. Do not inspect or control the focused Herdr session from outside Herdr.

When the check passes, the `herdr` binary in `PATH` talks to the current session. Use it to inspect neighboring work, create terminal layout, start agents and commands, read output, and wait for state changes.

## Learn the current CLI

The installed binary is the authority for command syntax. Start with:

```bash
herdr --help
```

Then print the relevant command group by running the group without a subcommand:

```bash
herdr agent
herdr pane
herdr workspace
herdr tab
herdr worktree
herdr terminal
herdr notification
herdr integration
herdr session
herdr machine
```

Do not run bare `herdr` for discovery; it launches or attaches the TUI. Do not probe a mutating nested command by omitting arguments. Commands such as `herdr workspace create` are valid with defaults and will execute.

Most control commands return JSON. Read identifiers and state from those responses instead of predicting them.

## Understand layout, panes, and agents

Choose the primitive that matches the job:

- Workspace, tab, and pane topology organize terminal locations.
- Pane commands control raw terminals, shells, tests, servers, input, and output.
- Agent commands control the recognized coding agent currently occupying a pane.

A pane exists whether or not it contains an agent. `agent start` requires an existing available shell pane and never creates, splits, or moves layout. Use pane commands for ordinary processes. Use agent commands when Herdr must validate agent identity or interpret `idle`, `working`, `blocked`, `done`, and `unknown` lifecycle states.

Agent commands accept either a unique live agent name or the pane ID currently hosting that agent. They do not accept terminal IDs or bare agent-kind labels. Names must match `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}` and be unique among live agents. A name follows the current pane occupant and is cleared when that agent exits, is released, or is replaced.

`idle` and `done` both mean the agent is ready for input. The CLI/API uses the server's seen state to distinguish them; explicit focus commands mark the target seen, while reads do not. Each TUI client tracks viewed completions independently, so its Done badge can differ from the CLI or another client's badge. `blocked` means Herdr recognized an approval or question UI. `unknown` means an agent is present but Herdr cannot classify it confidently; it does not prove completion.

## Use IDs and caller context

Public IDs are opaque stable handles:

- workspace: `w1`
- tab: `w1:t1`
- pane: `w1:p1`

Closed tab and pane IDs are not reused. A pane moved into another workspace receives a new workspace-qualified pane ID. After `pane move`, continue with `.result.move_result.pane.pane_id` or the live agent name. The old value is reported as `.result.move_result.previous_pane_id`; only the moved process's inherited caller context keeps resolving that old ID, so do not use it as a general agent target.

Herdr injects the caller's context into each managed pane:

```bash
printf '%s\n' "$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID" "$HERDR_TAB_ID" "$HERDR_PANE_ID"
```

Prefer `--current` when a pane command should target the calling pane. An omitted `pane split` target uses the calling pane when `HERDR_PANE_ID` is available, otherwise the focused pane. Other commands may use the UI-focused pane, which can belong to the user or another client.

Discover live state with:

```bash
herdr workspace list
herdr tab list --workspace "$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID"
herdr pane current --current
herdr pane list --workspace "$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID"
herdr agent list
```

Creation responses expose the IDs to use next. `workspace create` returns `.result.workspace`, `.result.tab`, and `.result.root_pane`. `tab create` returns `.result.tab` and `.result.root_pane`. `pane split` returns the new pane as `.result.pane`.

IDs and live agent names are scoped to one server. Two saved SSH machines can both have `w1:p1` or an agent named `reviewer`. Selecting a machine in the TUI does not retarget commands running in your pane: without `--machine`, they still use the inherited session and socket context.

To control a saved SSH machine, use the same global prefix for discovery and every later command:

```bash
herdr --machine <label-or-id> agent list
herdr --machine <label-or-id> pane list
herdr --machine <label-or-id> agent prompt <remote-agent-name> "Reply with your current status." --wait --timeout 120000
```

The selector must be an enabled saved profile ID or a unique, case-sensitive label, not an arbitrary SSH hostname. Commands use that profile's remote session without an open TUI. Do not combine `--machine` with `--session` or `--remote`. Discover IDs on that machine; inherited local IDs and `--current` do not identify remote panes.

Both installations must support machine API forwarding, and the remote server must already be running and API-compatible. Forwarding never installs, starts, or restarts a server and never falls back to Local. Local configuration, session management, installation commands, and interactive attachment are not forwarded. Remote worktree paths must be absolute, `~`, or start with `~/`; plugin link paths must be absolute. A connection failure does not prove a mutation was not applied: inspect remote state before retrying.

`herdr machine list` lists saved connection profiles, not a cross-machine pane inventory; add `--json` for scripts. Only add, remove, enable, or disable profiles when the user asks. Removing a profile disconnects the client but does not stop remote sessions. Adding a machine uses the remote default session unless `--remote-session` is explicitly supplied. Setup asks before stopping an incompatible server and defaults to No; do not approve replacement without the user's consent. Experimental handoff is not part of `machine add`.

## Start and coordinate an agent

Default to a sibling pane in the current tab and the current working directory. Do not create a workspace, tab, worktree, or different cwd unless the user explicitly requests that topology or location.

Honor a direction requested by the user. Otherwise inspect the caller pane:

```bash
herdr pane layout --pane "$HERDR_PANE_ID"
```

Split a wide pane to the right and a narrow or tall pane down. Avoid repeated same-direction splits that create unusably narrow columns or short rows. Keep the user's focus in the calling pane and explicitly preserve the caller's working directory:

```bash
herdr pane split --current --direction right --cwd "$PWD" --no-focus
```

Replace `right` with `down` when appropriate. Read the new pane ID from `.result.pane.pane_id`.

An available shell pane must be at its interactive prompt, with the shell itself in the foreground and no foreground command, editor, or agent running. Start a supported agent in that pane with a useful unique name:

```bash
herdr agent start reviewer --kind codex --pane <returned-pane-id>
```

Use the kind requested by the user. Run `herdr agent` to inspect the installed kind list and options. Pass native agent arguments only after `--`:

```bash
herdr agent start reviewer --kind codex --pane <returned-pane-id> -- <agent-args...>
```

A successful `agent start` returns only after Herdr detects the expected agent in the same pane and considers it ready for interactive input. If the agent is blocked during startup, the command returns `agent_not_ready` immediately but keeps the name available for `agent read` and `agent send-keys`. Wait until the agent becomes idle before prompting it. Startup defaults to a 30-second timeout.

Submit work through the agent surface:

```bash
herdr agent prompt reviewer "Review the current diff and report only actionable findings." --wait --timeout 120000
```

`agent prompt` honors the pane's live bracketed-paste mode and sends text followed by encoded Enter as one ordered submission. It reports successful submission only after both have been written; that alone does not prove the agent started a turn. For Codex on Windows, Herdr sends a paste boundary before Enter so submission does not depend on prompt size. It rejects an agent already waiting at an approval or question dialog with `agent_blocked` before sending any input. Inspect the blocked UI and ask the user before answering it. For normal agent work, `--wait` is enough: it waits for the first settled `idle`, `done`, or `blocked` state. Do not repeat those defaults with `--until`.

With `--wait`, a prompt sent from a non-working state must produce observed `working` or `blocked` activity. After submission, Herdr waits up to five seconds for that activity; unrelated `idle`, `done`, or session changes do not satisfy this gate. It returns `agent_prompt_stalled` if no activity is observed, or `timeout` if the caller's timeout expires first. The caller timeout includes submission time. Without a timeout, the settled-state wait is indefinite after activity is observed. This wait tracks lifecycle state, not an individual turn; if the agent is already working, completion of the active turn may satisfy it.

Use `--until` only for a state-specific workflow, such as waiting for an already-running agent to request input:

```bash
herdr agent wait reviewer --until blocked --timeout 120000
```

Without `--until`, standalone `agent wait` uses the same settled-state defaults as `agent prompt --wait`.

Use logical keys for interactive agent UI controls:

```bash
herdr agent send-keys reviewer esc
herdr agent send-keys reviewer ctrl+c
```

Herdr validates all keys before writing any bytes. Read the result through the resolved agent:

```bash
herdr agent get reviewer
herdr agent read reviewer --source recent-unwrapped --lines 120
```

If a wait fails or returns `blocked`, inspect `agent get` and `agent read` before deciding what input to send. A timeout or stalled response does not prove the prompt was never delivered; do not blindly submit it again. Use the pane surface only when raw terminal control is intentional.

## Run an ordinary command in another pane

Create a sibling pane with the same geometry rule, preserve the caller's working directory, and keep user focus unchanged:

```bash
herdr pane split --current --direction right --cwd "$PWD" --no-focus
```

Read the new pane ID from `.result.pane.pane_id`, then run and inspect the command:

```bash
herdr pane run <returned-pane-id> "just test"
herdr pane wait-output <returned-pane-id> --match "test result" --timeout 120000
herdr pane read <returned-pane-id> --source recent-unwrapped --lines 120
```

`pane run` atomically sends command text and Enter. `pane wait-output` searches the selected snapshot immediately, so output that already exists can match. Use `--match <text>` for a literal substring or `--regex <pattern>` for a Rust regular expression. Omitting `--timeout` allows an indefinite wait.

Use the read source that matches the task:

- `visible`: the currently rendered viewport.
- `recent`: recent rendered output, including soft wraps.
- `recent-unwrapped`: recent output with soft wraps joined; prefer it for logs and transcripts.
- `detection`: the plain-text bottom-buffer snapshot used for agent detection.

Use `--format ansi` when colors and terminal styling are evidence. Otherwise use text.

`--lines` asks Herdr for more rows from the pane's available screen and host scrollback. Alternate-screen rows do not enter ordinary host scrollback. For supported idle agents, Herdr can collect application-owned history and restore the viewport afterward, but not every application or response can be recovered this way.

If a larger recent read still does not reveal the completed response, ask the agent to write it as Markdown in a temporary directory and reply only with the file path, then read that file on the same machine. Use this only as a fallback; do not request file output in the initial prompt.

## Safety and coordination rules

- Use `--no-focus` for background work unless the user asked to switch context.
- Use `--current`, an explicit pane ID, or a unique agent name. Do not rely on another client's focused pane.
- Parse IDs from JSON responses. Do not derive them from sidebar order or examples.
- Do not close workspaces, tabs, panes, or sessions you did not create unless the user explicitly asked. `workspace close --group` closes the primary workspace and its linked worktree workspaces; never add it merely to bypass `workspace_group_close_required`.
- Use `--trust-repository` only after the user has verified the repository. It grants per-request Git trust; it is not a routine retry for a failed worktree command.
- Client and server versions can differ after an update. Check `herdr status` before relying on new server features. A missing method is not permission to stop or upgrade a server.
- Never run `herdr server stop` from an active session unless the user explicitly intends to stop the server and its pane processes.
- Never kill the main Herdr process. Use named test sessions for experiments that need an isolated server.
- CLI server errors are JSON on stderr with exit status 1. CLI syntax errors exit with status 2.

# Skill Author

Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
once a draft exists).

## When to use this vs `skill-creator`

| Task | Use |
|---|---|
| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |

If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.

## Workflow

### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)

Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:

1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)

Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.

### 2. Scaffold

Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
```

Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):

| Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
|---|---|---|
| **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
| **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
| **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |

The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.

> **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
> but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
> available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this
> project (`--project`)?" before running the script. The script is
> non-interactive — once you've picked a scope, files land and symlinks fan
> out without further prompting.

After running, the script emits a single JSON object on stdout with
`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}` so you can chain
follow-up actions deterministically.

### 3. Author the SKILL.md

Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
that matter most:

- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
  this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
  501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
  loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
  escape hatches.

Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
happens"), not just that it exists.

### 4. Design any scripts

Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
requirements:

- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations

For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
have to set up an environment first.

### 5. Lint

Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
```

It checks three things:

1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; name is
   hyphen-case and <=64 chars; description has a "use when" trigger phrase,
   respects the 1024-char hard limit, and SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
   script).
3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).

Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.

### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator

Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
skill runs test cases and benchmarks."

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold the canonical skill dir
  (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/) and add discovery symlinks for
  non-universal agents. Auto-detects scope (LOCAL / PROJECT / GLOBAL); see
  table in step 2.
  - Scope flags (mutually exclusive): `--local` (force this repo's
    `skills/local/`), `--project` (force `<repo>/.agents/skills/`),
    `--global` (force `~/.agents/skills/`).
  - Other flags: `--vendor` (LOCAL only — `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead of
    `skills/local/`; rare, vendored skills normally come via `vendor.yaml`);
    `--root DIR` (override walk-up); `--no-symlinks` (skip the fan-out);
    `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite existing canonical dir + replace
    symlinks).
- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).
- **`scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh [PATH...]`** — YAML-parse the frontmatter of
  every `SKILL.md` under PATH (default `.`) with a real parser, and check that
  the root is a mapping with string `name` + `description`. Catches the
  breakage class `lint-skill.sh`'s awk extractor cannot see — an unquoted
  `description:` containing `": "` makes `npx skills` (and Claude Code /
  Cursor) **silently skip the skill**. `lint-skill.sh` calls this for the
  single-skill case; run it directly to sweep a whole collection.
  - Flags: `--parser auto|yq|python3|node` (`node` = the js `yaml` package,
    exactly what `npx skills` uses); `--quiet`.

## Bundled assets

Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:

- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.

## Reference files

- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.

## Gotchas

- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
  symlink with a real file.
- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
- **`description` is always-on context and has agent-specific hard limits.**
  Put concrete trigger phrases in frontmatter, but keep local skills in the
  120-500 char preferred range when possible. Treat >1024 chars as invalid:
  Codex and Cursor/spec-aligned validators can skip the skill entirely.
- **Quote any `description` containing `:`, `#`, or leading punctuation.** An
  unquoted YAML plain scalar cannot contain `": "` — `npx skills` fails with
  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings" and drops the skill
  from the picker without a non-zero exit. ` #` is worse: it parses, but YAML
  treats the rest as a comment and silently truncates your trigger string.
  Single quotes need no escaping except `'` itself. Run
  `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` to catch both; see
  `pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md` in this repo.
- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
  investing in authoring.
- **Scope auto-detect can surprise you.** `new-skill.sh` walks up looking for
  a publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
  `skills/.claude-plugin/`) *first*, then a `.git`. If you ran it from inside
  a clone of this repo while meaning to add a skill to your *other* project,
  it'll silently land in `skills/local/`. Pass `--project` or `--global`
  explicitly when intent isn't obvious, and prefer asking the user
  system-wide-vs-project-wide before running.
- **Discovery symlinks must be `../../`-relative**, not repo-root-relative —
  POSIX resolves symlink targets relative to the link's own directory. The
  script enforces this and verifies each link with `test -e <link>/SKILL.md`;
  if you ever hand-create one, see
  [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md).

## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)

Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
quantitative validation.

 `./skills/local/pueue-job-queue/SKILL.md`

````text
1	---
2	name: pueue-job-queue
3	description: Drive Nukesor/pueue (https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue) for queued, parallel, scheduled, and lightly-DAG'd shell jobs — wraps `pueue add --after`, `pueue status --json`, `pueue log --json`, group-level parallelism, and `pueued` daemon health. Use when the user wants to background long-running shell commands across reboots, queue dozens of jobs with capped parallelism, run a fan-out / fan-in pipeline of shell steps, says "pueue", "pueued", "pueue add", "pueue queue", "pueue group", "task queue for shell", "background this job", or asks how to schedule/parallelize CLI work without a real orchestrator (Airflow/Prefect/Dagster). Good fit for ML sweeps, long-running data pipelines, batched evaluations, scheduled `--delay` jobs, "wait for X then run Y" sequences.
4	---
5	
6	# pueue job queue
7	
8	Pueue is a daemon-backed shell job queue. The daemon (`pueued`) accepts tasks
9	via the `pueue` CLI, runs them across parallelism-capped **groups**, persists
10	state across reboots, and exposes status / logs as JSON. This skill teaches
11	the agent to drive pueue end-to-end: submit single tasks or whole DAGs, cap
12	parallelism per group, block until completion, retrieve logs, and retry.
13	
14	The skill is a **CLI bridge**, not a scheduler. Pueue's `--after` is **AND-only**
15	and **success-only** — that maps cleanly to declarative DAGs and not much
16	beyond. For OR-deps, conditional branching, retry-with-backoff, or distributed
17	scheduling, escalate to a real orchestrator (see "When NOT to use").
18	
19	## When to use
20	
21	- "Run these 30 commands, max 4 at a time" → `pueue group add ml && pueue parallel 4 --group ml` then loop `submit.sh --group ml`.
22	- "Kick off a long training job and let me close my laptop" → `submit.sh -- ./train.sh` (pueue persists across reboots).
23	- "Run task B only after task A finishes successfully" → `submit.sh --after $A_ID -- ./b.sh`.
24	- "Fan out 4 trainings, then evaluate" → `submit-dag.py dag.yaml`.
25	- "Schedule this for tonight" → `submit.sh --delay 6h -- ./nightly.sh`.
26	- "Block until task 17 is done, then tell me what happened" → `wait.py --ids 17`.
27	- The user mentions pueue, pueued, the pueue CLI, or asks about a "task queue for shell jobs".
28	
29	## When NOT to use
30	
31	- **One short shell command** the user wants to run right now. Just run it. Pueue adds daemon overhead for nothing.
32	- **Cross-host *scheduling*** (jobs distributed across N machines) → Airflow / Dagster / Prefect / Slurm. Note this is not the same as driving a *single* remote daemon, which pueue does support — see `references/remote-daemon.md`.
33	- **Conditional / OR / retry-with-backoff dependencies** → real orchestrator. Pueue's `--after` is AND-only and success-only.
34	- **Typed task IO and artifact tracking** (data lineage, cached intermediate outputs) → DVC (`dvc exp run --queue`), Prefect, Airflow.
35	- **Long-running services** (web servers, daemons) → systemd, launchd, supervisord. Pueue is for finite tasks.
36	
37	## Authoritative sources
38	
39	- Repo: https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue
40	- Wiki: https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki
41	- `pueue --help`, `pueue <subcommand> --help`, `man pueue`
42	
43	## Mental model
44	
45	| Concept | What it is | How to interact |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| **Daemon** (`pueued`) | Long-running process holding queue state. Required. | `pueued -d` to start. `pueue shutdown` to stop. |
48	| **Task** | One shell command, identified by integer id. | `pueue add ...`, `pueue status`, `pueue kill`, `pueue remove`. |
49	| **Group** | Named queue with its own parallelism limit. `default` always exists. | `pueue group add <name>`, `pueue parallel N --group <name>`. |
50	| **Dependency** | Task waits for one or more parents to **succeed** before running. | `pueue add --after <id> --after <id> -- <cmd>`. AND-only, success-only. |
51	| **Status** | Tagged enum: `Queued`, `Running`, `Stashed`, `Paused`, `Locked`, `Done`. `Done` carries a `result` (`Success`, `Killed`, `DependencyFailed`, or `{"Failed": <exit_code>}`). | `pueue status --json`. |
52	
53	## Setup quickstart
54	
55	```bash
56	# 1. Verify daemon is healthy. Auto-start if missing.
57	bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/check-daemon.sh --start --json | jq
58	
59	# 2. (Optional) Create a group with 4 parallel slots.
60	pueue group add ml
61	pueue parallel 4 --group ml
62	```
63	
64	For per-OS daemon paths and launchd/systemd setup, read
65	`references/daemon-and-config.md`.
66	
67	## Always pass a label
68	
69	`pueue status` shows the **label** column before the command. In a busy
70	queue, scanning labels is the only way to tell `train.py` runs apart at a
71	glance. **Always pass `--label`** when submitting, and bias toward names
72	that distinguish *this* task from its siblings.
73	
74	Convention:
75	
76	- Shape: `<verb>-<subject>-<key>` (≤30 chars). `verb` = action,
77	  `subject` = artifact, `key` = the variable that distinguishes this run.
78	- Encode the discriminator: seed, dataset slice, model variant, date, host.
79	- Don't restate the command — `train.py --seed 1` becomes label
80	  `train-baseline-seed1`, not `python-train-py-seed-1`.
81	- For DAGs, `submit-dag.py --label-prefix <run>-` makes every task labeled
82	  `<run>-<task_name>` so `wait.py --label-prefix <run>-` selects the whole
83	  graph and `pueue clean` can be filtered later.
84	
85	| Good | Bad |
86	|---|---|
87	| `train-baseline-seed1` | `task1` (no metadata) |
88	| `eval-prod-2026q1` | `python eval.py --quarter 2026q1` (restates cmd) |
89	| `fetch-prices-AAPL` | `fetch-data` (multiple identical labels) |
90	| `nightly-featurize` (DAG) | `step-2-of-5` (rename a step → label rots) |
91	
92	## Workflow A — submit one task
93	
94	```bash
95	bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit.sh \
96	  --label train-baseline --group ml \
97	  -- python train.py --seed 1
98	# stdout: {"task_id":17,"label":"train-baseline","group":"ml","after":[],...}
99	# stderr: submitted task 17 (group=ml, label=train-baseline)
100	```
101	
102	Capture the id with `jq -r .task_id`. The script wraps `pueue add
103	--print-task-id` and falls back to a status-by-label lookup if the id parse
104	fails (defensive against future format changes).
105	
106	## Workflow B — batched runs with capped parallelism
107	
108	```bash
109	# One-time: create + size the group
110	pueue group add sweep
111	pueue parallel 4 --group sweep
112	
113	# Loop: submit 30 tasks; pueue runs at most 4 at a time
114	for SEED in $(seq 1 30); do
115	  bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit.sh \
116	    --label "sweep-$SEED" --group sweep \
117	    -- python train.py --seed "$SEED"
118	done
119	
120	# Block until all sweep-* tasks are done
121	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py \
122	  --label-prefix sweep- --group sweep
123	```
124	
125	Group parallelism is the parallelism primitive in pueue — there is no
126	per-task pool. Set it once, submit freely.
127	
128	## Workflow C — fan-out / fan-in DAG
129	
130	For multi-task pipelines with success-only dependencies, write a YAML spec
131	and submit it declaratively. **Prefer `--isolated-group`** — it creates a
132	fresh group sized to the DAG's fan-out width and leaves your other groups
133	(especially `default`) untouched:
134	
135	```bash
136	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit-dag.py \
137	  skills/local/pueue-job-queue/assets/dag.example.yaml \
138	  --label-prefix nightly- --isolated-group
139	# stderr: isolated-group: created 'dag-dcda9347' with parallel_tasks=2
140	# stdout: {"tasks":{"fetch":17,...},
141	#          "topo_order":[...],
142	#          "width_per_group":{"dag-dcda9347":2},
143	#          "isolated_group":"dag-dcda9347"}
144	```
145	
146	Each task gets the label `<--label-prefix><task_name>` so you can
147	`wait.py --label-prefix nightly-` later. After the run, clean up with
148	`pueue group remove <name>` (or run `cleanup.sh --remove-empty-groups`).
149	
150	The submitter topo-sorts, validates the graph (cycle detection, unknown
151	references, missing `cmd:`), computes the **DAG width per group** (the
152	minimum `parallel_tasks` needed for fan-out to actually run in parallel),
153	then submits in order — wiring `--after` from the in-flight name→id map.
154	**No partial submits**: validation fails loud before any `pueue add` runs.
155	
156	Three parallelism modes, in order of recommendation:
157	
158	1. **`--isolated-group [NAME]`** (recommended). Fresh group, sized to width,
159	   no side effects on other groups. NAME auto-generates from spec hash if
160	   omitted. Mutually exclusive with `--default-group`.
161	2. **`--auto-parallel`**. Mutates `pueue parallel` on the target group in
162	   place. Use this when the DAG is meant to live in a long-lived shared
163	   group (e.g. `ml`) and that group's parallelism should permanently grow.
164	3. **No flag**. Only warns (in stderr + JSON's `parallelism_warnings`).
165	   Useful in `--dry-run` planning.
166	
167	See `assets/dag.example.yaml` for a 5-task fan-out/fan-in template and
168	`references/dag-patterns.md` for more shapes.
169	
170	## Workflow D — block until tasks reach terminal state
171	
172	```bash
173	# Wait for specific ids
174	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py --ids 17,18,19 --timeout-seconds 300
175	
176	# Wait for everything in a group
177	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py --group ml
178	
179	# Wait for a label prefix (e.g. all tasks the DAG submitter created)
180	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py --label-prefix nightly-
181	```
182	
183	Output is a JSON summary on stdout:
184	
185	```json
186	{"summary": {"total": 4, "success": 3, "failed": 1, "killed": 0, "dependency_failed": 0},
187	 "tasks": [{"id": 17, "status": "Done", "result": "Success", "exit_code": 0,
188	            "label": "nightly-fetch", "group": "ml",
189	            "start": "...", "end": "..."}],
190	 "elapsed_seconds": 42.3}
191	```
192	
193	Exit codes: `0` all succeeded, `5` ≥1 task failed/killed/dependency-failed,
194	`6` timeout. The agent can branch on exit code instead of parsing JSON.
195	
196	## Workflow E — logs, retry, kill
197	
198	One-line `pueue` calls (full list in `references/cli-cheatsheet.md`):
199	
200	```bash
201	pueue log --json --full 17        # full stdout/stderr as JSON
202	pueue restart --in-place 17       # retry in-place (overwrites old log)
203	pueue kill 17 && pueue remove 17  # kill + drop from queue
204	```
205	
206	For ad-hoc filtering, prefer pueue's built-in QUERY DSL over piping
207	through `jq` — it's faster (server-side filter) and shorter:
208	
209	```bash
210	pueue status --json 'status=Failed order_by end desc first 10'
211	pueue status --json 'label %= sweep-'   # substring match
212	```
213	
214	See `references/json-schema.md` for the QUERY grammar + jq fallbacks.
215	
216	## Workflow F — periodic cleanup
217	
218	Pueue's task list grows unbounded. `pueue status --json` walks the whole
219	table, so a queue with thousands of completed tasks slows down everything
220	that touches status. Run `cleanup.sh` weekly:
221	
222	```bash
223	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/cleanup.sh \
224	  --successful-only --remove-empty-groups --logs-older-than 30
225	# stdout: {"cleaned_tasks":[...], "removed_groups":["dag-abc12345"],
226	#          "deleted_logs":[...], "kept_running":[...], ...}
227	```
228	
229	`--successful-only` keeps failures around for inspection; drop the flag
230	for a full sweep. Pair with the agent's existing weekly maintenance habit
231	(or `/schedule` an agent to run it).
232	
233	## Available scripts
234	
235	- **`scripts/check-daemon.sh`** — Single-shot daemon health + version + log-dir check, with optional auto-start. Outputs JSON to stdout.
236	  - Flags: `--start`, `--json` (default on), `--help`.
237	  - Exit: `0` healthy, `2` pueue not installed, `3` daemon unreachable, `4` client/daemon version mismatch.
238	- **`scripts/submit.sh`** — Submit ONE task, return clean JSON `{task_id, group, label, after, ...}`. Wraps `pueue add --print-task-id` with defensive id parsing. Auto-creates the group if missing.
239	  - Flags: `--label`, `--group`, `--after` (repeatable), `--immediate`, `--stashed`, `--delay`, `--priority`, `--working-dir`, `--escape`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
240	  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` pueue not installed, `3` `pueue add` failed, `4` daemon unreachable.
241	- **`scripts/wait.py`** — Block until selected tasks reach terminal status; emit a JSON summary. Selectors: `--ids`, `--label`, `--label-prefix`, `--group`. Quiet by default — emits only one initial line + state-change events on stderr; pass `--verbose` for per-tick output.
242	  - Flags: `--ids`, `--label` (repeatable), `--label-prefix`, `--group`, `--poll-seconds`, `--timeout-seconds`, `--fail-fast`, `--verbose`, `--help`.
243	  - Exit: `0` all succeeded, `1` arg error, `4` daemon unreachable, `5` ≥1 failed/killed/dependency-failed, `6` timeout.
244	- **`scripts/submit-dag.py`** — Declarative DAG submitter. Reads YAML or JSON (file path or `-` for stdin), topo-sorts, validates, submits with wired `--after`, returns `{name → id, topo_order, width_per_group, isolated_group?}`. Computes DAG fan-out width per group; with `--isolated-group [NAME]` creates a fresh dedicated group sized to the width (preferred — leaves user's other groups untouched). With `--auto-parallel` mutates target groups in place. Without either, only warns.
245	  - Flags: `--format`, `--default-group`, `--label-prefix`, `--dry-run`, `--print-graph`, `--auto-parallel`, `--isolated-group [NAME]`, `--help`.
246	  - Exit: `0` all submitted, `1` schema/cycle/unknown-ref/conflicting flags, `2` pueue not installed, `3` mid-run pueue failure (stdout still emits IDs that DID submit, for cleanup).
247	- **`scripts/cleanup.sh`** — Prune pueue task history, empty groups, and old log files. Wraps `pueue clean` + `pueue group remove` for empty non-default groups + optional log-file mtime pruning. Emits a JSON report. Run weekly to keep `pueue status --json` fast.
248	  - Flags: `--successful-only`, `--group GROUP`, `--remove-empty-groups`, `--logs-older-than N`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
249	  - Exit: `0` ok (or dry-run), `1` bad args, `2` pueue not installed, `3` daemon unreachable.
250

252	
253	- `assets/dag.example.yaml` — 5-task fan-out/fan-in (`fetch → featurize → {train_a, train_b} → evaluate`). Pass it to `submit-dag.py` with `--dry-run` first to see the topo order.
254	- `assets/pueue.yml.example` — Config snippet showing `pause_group_on_failure: true`, `default_parallel_tasks`, and a sample `groups:` block. The header comment names the platform-specific destination paths.

256	## Reference files
257	
258	- `references/cli-cheatsheet.md` — Read **when** the task needs `pueue follow`, `pueue log`, `pueue restart`, `pueue kill`, `pueue clean`, `pueue group/parallel`, `pueue pause/start`, `pueue reset`, `pueue edit`, `pueue env`, or any other un-wrapped `pueue` subcommand. Has a one-line "when to use" for each.
259	- `references/json-schema.md` — Read **when** writing custom `jq` queries against `pueue status --json` or `pueue log --json`, or when a script's JSON parsing surprises you. Documents the observed schema on pueue 4.0.2 with concrete examples for each status variant.
260	- `references/dag-patterns.md` — Read **when** the user asks for shapes beyond fan-out/fan-in (mixed sequential+parallel, diamond, etc.) or hits the AND-only / success-only limitation. Has examples and a "when to escalate to a real orchestrator" decision table.
261	- `references/daemon-and-config.md` — Read **when** setting up `pueued` for the first time, configuring per-OS paths, picking config knobs (`pause_group_on_failure`, `default_parallel_tasks`), or wiring up launchd / systemd-user.
262	- `references/remote-daemon.md` — Read **when** the daemon is on another machine: SSH unix-socket forwarding (recommended, needs no server change), direct TCP + TLS, and the working-directory trap that makes cross-platform remote *submission* impractical. Short version: `ssh host 'pueue add ...'` to submit; a forwarded client to read/control.
263	
264	## See also
265	
266	- `long-running-jobs` — pueue is one *implementation* of "let the queue own the
267	  chain" (`--after`) and "block once" (`wait.py`). That skill owns the prior
268	  question: **which** of those an agent should reach for, when a scheduled
269	  check-in is ever justified, and how to record completion durably so a run
270	  survives losing the session. Read it if you are tempted to poll
271	  `pueue status` on a timer.
272	- `slurm-hpc` — the cluster-side equivalent when jobs leave this machine.
273	
274	## Gotchas
275	
276	- **DAG fan-out is gated by `parallel_tasks` per group.** Even when two siblings both depend only on `A` and the DAG allows them to run in parallel, they will *serialize* if their group's `parallel_tasks=1`. Pueue's parallelism primitive is the group, not the dependency graph. `submit-dag.py` warns when DAG width exceeds the group's slots and suggests the exact `pueue parallel N --group G` command; pass `--auto-parallel` to apply it.
277	- **`pueue add -- bash -c 'sleep 60'` does not preserve quoting.** Pueue joins all `<COMMAND>` args and re-shells. The single-quoted `'sleep 60'` is unwrapped by *your* shell before pueue sees it, then pueue re-splits. Quote the **whole** command as one arg: `pueue add 'sleep 60'` or `submit.sh -- 'bash -c "sleep 60 && echo done"'`.
278	- **`--after` is AND-only and success-only.** Failed parent → dependent's `status.Done.result` becomes `"DependencyFailed"` and it never runs. There is no OR, no run-on-failure, no retry-on-failure. If you need that, you need a real orchestrator.
279	- **Pueue does NOT auto-create groups.** `pueue add --group new_name` exits 1 with `"Group new_name doesn't exists. Use one of these: [...]"`. `submit.sh` calls `pueue group add` first if the group is missing.
280	- **`pueue restart` (default) creates a NEW task id.** The old id stays in history with its result. To retry in-place (reusing the id, overwriting the log), pass `--in-place`. Choose deliberately — agent users often want `--in-place` for "retry this".
281	- **`pause_group_on_failure` is config-only, no CLI flag.** Set it in `pueue.yml`; reload with `pueue reset` or restart `pueued`.
282	- **Logs live in platform-specific dirs**, not your CWD. macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/pueue/logs/`. Linux: `~/.local/share/pueue/logs/`. Windows: `%APPDATA%\pueue\logs\`. `pueue log --json --full <id>` reads them for you.
283	- **`pueue wait` returns 0 even if the waited-on tasks failed.** It blocks until terminal, period. To know success/failure, query `pueue status --json` afterward (or use `wait.py`, which does this for you and returns a non-zero exit on failures).
284	- **`pueue remove` requires each id as a separate positional arg** (not a space-joined string from a subshell). Use bash arrays: `IDS=($(...)) && pueue remove "${IDS[@]}"`.
285	- **`pueue clean --successful-only` is a flag, not the default.** Plain `pueue clean` removes ALL finished tasks (including failures, which you may want to keep for debugging). Be deliberate.
286	- **`pueue add --print-task-id` writes the bare integer to stdout.** No JSON, no prose. `submit.sh` parses with a regex that tolerates future format changes; if you bypass `submit.sh`, capture with `ID=$(pueue add --print-task-id ... )` directly.
287	- **A terminal result that isn't `Success` is a failure — don't enumerate the bad ones.** `result` is a tagged enum, and `{"FailedToSpawn": "<os error>"}` is dict-shaped, not the bare string older notes implied. Matching a known-bad list let it fall through as success, so `wait.py` returned `0` for a task that never started. It now allowlists `Success` and fails closed on anything else.
288	- **Driving a remote daemon: the working directory is resolved on the CLIENT.** `pueue add` records and canonicalizes the cwd locally, so submitting to a remote daemon fails three different ways — local cwd sent (task ends `FailedToSpawn`), remote-only path rejected outright (`Failed to canonicalize given working directory path`), or a macOS symlink silently rewritten (`/tmp` → `/private/tmp`). Use `ssh host 'pueue add ...'` to submit; a forwarded client is for reading and control. See `references/remote-daemon.md`.
289
````

## 建议结论

**值得研究，先做隔离 POC；验证后收录参考流程与 gotchas，不做通用 adapter 或生产 dispatcher。**

区分三件事：**任务已结束、消息已提交、指定会话已处理消息**。前两项不能证明第三项；持久结果文件应是真相来源，唤醒只是尽力通知。

- **原 Herdr 会话续接**：使用现有 `herdr agent prompt`，不把 human toast 当作唤醒。
- **全新上下文交接**：创建明确的新 shell pane，再 `agent start`，发送预设指令和结果清单；不使用 resume/fork，保留 cwd、不抢焦点。
- **herdr-core**：仅作为独立、可选实验。上游 `b63ecbd1` 的 `hc send` 是 PTY paste + 200ms + Enter，**不是 durable inbox**；其 `HC_SESSION` / `HC_SOCKET` / `tN` 注册表不能直接映射旧 Herdr pane。

以上是已提供的本机检查与源码证据，**不是本轮端到端执行结果**。

## 实施／验证顺序

### 1. 固定小型完成契约

仅用三个输出短文本的任务 a、b、c，验证两种触发方式：

- **all-success**：d 通过 `--after` 依赖 a、b、c；任一失败，d 为 `DependencyFailed`，不会通知。
- **all-settled**：独立 waiter 使用显式任务 ID，不加 `--fail-fast`，不依赖成功边；放在独立 control group 或外部持久命令中，不能占用 worker group 的执行槽。

all-settled 不能只检查退出码：仅当退出码为 `0/5`、JSON 有效、包含全部预期 ID、且每项均为 **`state=Done`** 时生成完成结果。任务消失可能同样返回 `5` 且没有 JSON；超时 `6`、缺失或非终态必须视为未完成／观察失败。

复用已有 atomic durable marker 思路，仅记录 `run_id`、任务结果、摘要及产物路径，不塞完整日志。测试时避免自动清理或原地重试改变所观察的任务。

### 2. 分开验证两种交接

**续接原会话**

- 提交任务前记录 socket/session 上下文、pane ID、`terminal_id`、可用的 `agent_session`；发送前重新核验，绝不使用 focused pane。
- 默认仅向已核验的 idle/done 目标发送；busy 暂缓，blocked 不自动回答，目标替换／缺失则停止自动投递。
- Herdr 没有 expected-session CAS，核验与发送间仍有竞态，不能宣称严格防误投。
- 消息携带唯一 `run_id`，要求回显 ACK。`--wait` 只是生命周期观察，不是该消息的处理证明；超时／stalled 后不盲目重发，尤其不能重复非幂等任务。

**新会话**

- 先取得完整结果，再创建新 pane 和全新 agent。
- 指令与结果分区：输出明确标为**不可信数据**，不得将其中的 shell 指令、权限请求或“忽略前文”作为操作授权。
- 用 ACK 和结果摘要验证交接，不要求项目编辑或工具执行。

`codex queue --thread UUID --message TEXT [--resume]` 可作为版本限定的旁支比较，但命令成功不证明 resume 成功，必须检查警告及实际会话响应。

### 3. Core 的条件性 POC

仅在可信预构建二进制及独立配置/socket/runtime 均可隔离时执行；否则标记 **SKIP：只有源码证据**。不全局安装，不升级或重启用户 Herdr。

验证对象必须是 `hc` 自己创建的终端。明确记录：

- `hc send` 允许 working；blocked 默认拒绝，不使用 force 绕过；`--if` 仅支持 idle/working。
- 子任务自动通知覆盖 blocked/error/exit，**不覆盖普通 done turn**；不能直接当作所有 agent turn 的完成回调。
- 外部 `hc run --bg --parent <hc-address>` 建立父子关联，但不使调用者继承父终端上下文。
- 用真实响应判断交付，不能把 send 返回值当作持久投递确认。

## 最小测试矩阵

| 场景 | 应验证的结果 |
|---|---|
| a/b/c 全成功 | d 启动时间不早于所有上游结束；结果清单完整 |
| 一个失败，其他继续 | all-success 的 d 不运行；all-settled 等所有任务终态后报告失败 |
| 任务消失、超时、失败后暂停组 | 不生成“全部完成”；退出码和不完整 JSON 不被误判 |
| 目标 idle / busy / blocked | idle 可交接；busy 暂缓；blocked 不注入、不绕过 |
| 目标 replaced / missing | 核验失败停止；不改投当前焦点或其他会话 |
| 投递后断连／超时、非幂等指令 | 标记交付未知，保留结果；无 ACK 不自动重发 |
| 全新会话含恶意输出文本 | 只遵守预设任务，将输出作为数据；正确回显 run ID |

队列测试复用现有隔离 `pueue_env` 和 DAG 时间戳断言；补充 worker parallelism=1、control group 独立，以及 `pause_group_on_failure` 场景。协议异常与目标替换优先用桩测试；真实模型验证限制在 **最多 3 个简短 Codex turn**，使用专门创建的测试 pane，不给用户正在工作的会话注入测试消息。

## 收录范围与验收

1. **先记录研究**：版本／源码 commit、源码推断、实际执行证据、未验证项、隔离条件及 go/no-go。

3. **测试仅补缺口**：优先扩展现有等待／DAG 测试，不新增常驻服务、重试数据库、跨运行时身份映射或通用 adapter。

现有 `SKILL.md` 的 wait JSON 示例写成 `status`，实际输出是 `state`；若发布此流程，应顺带修正，并明确“退出码不足以证明完整收敛”。

## Bottom line

At upstream master **`b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba`**, pushed **2026-11-02**:

- **Existing-session continuation:** supported for an **hc-managed terminal**, by pasting text and submitting Enter. **Not an inbox.**
- **Fresh-session continuation:** supported through templates that launch a new process and submit role instructions plus a task. **No built-in conversation/context transfer.**
- **External pueued task:** can address an existing hc terminal explicitly, or create a child using `--parent <hc-address>`.
- **Existing Herdr 0.9.5 panes/server:** do **not** treat hc as compatible. Core has its own registry, identifiers, endpoints, and API; no legacy-pane adapter appears in its documented API or inspected implementation.

All research used read-only GitHub API requests. No checkout, file writes, upstream execution, or terminal controls.

## 1. Exact CLI surface

The generated reference is authoritative for this revision:

- [`/docs/commands.md`, lines 479–504 — run](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/docs/commands.md#L479-L504)
- [lines 518–536 — send](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/docs/commands.md#L518-L536)
- [lines 626–656 — wait](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/docs/commands.md#L626-L656)

```text
hc run [OPTIONS] [ARGV]...
  --json --name NAME --cwd CWD --on MACHINE --label K=V
  --parent PARENT --no-parent --no-notify --outlive-parent
  --rm --keep --bg --timeout SECONDS

hc send [OPTIONS] TERMINAL TEXT
  --json --force --if idle|working --wait --timeout SECONDS

hc wait [OPTIONS] [TERMINAL]
  --json --children any|all --output TEXT --timeout SECONDS
```

Each also accepts `-h`/`--help`.

Important differences from legacy Herdr:

- Timeouts are **seconds**, default configuration `wait_timeout`, otherwise **180**.
- `run` waits by default; `--bg` skips the completion wait. **Template `--bg` still waits for initial readiness/submission or its failure** before returning.
- `run --timeout` is a wait check-in, **not a command-kill deadline**.
- No public `run --env` flag: `env` is RPC-only. Likewise `caller` is not a CLI flag.
- `--keep` recovers a lost program with a **shell**, never reruns the command or resumes an agent.
- `--parent` conflicts with `--no-parent`.

Source: [`/crates/herdr-core/src/api/types.rs`, 198–280](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/api/types.rs#L198-L280), [`/crates/herdr-core/src/api/run.rs`, 30–54](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/api/run.rs#L30-L54).

## 2. `send`: PTY submission, not deferred inbox

Implementation:

1. Serialize input per terminal.
2. Wait for approximately **3 seconds without human typing**.
3. Check live status at submission time.
4. Paste, using bracketed paste if requested by the program.
5. Pause **200 ms** by default.
6. Send carriage return, or the template’s configured submit key.

Source: [`/crates/herdr-core/src/input.rs`, 111–220](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/input.rs#L111-L220).

| Target status | Normal `send` |
|---|---|
| `working` | **Allowed immediately after input gates**; does not wait for idle |
| `idle` / `done` | Allowed |
| `blocked` | Rejected; error kind `blocked`, CLI exit 9 |
| No status | Allowed; core cannot know whether a dialog is showing |
| `--if` mismatch | Nothing typed; `status_mismatch`, CLI exit 10 |

`--force` bypasses the blocked guard and **may answer an approval dialog**. It is inappropriate for an unattended completion callback.

`--if idle` is atomic but matches **exactly idle**, not `done`. There is no `--if idle-or-done` and no `--defer-until-idle`.

Tests explicitly verify paste behavior, blocked rejection, and atomic status checks: [`/crates/herdr-core/tests/m4.rs`, 76–95 and 138–154](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/tests/m4.rs#L76-L154).

### What “message” in `wait` means

When a send reaches a working terminal, core records a **sender/wakeup marker** so the recipient’s `hc wait` can return. The text has **already been typed into the terminal**; this is not a deferred message body.

Source: [`/crates/herdr-core/src/api.rs`, 444–486](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/api.rs#L444-L486), [`/crates/herdr-core/src/wait.rs`, 23–44](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/wait.rs#L23-L44).

Consequently, whether a busy agent actually queues, steers on, ignores, or mishandles this input depends on **that agent’s interactive implementation**.

## 3. Completion and status caveats

Core uses **OSC 7501 Program Status Protocol**, not brand recognition or screen scraping. Programs without it have no agent status.

Source: [`/schema/README.md`, 214–219](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/schema/README.md#L214-L219).

- A plain `wait` considers a never-reporting program working until it exits.
- `send` reports `started: true|false|null`; null means no reporting.
- `send --wait` can return `wait.reason: "not_started"` with `ended: false`. Submission may still have occurred; **do not blindly resend**.
- Sending while already working does **not** establish a uniquely identified next turn. The implementation records the current turn; completion of the already-active turn can satisfy the wait.
- `wait --output TEXT` matches output **after the wait starts**, not an existing snapshot.
- `wait --children all` means **none working**, not all successful; blocked/error children qualify as not working.

Source: [`/crates/herdr-core/src/wait.rs`, 125–187](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/wait.rs#L125-L187), [`/crates/herdr-core/src/api/waiting.rs`, 193–285](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/api/waiting.rs#L193-L285), [`/crates/herdr-core/tests/m5.rs`, 168–184](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/tests/m5.rs#L168-L184).

## 4. Built-in parent notes

These are distinct from explicit sends.

Core automatically types notes when a child:

- reports `blocked`;
- reports `error`;
- exits, **including exit 0**.

**An ordinary agent turn reaching `done` does not generate a note.** The agent is expected to report its result with `hc send`.

Parent-note delivery:

- requires a live parent that has reported OSC status;
- **defers while parent is blocked**;
- permits delivery while parent is **working**;
- eventually uses paste + Enter, not an inbox;
- suppresses news already seen by the parent or covered by its active wait;
- includes up to 20 truncated last output lines for an exited non-reporting program.

Disable with child `--no-notify`; global `notes = false` also disables automatic `<hc>` message tags.

Source: [`/crates/herdr-core/src/notes.rs`, 38–108, 165–176, 235–305](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/notes.rs#L38-L108).
Direct regressions: [`/crates/herdr-core/tests/m6.rs`, 86–160](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/tests/m6.rs#L86-L160).

A pueue task does not automatically become an hc child. Built-in notes concern **hc terminal records**, not arbitrary pueue task IDs.

## 5. Explicit targeting from external pueued

**Verified:** an external process can create a child using:

```sh
hc run --bg --json --parent "$hc_parent" command arguments
```

The external-parent test is explicit: [`/crates/herdr-core/tests/m6.rs`, 57–68](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/tests/m6.rs#L57-L68).

Requirements:

- Capture the **hc address and selected hc endpoint/session**, not legacy `$HERDR_PANE_ID`.
- Use an explicit target for `send`; there is no implicit parent-send flag.
- Children die with their parent unless `--outlive-parent` is used.
- Validate that the intended parent still hosts the intended program. Names can be reused; even a kept terminal’s stable address can later host a replacement shell.

**Subtlety:** `--parent` creates the relationship but does **not** change caller identity. Outside hc, caller is `ppid:<process-id>`. Template reply instructions/tags derive from **caller**, not explicit parent.

Thus an external fresh-launch task should explicitly say, for example, “Report the result with `hc send <captured-address> ...`”; do not assume `--parent` inserts that instruction.

Source: [`/crates/herdr-core/src/api/run.rs`, 114–145](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/api/run.rs#L114-L145), [`/crates/herdr-core/src/cli.rs`, 716–719](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/cli.rs#L716-L719), [`/crates/herdr-core/src/templates.rs`, 137–175](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/templates.rs#L137-L175).

## 6. Fresh context through templates

Template support is sufficient for a **fresh follow-up agent**:

```sh
hc run --bg --json --cwd "$repo" --no-parent followup "$completion_task"
```

Or add an explicit parent relationship instead of `--no-parent`.

Templates define `command`, opening instructions, and optional `ready`, `submit`, `stop`, `paste_gap_ms`. Core starts the command and submits **body + blank line + task**.

- It does not copy an existing conversation.
- Fresh versus resumed agent context depends on the template’s agent command/options.
- Default readiness requires OSC status within approximately **30 seconds**.
- Without readiness, the program remains live but `first_message.sent` is false.
- `ready: quiet` opts into output-settled readiness; **it neither proves readiness nor supplies agent status**.

Source: [`/docs/templates.md`, 37–85](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/docs/templates.md#L37-L85), [`/crates/herdr-core/tests/m7.rs`, 119–158](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/tests/m7.rs#L119-L158).

## 7. Isolation and legacy compatibility

Core isolation controls:

| Control | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `HC_SESSION` | Separate daemon/terminal state; default `default` |
| `XDG_STATE_HOME` | State home |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | Config/templates home |
| `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` | Unix socket directory base |
| `HC_SOCKET` | Explicit client socket; overrides config `socket` |

Sessions **share config/templates** unless config home is isolated. Changing only `HC_SOCKET` does **not** change state directory.

Managed children receive `HC_TERMINAL_ID` and `HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET`; the latter prevents caller identity leaking into another selected core.

Source: [`/docs/security.md`, 33–45, 59–81](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/docs/security.md#L33-L81), [`/crates/herdr-core/src/paths.rs`, 17–48](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/paths.rs#L17-L48), [`/crates/herdr-core/src/client.rs`, 250–255](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/client.rs#L250-L255).

Given the coordinator’s local finding—Herdr **0.9.5/protocol 22**, `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, no installed hc—the safe conclusion is **separate hc-managed terminals required**:

- hc IDs are `t1`, `t1b`, etc.; lookup is against core’s own registry.
- Core uses `terminal.*` JSON-RPC, protocol generation 1.
- No pane/workspace import or legacy control adapter is exposed.
- Existing Herdr can potentially serve as the **outer terminal viewer** for `hc attach`; that does not make an existing agent hc-managed.

Evidence: [`/crates/herdr-core/src/terminals.rs`, 161–199, 310–321](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/crates/herdr-core/src/terminals.rs#L161-L199), [`/schema/README.md`, 12–42](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/b63ecbd1e6b6a7d63fb7bcf40f268930417723ba/schema/README.md#L12-L42).

## Minimal isolated proof-of-concept plan

For later approval/execution, not performed here:

1. Use a separately obtained hc binary, **unique `HC_SESSION` and scratch XDG homes/socket**, never the existing Herdr endpoint. Even `hc ls` can autostart a daemon.
2. Start a synthetic OSC-reporting parent in that isolated core.
3. From an external process with no inherited hc caller identity, verify explicit `--parent` linkage and an ordinary child’s exit note.
4. Verify three delivery cases: working parent accepts typed input; blocked parent rejects direct send; automatic child note waits until unblock.
5. Launch one fresh template with an explicit completion task and check `.address` and `.first_message.sent`/`.started`.
6. Only then connect a single disposable pueue completion callback to the captured isolated endpoint/address.

This proves transport, parent linkage, and fresh launch independently. Real-agent OSC integration and busy-input behavior remain separate acceptance criteria.

# Pueue → Herdr／Herdr Core：完成通知與 agent 續跑研究

## Context

使用者希望 a/b/c jobs 結束後，由 d 喚回原 agent 繼續工作，或帶著預設 prompt 與結果啟動乾淨的新 conversation；尤其適用於沒有 harness-native 喚醒機制的環境。這次先做可重現的小型實驗，再評估收錄到 `pueue-job-queue`，不直接建造完整 agent 編排框架。

**目前只有唯讀研究，尚未跑 jobs、傳送 prompts、安裝 Core 或修改 skill。**

## 初步研究結論

**建議採用「Pueue 管 jobs + 持久結果檔 + 可選續跑入口」；目前的 Herdr pane 用 Herdr，Core 另作獨立實驗。**

| 問題 | 已確認的行為與影響 |
|---|---|
| d after a/b/c | `--after` 是 all-success；任一上游失敗，d 變成 `DependencyFailed`，通知程式不會執行。 |
| 不論成功失敗都回報 | 複用 `wait.py --ids ...`，不加 `--fail-fast`；獨立 control group 等待，不占 worker group 的 slot。 |
| 回到原 Herdr agent | `herdr agent prompt` 可提交下一輪輸入；`notification show` 只是給人的 toast，不能代替 agent prompt。 |
| 乾淨的新 context | 新 pane + 正常啟動新 agent，再傳入 handoff prompt；不用 resume/fork。新 conversation 仍會載入一般 system/project instructions。 |
| 新 Core | `hc send` 是 PTY paste + Enter，不是 durable inbox；Core 使用 OSC 7501 狀態，不辨識 agent 品牌或畫面。 |
| Core 是否能直接控制現在的 pane | 未找到舊 Herdr pane registry 的 bridge；Core 有自己的 `HC_SESSION`／`HC_SOCKET`／terminal IDs，不能直接互換。 |
| Core parent/child 通知 | 自動 notes 涵蓋 blocked/error/exit，不是每個 done turn；外部 worker 可透過 `hc run --parent <hc-address>` 明確建立關係，但不因此繼承 parent caller context。 |
| 不經 Herdr 的對照 | 本機 Codex 已有 `queue --thread ... --message ... [--resume]`。它不等於 Monitor；queue 成功也不保證 resume 成功。列為版本限定的替代入口，不擴充本次範圍。 |

版本證據：本機 Herdr client/server **0.9.5 / protocol 22**、Pueue **4.0.2**、Codex **0.166.0**；`HERDR_ENV=1`，`hc` 不在 PATH。Core 原始碼研究以 **b63ecbd1** 為基準，實測時記錄完整 commit／binary version。

## 執行計畫

### 1. 保存研究與建立隔離實驗

- 依專案流程追蹤評估／實作，使用 td 記錄測試與 handoff；評估對應 Discussion，確定收錄的修改對應 Issue/worktree。不 commit、push 或 merge。
- 新增 `backlog/pueue-herdr-continuation.md`，記錄版本、來源、指令、證據、限制與採納判斷；區分 **runtime-verified / source-verified / skipped**。
- 複用 `tests/conftest.py:59-151` 的 `pueue_env`：獨立 `PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH`、socket、state、teardown。不觸碰使用者真實 queue 或 daemon callback。
- Herdr 僅建立專用、`--no-focus` 的 sibling 測試 pane，保留 cwd，不向目前這段對話或其他現有 agent 發送測試訊息。關閉時只清理自己建立的資源。
- Core 使用官方可核驗、固定版本的暫存 prebuilt binary，不跑全域 installer；獨立下載目錄、script 目錄與 runtime/config/socket。若完整隔離或來源驗證不可行，跳過 Core runtime 測試，不升級／重啟現有 Herdr。

### 2. 驗證 a/b/c → 完成結果

使用只輸出短文字／寫暫存 artifact 的三個 jobs：

1. **all-success**：d 使用真正 `--after`；以時間戳證明 d 不早於所有上游結束。
2. **all-settled**：獨立 control group 的 d 不帶 success dependency；用 `wait.py` 等明確 IDs，確認一個 job 失敗時仍等較慢的其他 jobs 結束，再產生回報。
3. **負面情境**：失敗後 pause、有限 timeout、task 被移除、worker group parallelism=1。不自動 resume 使用者 queue，也不把不完整觀察說成全部完成。

**完成契約：** 不能只看 `wait.py` exit 0/5；exit 5 也可能是 task vanished。驗證 stdout JSON、完整預期 ID 集合、每個 `state == "Done"` 後，才原子寫入 `result.json`。timeout／missing 分別記為 incomplete／observation failure。

結果檔保留 `run_id`、task IDs、job outcomes、短摘要與 artifact paths；另存 delivery outcome。先持久化，再發通知，不能讓發送失敗遺失 job 結果。避免把完整環境變數或未篩選的大量 logs 塞入 prompt。

### 3. 驗證兩種續跑

**A. 原 Herdr conversation**

- 排程時固定 socket/session routing、pane ID、`terminal_id`、可取得的 `agent_session`、cwd 與 run ID；發送前重查，不依赖當下 focused pane。
- 僅對身份吻合的 idle/done agent 自動發送。working 暫緩，blocked/unknown、目標消失或替換則保留待處理結果，不注入按鍵、不繞過 approval。
- 使用 `agent prompt`，要求回覆唯一 `ACK:<run_id>` 與合成結果摘要，藉實際輸出確認新 turn，而非僅靠 command exit 或 `--wait`。
- Herdr prompt API 沒有 expected-session compare-and-send；身份預查仍有競態，不能宣稱嚴格防誤投／exactly-once。發送後 timeout/stall 記為 delivery unknown，不盲目重送。

**B. 全新 conversation**

- jobs 結束、結果檔穩定後才建立新 shell pane；解析建立回應的 ID，`agent start` 後傳 handoff。
- handoff 分成「預先授權的下一步」與「不可信 job 結果」；提供簡短摘要／檔案路徑，不把輸出中的指令當作新授權。
- 用新 session identity、非 resume/fork 的啟動參數與結果 ACK 驗證乾淨交接。這個模式不需要保留原 agent history，也不必保持原 pane 活著。

**模型成本界線：** 先以本地 receiver／stub 驗證大部分控制流程；Herdr 最多 3 個極短 Codex turns（初始、續跑、新 session），Core 通過隔離檢查後最多再 2 個。只處理合成資料、不要求改專案或執行工具；不加 permission-bypass，不自動接受 trust/approval。

### 4. Core 的對照測試

- 只操作本次 `hc` 建立並回傳的 terminal addresses；不將既有 `HERDR_PANE_ID` 當 hc target。
- 分別觀察 PTY 收到文字與真實 agent 是否開始處理；沒有 OSC status 不得推斷為 idle/done。
- 確認 `hc send` 的 working/blocked 行為；不使用 force。驗證外部 pueue worker 能明確指定 parent/target，而不是依賴 worker 恰好繼承正確環境。

- 評估重點是 Core 是否適合作為新、headless 流程的入口；不做 Herdr→Core 遷移或跨 registry adapter。

### 5. 僅收錄通過實驗的最小 recipe

推薦收錄 **reference + 少量 gotchas**，不要先新增通用 dispatcher。

- `skills/local/pueue-job-queue/references/agent-continuation.md`：新增兩種完成條件、兩種交接流程、Herdr/Core 選擇規則、實測版本与復原方式。Core 未通過 runtime 驗證時，只記研究限制，不宣稱正式支援。

# Pueue → Herdr／Herdr Core：完成通知與 agent 續跑研究

## Context

使用者希望 a/b/c jobs 結束後，由 d 喚回原 agent 繼續工作，或帶著預設 prompt 與結果啟動乾淨的新 conversation；尤其適用於沒有 harness-native 喚醒機制的環境。這次先做可重現的小型實驗，再評估收錄到 `pueue-job-queue`，不直接建造完整 agent 編排框架。

## 初步研究結論

**建議採用「Pueue 管 jobs + 持久結果檔 + 可選續跑入口」；目前的 Herdr pane 用 Herdr，Core 另作獨立實驗。**

| 問題 | 已確認的行為與影響 |
|---|---|
| d after a/b/c | `--after` 是 all-success；任一上游失敗，d 變成 `DependencyFailed`，通知程式不會執行。 |
| 不論成功失敗都回報 | 複用 `wait.py --ids ...`，不加 `--fail-fast`；獨立 control group 等待，不占 worker group 的 slot。 |
| 回到原 Herdr agent | `herdr agent prompt` 可提交下一輪輸入；`notification show` 只是給人的 toast，不能代替 agent prompt。 |
| 乾淨的新 context | 新 pane + 正常啟動新 agent，再傳入 handoff prompt；不用 resume/fork。新 conversation 仍會載入一般 system/project instructions。 |
| 新 Core | `hc send` 是 PTY paste + Enter，不是 durable inbox；Core 使用 OSC 7501 狀態，不辨識 agent 品牌或畫面。 |
| Core 是否能直接控制現在的 pane | 未找到舊 Herdr pane registry 的 bridge；Core 有自己的 `HC_SESSION`／`HC_SOCKET`／terminal IDs，不能直接互換。 |
| Core parent/child 通知 | 自動 notes 涵蓋 blocked/error/exit，不是每個 done turn；外部 worker 可透過 `hc run --parent <hc-address>` 明確建立關係，但不因此繼承 parent caller context。 |
| 不經 Herdr 的對照 | 本機 Codex 已有 `queue --thread ... --message ... [--resume]`。它不等於 Monitor；queue 成功也不保證 resume 成功。列為版本限定的替代入口，不擴充本次範圍。 |

版本證據：本機 Herdr client/server **0.9.5 / protocol 22**、Pueue **4.0.2**、Codex **0.166.0**；`HERDR_ENV=1`，`hc` 不在 PATH。Core 原始碼研究以 **b63ecbd1** 為基準，實測時記錄完整 commit／binary version。

## 執行計畫

### 1. 保存研究與建立隔離實驗

- 依專案流程追蹤評估／實作，使用 td 記錄測試與 handoff；評估對應 Discussion，確定收錄的修改對應 Issue/worktree。不 commit、push 或 merge。
- 新增 `backlog/pueue-herdr-continuation.md`，記錄版本、來源、指令、證據、限制與採納判斷；區分 **runtime-verified / source-verified / skipped**。
- 複用 `tests/conftest.py:59-151` 的 `pueue_env`：獨立 `PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH`、socket、state、teardown。不觸碰使用者真實 queue 或 daemon callback。
- Herdr 僅建立專用、`--no-focus` 的 sibling 測試 pane，保留 cwd，不向目前這段對話或其他現有 agent 發送測試訊息。關閉時只清理自己建立的資源。
- Core 使用官方可核驗、固定版本的暫存 prebuilt binary，不跑全域 installer；獨立下載目錄與 script 目錄，設定唯一 `HC_SESSION` 及獨立 `XDG_STATE_HOME`／`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`／`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`／`HC_SOCKET`。只改 socket 不會隔離 state，只改 session 不會隔離 templates。清除繼承的 hc caller identity，且任何可能自動啟 daemon 的 hc 指令都先套用隔離設定。若完整隔離或來源驗證不可行，跳過 Core runtime 測試，不升級／重啟現有 Herdr。

### 2. 驗證 a/b/c → 完成結果

使用只輸出短文字／寫暫存 artifact 的三個 jobs：

1. **all-success**：d 使用真正 `--after`；以時間戳證明 d 不早於所有上游結束。
2. **all-settled**：獨立 control group 的 d 不帶 success dependency；用 `wait.py` 等明確 IDs，確認一個 job 失敗時仍等較慢的其他 jobs 結束，再產生回報。
3. **負面情境**：失敗後 pause、有限 timeout、task 被移除、worker group parallelism=1。不自動 resume 使用者 queue，也不把不完整觀察說成全部完成。

**完成契約：** 不能只看 `wait.py` exit 0/5；exit 5 也可能是 task vanished。驗證 stdout JSON、完整預期 ID 集合、每個 `state == "Done"` 後，才原子寫入 `result.json`。timeout／missing 分別記為 incomplete／observation failure。

結果檔保留 `run_id`、task IDs、job outcomes、短摘要與 artifact paths；另存 delivery outcome。先持久化，再發通知，不能讓發送失敗遺失 job 結果。避免把完整環境變數或未篩選的大量 logs 塞入 prompt。

### 3. 驗證兩種續跑

**A. 原 Herdr conversation**

- 排程時固定 socket/session routing、pane ID、`terminal_id`、可取得的 `agent_session`、cwd 與 run ID；發送前重查，不依赖當下 focused pane。
- 僅對身份吻合的 idle/done agent 自動發送。working 暫緩，blocked/unknown、目標消失或替換則保留待處理結果，不注入按鍵、不繞過 approval。
- 使用 `agent prompt`，要求回覆唯一 `ACK:<run_id>` 與合成結果摘要，藉實際輸出確認新 turn，而非僅靠 command exit 或 `--wait`。
- Herdr prompt API 沒有 expected-session compare-and-send；身份預查仍有競態，不能宣稱嚴格防誤投／exactly-once。發送後 timeout/stall 記為 delivery unknown，不盲目重送。

**B. 全新 conversation**

- jobs 結束、結果檔穩定後才建立新 shell pane；解析建立回應的 ID，`agent start` 後傳 handoff。
- handoff 分成「預先授權的下一步」與「不可信 job 結果」；提供簡短摘要／檔案路徑，不把輸出中的指令當作新授權。
- 用新 session identity、非 resume/fork 的啟動參數與結果 ACK 驗證乾淨交接。這個模式不需要保留原 agent history，也不必保持原 pane 活著。

**模型成本界線：** 先以本地 receiver／stub 驗證大部分控制流程；Herdr 最多 3 個極短 Codex turns（初始、續跑、新 session），Core 通過隔離檢查後最多再 2 個。只處理合成資料、不要求改專案或執行工具；不加 permission-bypass，不自動接受 trust/approval。

### 4. Core 的對照測試

- 只操作本次 `hc` 建立並回傳的 terminal addresses；不將既有 `HERDR_PANE_ID` 當 hc target。
- 分別觀察 PTY 收到文字與真實 agent 是否開始處理；沒有 OSC status 不得推斷為 idle/done。模板預設等待 OSC readiness；檢查 `first_message.sent`／`started`，不能把 `--bg` 返回當成首訊息成功。`ready: quiet` 只表示輸出穩定，不作安全 readiness 的替代證據。
- 確認 `hc send` 的 working/blocked 行為；不使用 force。`--if idle` 有原子 status guard，但只匹配 idle、不含 done，也不是身份 guard。驗證外部 pueue worker 能明確指定 parent/target，而不是依賴 worker 恰好繼承正確環境。
- fresh follow-up 若要獨立於原 agent 存活，使用 `--no-parent`；若保留親子關係，明確評估 `--outlive-parent`，因為預設 child 會隨 parent 結束。`--parent` 不會自動注入正確的回覆地址，需要明寫 handoff instructions。
- 用小型 OSC-reporting receiver 測 parent 的 blocked/error/exit notes；分清「process exit」與「仍存活 agent 的 turn done」。不要把自動 notes 當成可靠 completion hook。
- 評估重點是 Core 是否適合作為新、headless 流程的入口；不做 Herdr→Core 遷移或跨 registry adapter。
